info.title: WinkPG API
info.description:
The **WinkPG API** is the programmatic interface to the WinkPG payment gateway, a multi-tenant, multi-merchant platform for processing payments, managing merchants, and driving the transaction lifecycle.

It follows REST conventions: resource-oriented endpoints, JSON request and response bodies, and standard HTTP status codes and verbs. All endpoints require authentication; use **Authorize** to supply your credentials before calling them.

<!-- winkpg:error-code-appendix -->

## Error codes

Every failed request returns the error envelope described by the `default` response on each operation. `error.code` carries one of the values below, so a caller can branch on the cause without parsing message text. The status column is the HTTP status the response carries when that code is raised. Codes are grouped by the module that declares them.

Framework codes that arrive with a vendored module are not listed here. The complete set, those included, is published on this document's machine-readable `x-error-codes` extension.

### Api Key Authorization

| Code | Message | HTTP status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH` | The key is in service but belongs to the other environment: a sk_test_ key against a merchant that is now trading live, or a sk_live_ key against one that is not. | 401 |
| `KEY_EXPIRED` | The key was in service but has passed its expiry. Renew it. | 401 |
| `KEY_INVALID` | The presented value did not match any key. A malformed value is answered the same way. | 401 |
| `KEY_REVOKED` | The key has been revoked (or otherwise taken out of service) and will never be accepted again. Mint a new key; the value will not start working again. | 401 |
| `KEY_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` | The key authenticated but is scoped, and none of the scopes it holds covers the operation it addressed. Nothing is wrong with the credential itself: grant the key the scope the operation needs, or call it with one that already holds it. | 403 |
| `TRIAL_EXPIRED` | The key is in service and stamped for the right environment, but the merchant it belongs to is on a time-limited plan whose deadline has passed. | 401 |

post.summary: Rotate an API key
post.description:
Mints a replacement owned by the same user and merchant, with the same access, and returns
it with its value revealed. This is the only time that value is shown.
            
The key being rotated keeps authenticating for an overlap window (24 hours by default,
seven days at most) so the integration can deploy the replacement without an outage, and
is then refused with KEY_REVOKED. To end the overlap sooner, revoke the rotated key: that
takes effect on the very next request.
            
Gated on the same permission as revoke, because it is the same decision about the same
credential. Refused for a key that has already been revoked or already been rotated.

---

get.description:
The boxes are counted concurrently. Serially they were the slowest part of a first page
                load, because every box that misses the short-lived cache costs its own cross-partition
                aggregate and they were paid one after another.
                


                Each concurrent count runs in its own unit of work, and that is load-bearing rather than
                tidiness. The repository resolves its DbContext from the ambient unit of work, so boxes
                sharing one would put two queries on one context and EF Core would throw "a second
                operation was started on this context" -- precisely in the two-or-more-cache-misses case
                the concurrency exists to speed up. A fresh unit of work resolves from a fresh service
                scope, so each box gets its own context.
                


                A box that fails is dropped from the result rather than failing the call. The caller
                renders a box with no entry as its placeholder, so one unlucky count costs its own box
                and no other.
                

---

**Scope**: merchant

If the matched SPM record carries a `PaymentTokenId`, the bound payment token is revoked server-side AFTER the SPM delete has been persisted.

The two effects are ordered: the stored payment method is persisted as deleted first, and
the bound payment token is revoked only after that succeeds. A list of the customer's
payment methods taken immediately afterwards therefore never shows the deleted one, whether
or not the revocation has finished.

**Scope**: merchant

from the matched stored payment method itself, which is the authoritative binding between
the customer, the merchant, the payment method and the token.

parameters.name: PagePurpose
parameters.description:
Optional server-side filter on the page's effective Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose. When set,
only pages whose resolved purpose (null resolves to Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.Payment)
equals this value are returned. Used by purpose-scoped candidate lookups (e.g. the reseller
billing-preferences card-capture HPP picker, which must only ever surface
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.SaveCard pages) so a caller cannot retrieve a non-matching page
through that path. `null` leaves the result unfiltered by purpose.

parameters.name: MerchantId
parameters.description:
Optional server-side filter on the owning merchant. When set, only pages whose
`MerchantId` equals this value are returned, and the total count reflects that same
filtered set. `MerchantId` is the Cosmos partition key for hosted payment pages, so a
merchant-scoped request is a single-partition query rather than a cross-partition scan. This
narrows within the caller's existing access scope and never widens it: a merchant the caller
cannot see yields an empty result rather than a leak. `null` leaves the result
unfiltered by merchant. Mirrors `GetHostedPaymentPageContinuationInput.MerchantId` on
the continuation list path.

post.summary: Creates a new HPP session with pre-populated field data.
post.description:
Send an `idempotencyKey` to make the call safe to retry: the same key with the same request
body returns the session already opened rather than opening a second one, and the response's
`idempotencyStatus` says which happened. Reusing a key with a different body is refused.
The key is a request-body field; no `Idempotency-Key` header is read.

---
**Required permissions**: `HostedPaymentPage.HppSessions`, `HostedPaymentPage.HppSessions.Create`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

requestBody.description: The session creation parameters.

Basic checkout session.description: The simplest session: a single-use pay link for the targeted hosted page. The page's own configuration decides everything else (amount fields, capture mode, card storage). The label and correlation id are optional merchant-side references for tracing.

Prefilled checkout session.description: Pre-fills form fields so the customer only enters card details. Use the well-known field keys (base_amount, invoice_number, customer_email, billing/shipping address fields) or an enabled merchant custom field name. A well-known key is rejected when its field is hidden on the targeted page's configuration (base_amount is always accepted); unrecognized keys are ignored when the form renders.

Retry-safe session for an order.description: Adds an idempotencyKey so the call is safe to resend. The same key with the same body returns the session already opened, with the same session id, link and expiry, instead of opening a second one; the response's idempotencyStatus reports Replayed when that happens, and KeyIgnored when create idempotency is not yet enabled for the merchant. Reusing the key for a different body is refused, so derive it from the thing you are collecting payment for. Up to 128 characters of letters, digits and '.', '_', ':' or '-'. It is a body field: no Idempotency-Key header is read.

Embedded iframe checkout.description: A session embedded in an iframe on the merchant's site. parentOrigin must be a strict HTTPS origin (scheme + host, no path) whose host matches the page's allowed embedding domains; it enables postMessage lifecycle events (ready, payment_succeeded, etc.). enableFieldEvents opts into per-field focus/blur events (field identifiers only, never values). presentationMode=Embedded drops the standalone page chrome (surface, full-viewport height, page gutters) so the form sits flush inside the frame and stays readable down to 320 px; it is chrome only, so the flow, the collected fields and every compliance disclosure are unchanged, and it is independent of parentOrigin (an iframe that wants no postMessage events may set it alone). expirySeconds must stay within the purpose's TTL bounds (60 to 900 seconds for the default CheckoutLink purpose).

Charge and store the card (card on file).summary: Charge and store the card (card on file)
Charge and store the card (card on file).description: Charges the customer and vaults the card as a reusable payment token when the payment succeeds. requestedCredentialStorage renders the consent prompt on the checkout page and records the consented usage scopes; UnscheduledCOF permits later merchant-initiated charges for pre-agreed events (top-ups, no-show fees, delayed charges). If tokenizeOnPayment is true with no declared scope, the scope defaults to UnscheduledCOF server-side.

value.label: Account top-up with card on file

Charge and store for recurring billing (.summary: Charge and store for recurring billing (bound customer)
Charge and store for recurring billing (.description: Vaults the card with consent scoped to both scheduled recurring charges and unscheduled card-on-file charges. The flags combine, so declare every scope the stored credential will be used under: a later merchant-initiated charge is rejected unless its reason maps to a consented scope. customerId binds the session to a known customer so the stored credential and consent land on exactly that record instead of an email-based find-or-create; the id must be an active customer under the page's merchant. requireConsent true forces the consent box to be mandatory: submit is blocked until the cardholder ticks it, regardless of the tenant StoredCredentialConsents.RequireConsent default.

Offer optional card saving.description: Shows the save-card box but leaves it optional: requireConsent false renders the prompt yet lets the cardholder decline. Declining completes a normal sale with no token vaulted and no consent record written; ticking it vaults the card for later unscheduled card-on-file charges. Omitting requireConsent instead inherits the tenant StoredCredentialConsents.RequireConsent setting.

Never store the card.description: Forces tokenization off for this session regardless of the merchant's tokenize-on-payment default. Use for one-off payments where a stored credential is not wanted. Leaving tokenizeOnPayment null instead defers to the merchant default.

Save a card without charging (save card.summary: Save a card without charging (save card only)
Save a card without charging (save card.description: Stores the card with no charge: the gateway runs a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 with AVS/CVV, immediate void), vaults the card, and captures consent. Requires the merchant's processor to support zero-dollar verification; the request is rejected at creation otherwise. Must not be combined with a non-zero base_amount prefill. The consent scope defaults to UnscheduledCOF when none is declared.

Save Card purpose override on a Payment.summary: Save Card purpose override on a Payment page
Save Card purpose override on a Payment.description: Runs a save-card-only flow against a page whose own purpose is Payment, so one page can back both checkout and card-capture sessions without a second page instance. The resolved purpose drives everything downstream (zero-dollar verification, consent, tokenization), and the same fail-closed checks a dedicated Save Card page enforces are re-checked at session create.

Save card with initial charge (subscript.summary: Save card with initial charge (subscription enrollment)
Save card with initial charge (subscript.description: Charges the first payment of a recurring schedule as a real sale, vaults the card with Recurring consent, and creates a contract for the remaining payments. The recurring plan override is required for this purpose and must have complete economics: a positive recurring amount, an interval of at least 1, and at least two total payments (the initial charge plus one recurring payment). initialChargeAmount optionally overrides payment one (for example a bundled setup fee); the target page must accept card only. Recurring consent is always captured because the initial charge depends on it; a requestedCredentialStorage sent alongside is unioned in rather than replacing Recurring, so declaring UnscheduledCOF here lets the vaulted card also authorize later ad-hoc merchant-initiated charges beyond the schedule.

Authorize now, capture later.description: Overrides the capture mode for this session: the payment is authorized in full but not captured, leaving an Authorization eligible for a later capture or void through the standard transaction actions. Only valid for the chargeable Payment purpose. A null captureMode inherits the page's configured mode; send Sale explicitly to force authorize-and-capture on a page configured for delayed capture.

Fixed amount the customer cannot change.summary: Fixed amount the customer cannot change (invoice)
Fixed amount the customer cannot change.description: Locks the amount for this session: base_amount is required and renders read-only on the page, and the server verifies the submitted amount matches before creating the transaction. Use for paying an exact invoice. Amount mode is only valid on the chargeable Payment flow; it is rejected on a save-card / card-capture session.

Suggested amount the customer can change.summary: Suggested amount the customer can change (donation)
Suggested amount the customer can change.description: Pre-fills base_amount as a suggested amount but leaves it editable, so the cardholder can accept it or enter their own. Use for a suggested donation. base_amount is required for Suggested mode.

Link denominated in an explicit currency.summary: Link denominated in an explicit currency
Link denominated in an explicit currency.description: Names the currency the link is denominated in instead of leaving it implied. Only the merchant's own configured currency is accepted: a different code is rejected at create with HostedPaymentPage:HppSession:CurrencyNotSupported rather than accepted and then ignored at charge time. Omit the field and the session takes the merchant's currency anyway; either way the created session reports the currency it settled on in its effective block, so it can be read back rather than inferred.

409.description:
The idempotency key was already used for a different request
(`HostedPaymentPage:HppSession:CreateIdempotencyKeyReused`), the create it belongs to is
still running (`HostedPaymentPage:HppSession:CreateIdempotencyInProgress`), or the key can
no longer be resolved to a session and so cannot answer for it again
(`HostedPaymentPage:HppSession:CreateIdempotencySessionGone`, which calls for a new key
rather than a retry). Nothing was created in any of the three.

get.summary: Lists HPP sessions for a specific hosted payment page.
get.description:
**Required permissions**: `HostedPaymentPage.HppSessions`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: HostedPageId
parameters.description:
The HPP configuration ID to list sessions for, or `null` to list across every hosted
page in the caller's merchant scope.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: Optional status filter.

parameters.name: ExpiredOnly
parameters.description:
When `true`, returns only sessions that are still pending but whose expiry instant has
passed. Expiry is derived from the clock rather than stored as a status, so it cannot be
asked for through PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.GetHppSessionListInput.Status; this is the separate filter for it. Combined with
PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.GetHppSessionListInput.Status the two are ANDed, and any status other than pending yields no rows.

parameters.name: IncludeApproxTotalCount
parameters.description:
Set to false to skip the approximate total count query and receive a null count;
omit the value or set it to true to receive the count as before.

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

default.description: The request failed. The body carries the standard error envelope: a machine-readable `error.code`, a human-readable `error.message`, and `error.validationErrors` when the failure was a validation rejection. See the error-code reference in this document's description for the values `error.code` can take.

post.summary: Creates a ready-to-use Save Card page for storing a card on file.
post.description:
The page is created under merchantId and captures the card with a
zero-dollar verification rather than a charge, so its amount configuration is neutralized
for you. The merchant's processor must support zero-dollar verification; when it does not,
the request is refused with a validation error.

Everything else on the returned page can be changed afterwards through the ordinary update
call.

**Scope**: merchant

parameters.description: The owning merchant.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional internal name; a default unique name is generated when null.

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

post.description:

Gateway payments delegate to the payment platform, which returns the money with whichever
operation the originating transaction's settlement state permits. Manually-recorded payments
are reversed in place and require a reason.

**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

The request itself needs correcting. Callers branch on `error.code`:
`Invoicing:Refund:ManualReversalRequiresReason` (a manually recorded payment is being
reversed and no reason was supplied) or `Invoicing:Refund:AmountInvalid`.

404.description:
The invoice does not exist, or is not visible to this caller
(`Invoicing:Biller:ForeignBillerNotAllowed`).

409.description:
The invoice's current state refuses the refund. Callers branch on `error.code`:
`Invoicing:Refund:NotAllowedForStatus`, `Invoicing:Refund:NoRefundablePayments`,
`Invoicing:Refund:ExceedsAmountPaid`, `Invoicing:Refund:RequiresMerchantScope`,
`Invoicing:Refund:RejectedByGateway`, or `Invoicing:Refund:PartialFailure` (some
payments were returned before the sequence stopped; inspect the invoice before retrying).

`GET /api/merchants/{id}/processor-profiles` using `processorProfileId`. Two profiles
boarded on the same processor report identical flags: capability is a property of the
processor, not of the individual profile.

assumed, so a caller never reads support for something the processor cannot do.

get.summary: Register: resolves a register by its legacy numeric key within the caller's own merchant.
get.description:
Example: `GET /api/merchants/registers/by-legacy-number/41`.


This action throws where the interface returns null: over HTTP a null would be a 204 with an
empty body, which reads as success. 404 is the published contract for the route.


The merchant is deliberately not on this path, since the key resolves against the caller's
own merchant. The `by-legacy-number` literal keeps a bare `registers/{legacyNumber}`
from sitting beside `merchants/{id}` as a sibling-parameter disagreement, which aborts
SDK generation; it is safe in the other direction because such a literal collides only with a
sibling parameter of the same name.

get.description:
The boxes are counted concurrently. Serially they were the slowest part of a first page
                load, because every box that misses the short-lived cache costs its own cross-partition
                aggregate and they were paid one after another.
                


                Each concurrent count runs in its own unit of work, and that is load-bearing rather than
                tidiness. The repository resolves its DbContext from the ambient unit of work, so boxes
                sharing one would put two queries on one context and EF Core would throw "a second
                operation was started on this context" -- precisely in the two-or-more-cache-misses case
                the concurrency exists to speed up. A fresh unit of work resolves from a fresh service
                scope, so each box gets its own context.
                


                A box that fails is dropped from the result rather than failing the call. The caller
                renders a box with no entry as its placeholder, so one unlucky count costs its own box
                and no other.

post.summary: Counts how deliveries ended in a time window, broken down by outcome.
post.description:
This is drop accounting for an outage: how many events were still queued, how many were
            skipped without an outbound attempt because the destination was suppressed, and how many
            exhausted their retries and were dead-lettered, over the period a receiver was unreachable.
            It counts in the store and reads no delivery, so the answer costs the same whether the window
            holds ten deliveries or ten thousand.
            


            The window is bounded, and a wider one is refused rather than quietly narrowed: an answer
            silently covering a quarter of what was asked for would look exactly like a merchant who sent
            nothing for the rest of it. Count a longer period in steps.
            


            A POST because the window and its narrowing are a request body, matching the other
            continuation and summary reads in this platform. Nothing is created or changed.
            

---
**Required permissions**: `Notifications.Deliveries`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: suppressNulls
parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

requestBody.description: The window, and optionally the merchant and event type to narrow to.

200.description: The count of deliveries in each state, plus the window they cover.

400.description: The window is missing, inverted, or wider than the bound.

403.description: The caller may not read delivery history.

post.summary: Sends every replayable delivery in a time window to your endpoints again.
post.description: The bulk form of the single replay, for a receiver that was down: give it the window your receiver was unavailable for and the platform replays what did not land, one delivery at a time, on its own delivery path. The window says what to look at; it does not say how much this call will do. One call takes on at most a hundred deliveries and spends at most sixty seconds starting them, plus however long the last one it started takes to reach a verdict. Everything it selected but never reached is reported as `notAttempted` rather than dropped. Run the same request again while `reachedCap` is true or `notAttempted` is above zero, until both are clear. Running it again is safe and needs no idempotency key. A delivery that succeeded on the previous run is no longer replayable, so a repeat run only touches what is still outstanding. The same per-endpoint replay budget applies, shared with the single replay, so a run against a receiver that has only just come back cannot stampede it. Deliveries the budget refused are counted under `rateLimited` and are untouched, so a later run picks them up. --- **Required permissions**: `Notifications.Events.Replay` **Scope**: merchant

post.summary: Sends one webhook delivery to your endpoint again.
post.description: This is the other half of recovering from an outage: list what you missed, then ask for the ones that did not land to be sent again. The platform resets the delivery and attempts it on its own delivery path, so the payload, the signature and the headers are the ones your endpoint would have received. What replay can recover, and what it cannot. Only a delivery this platform raised and that ended `Failed`, `DeadLettered` or `Skipped`. An event that never became a delivery cannot be replayed, because there is nothing to send; neither can one that already succeeded. It answers with what happened, so it runs while you wait. One attempt is bounded by the platform's own attempt deadline of two minutes; in practice your endpoint's own timeout ends it far sooner. Three separate limits apply, and none of them needs an idempotency key. Your API key's request limit bounds how often you may ask. A per-endpoint replay budget bounds how much the platform will send to one address in a window, and a request over it is refused without touching the delivery. And asking twice for a delivery that has since succeeded is refused, because a delivered replay is no longer replayable. --- **Required permissions**: `Notifications.Events.Replay` **Scope**: merchant

get.description:
The boxes are counted concurrently. Serially they were the slowest part of a first page
                load, because every box that misses the short-lived cache costs its own cross-partition
                aggregate and they were paid one after another.
                


                Each concurrent count runs in its own unit of work, and that is load-bearing rather than
                tidiness. The repository resolves its DbContext from the ambient unit of work, so boxes
                sharing one would put two queries on one context and EF Core would throw "a second
                operation was started on this context" -- precisely in the two-or-more-cache-misses case
                the concurrency exists to speed up. A fresh unit of work resolves from a fresh service
                scope, so each box gets its own context.
                


                A box that fails is dropped from the result rather than failing the call. The caller
                renders a box with no entry as its placeholder, so one unlucky count costs its own box
                and no other.

transaction is read within merchantId only: one belonging to another
merchant is reported as not found. The resulting token charges like any other, so supply
its public reference as `TokenData.Token`.

No card number or full account number crosses the wire in either direction: the request
carries only identifiers, and the response carries the token handles plus masked and
last-four values. A transaction that stored no reusable payment method is refused with a
coded business error.

customerId is accepted so callers can pass the customer they intend to
            attach the token to, but it is not stored on the token itself.

parameters.name: merchantId
parameters.description: The owning merchant. Must be within the caller's scope, and the transaction must belong to it.

Merchant: list my transactions.description: Lists the caller's own transactions. When the request is authenticated with a merchant-owned API key, the results are already scoped to that merchant by the caller's context, so no MerchantId is required: send an essentially empty body (just maxResultCount) for the first page, then resend the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response to page further. MerchantId is optional here and cannot broaden visibility beyond the caller's own merchant(s); supply it only to narrow results when the key's user is linked to more than one merchant.

Reseller: list one merchant's transactio.description: Lists transactions for a single merchant that belongs to the calling reseller. A reseller-owned API key sees every merchant under that reseller by default; setting merchantId narrows the results to that one merchant. The value must be a merchant within the reseller: a merchantId outside the reseller's hierarchy simply returns no results, it never exposes another reseller's data. Omit merchantId to list across all of the reseller's merchants. Page further by resending the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response.

Fetch the next page.description: Fetches the page after a previous request. Resend the exact same filters you used on the first request (merchantId, maxResultCount, and so on), and add the continuationToken value returned in that request's response. The token is opaque: pass it back unchanged, do not parse or edit it. When a response comes back with a null continuationToken, the last page has been reached. The value shown here is illustrative; use the real token from your previous response.

get.summary: Returns one page of transactions within the caller's scope, newest first by default.
get.description:
At most MaxResultCount transactions are returned (default 10, ceiling 1000). Sorting accepts CreationTime or LastModificationTime with an optional ASC / DESC suffix; anything else falls back to newest-first. SkipCount is rejected with HTTP 400: this list is backed by a store that pages with continuation tokens, where an offset is charged for every row it steps over. To read beyond the first page, call POST /api/transactions/list/continuation and follow its NextContinuationToken, holding every other parameter constant for the whole sequence. TotalCount is an approximate count over the same filters, cached briefly, so it may lag concurrent writes. Narrow the page with MerchantId (one merchant), MerchantIds (repeat the parameter for several), Ids, and the creation / modification time bounds. Every one of those narrows within the scope the caller already has and never widens it, they combine, and TotalCount describes the same filtered set as the page. Filter and Name are rejected with HTTP 400: nothing on a transaction backs a free-text search, and a rejection is safer than the alternative of accepting the parameter and answering a narrowed request with the whole estate.

---
**Required permissions**: `Transactions.Reports`  
**Scope**: merchant

parameters.name: MerchantId
parameters.description:
Optional server-side filter on the owning merchant. When set, only transactions whose
`MerchantId` equals this value are returned, and `totalCount` reflects that same
filtered set rather than the whole estate. `MerchantId` is the Cosmos partition key for
transactions, so a merchant-scoped request is a single-partition query rather than a
cross-partition scan.


This narrows within the caller's existing access scope and never widens it: a merchant the
caller cannot see yields an empty page rather than a leak. `null` leaves the result
unfiltered by merchant. Mirrors `GetTransactionContinuationInput.MerchantId` on the
continuation list path.

parameters.name: MerchantIds
parameters.description:
Optional server-side filter restricting the result to several merchants at once. Repeat the
parameter to supply more than one value. Behaves as PhoeniXGate.Transactions.GetTransactionListInput.MerchantId does, except
that a transaction matches when its `MerchantId` equals any listed value.


Every filter on this request narrows. Supplying this alongside PhoeniXGate.Transactions.GetTransactionListInput.MerchantId
returns only the transactions that satisfy both, so a scalar value absent from this list
yields an empty page. A list holding nothing usable fails closed on an empty page too,
because a caller that asked to be narrowed must never be widened to the whole estate.
`null` or an empty list leaves the result unfiltered by merchant.

parameters.description: Gets or sets a general filter string for the result set.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Gets or sets the name filter for the result set.

parameters.name: IncludeDeleted
parameters.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to include deleted entities in the result set.

parameters.name: IncludeInactive
parameters.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to include inactive entities in the result set.

parameters.name: Ids
parameters.description: Gets or sets a list of entity IDs to filter the result set.

Visa Authorization.description: Card-not-present authorization (hold funds without capturing). Use this when you intend to capture the funds in a later step (typical for shipped goods).

MasterCard Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using a MasterCard test PAN.

Discover Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using a Discover test PAN.

Amex Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using an American Express test PAN. Amex CVV is 4 digits.

Sale (single-message Auth+Capture).description: Single-message authorize-and-capture in one round trip. The most common production transaction type for retail and e-commerce checkouts where goods/services are delivered immediately.

Sale with Tip.description: Single-message Sale carrying a tip. Total is computed by the server as Base + Tip + Tax + Shipping + Convenience.

Capture (follow-up to Authorization).description: Captures funds from a prior Authorization. Card data is inherited from the original transaction — only the OriginalTransaction.TransactionId is required. Send a partial-capture amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base when capturing less than the original auth.

Return / Refund.description: Refunds a previously settled transaction back to the cardholder. References the original transaction by id; amount may be partial or full.

Reversal (full).description: Undo a prior auth/capture. Submit TransactionType.Void; the gateway issues an online reversal (0420-equivalent message, releases the issuer hold) when the processor supports it, and falls back to an offline batch-close exclusion only when the processor declares it cannot service the online reversal. Omit InvoiceData.Amounts to undo the full authorized amount.

Reversal (partial).description: Reverses only part of a prior authorization, leaving the un-reversed remainder available for capture/settlement. Send the partial amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base. Requires a processor that advertises SupportsPartialReversal; the same TransactionType.Void shape is used as the full-amount reversal.

Force - Voice-Auth Capture.description: Voice-authorization Force: the merchant obtained a verbal approval code from the issuer over the phone and is now submitting the transaction. Supplies fresh card data, fresh InvoiceData, and the issuer-provided AuthCode. There is NO prior gateway transaction.

Force - Gateway-Capture (follow-up to Au.description: Gateway-Capture-as-Force: a follow-up to a prior gateway Authorization that maps to TransactionOperationType.Capture internally. Card data and amount are inherited from the resolved prior transaction - only OriginalTransaction.TransactionId (or MerchantTransactionId) is required.

Repeat Sale (recurring).description: Single-message authorize-and-capture for a recurring/repeating customer charge. Used by recurring-billing flows; carries an InitiationType + MITReason to mark this as a merchant-initiated transaction (MIT) for scheme compliance.

Authorization with Stored Payment Token.description: Authorization using a previously stored payment method. Send only the payment token (TokenData.Token); the server resolves the card data from the stored payment method at the customer/payment-method level, so you do not send PAN/CVV.

Authorization with Level 3 Data.description: Commercial-card authorization with Level 2 (tax) and Level 3 (line items) data. Submitting Level 3 typically qualifies the transaction for lower interchange rates on B2B card categories.

ACH / eCheck Sale.description: Single-message ACH debit (eCheck) against a US checking or savings account. Supplies CheckData rather than CardData; routing and account numbers are required.

Send a partial-capture amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base when capturing less than the original auth.

Return / Refund.description: Refunds a previously settled transaction back to the cardholder. References the original transaction by id; amount may be partial or full.

Reversal (full).description: Undo a prior auth/capture. Submit TransactionType.Void; the gateway issues an online reversal (0420-equivalent message, releases the issuer hold) when the processor supports it, and falls back to an offline batch-close exclusion only when the processor declares it cannot service the online reversal. Omit InvoiceData.Amounts to undo the full authorized amount.

Reversal (partial).description: Reverses only part of a prior authorization, leaving the un-reversed remainder available for capture/settlement. Send the partial amount via InvoiceData.Amounts.Base. Requires a processor that advertises SupportsPartialReversal; the same TransactionType.Void shape is used as the full-amount reversal.

Force - Voice-Auth Capture.description: Voice-authorization Force: the merchant obtained a verbal approval code from the issuer over the phone and is now submitting the transaction. Supplies fresh card data, fresh InvoiceData, and the issuer-provided AuthCode. There is NO prior gateway transaction.

Force - Gateway-Capture (follow-up to Au.description: Gateway-Capture-as-Force: a follow-up to a prior gateway Authorization that maps to TransactionOperationType.Capture internally. Card data and amount are inherited from the resolved prior transaction - only OriginalTransaction.TransactionId (or MerchantTransactionId) is required.

Repeat Sale (recurring).description: Single-message authorize-and-capture for a recurring/repeating customer charge. Used by recurring-billing flows; carries an InitiationType + MITReason to mark this as a merchant-initiated transaction (MIT) for scheme compliance.

Authorization with Level 3 Data.description: Commercial-card authorization with Level 2 (tax) and Level 3 (line items) data. Submitting Level 3 typically qualifies the transaction for lower interchange rates on B2B card categories.

ACH / eCheck Sale.description: Single-message ACH debit (eCheck) against a US checking or savings account. Supplies CheckData rather than CardData; routing and account numbers are required.

Visa Authorization.description: Card-not-present authorization (hold funds without capturing). Use this when you intend to capture the funds in a later step (typical for shipped goods).

Discover Authorization.description: Authorization-only request using a Discover test PAN.

post.description:
The lookup is confined to one merchant. When no transaction carries the key, the request
fails with 404 Not Found. Use it after a network failure to find out whether an earlier
submission was accepted before retrying: 404 means it was not, and a returned transaction
means it was.

Whether resending the original request would charge again depends on whether create
deduplication is enabled for the merchant. Where it is, a resend with the same key returns
the original transaction rather than charging. Where it is not, this lookup is the only
safeguard and a resend creates a second charge. When more than one transaction carries the
key, which is possible for keys sent before deduplication existed, the earliest is
returned.

post.description:
This endpoint uses continuation tokens instead of skip/take paging.

parameters.description: If true, omit properties with null values.

Merchant: list my transactions.description: Lists the caller's own transactions. When the request is authenticated with a merchant-owned API key, the results are already scoped to that merchant by the caller's context, so no MerchantId is required: send an essentially empty body (just maxResultCount) for the first page, then resend the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response to page further. MerchantId is optional here and cannot broaden visibility beyond the caller's own merchant(s); supply it only to narrow results when the key's user is linked to more than one merchant.

Reseller: list one merchant's transactio.description: Lists transactions for a single merchant that belongs to the calling reseller. A reseller-owned API key sees every merchant under that reseller by default; setting merchantId narrows the results to that one merchant. The value must be a merchant within the reseller: a merchantId outside the reseller's hierarchy simply returns no results, it never exposes another reseller's data. Omit merchantId to list across all of the reseller's merchants. Page further by resending the same body with the continuationToken from the previous response.

Fetch the next page.description: Fetches the page after a previous request. Resend the exact same filters you used on the first request (merchantId, maxResultCount, and so on), and add the continuationToken value returned in that request's response. The token is opaque: pass it back unchanged, do not parse or edit it. When a response comes back with a null continuationToken, the last page has been reached. The value shown here is illustrative; use the real token from your previous response.

post.summary: Execute a follow-up operation on an existing transaction.
post.description: The token is accepted and not passed on, on purpose. Before the interface existed this action took no token and the app service therefore ran with `CancellationToken.None`; forwarding the request-abort token instead would newly let a client disconnect cancel a money-moving operation mid-flight. The operation-idempotency machinery claims a key, dispatches to the orchestrator, then finalizes or releases, and releasing a claim whose operation was already dispatched is a duplicate-charge hazard, so a cancellation landing between the claim and the dispatch is a new way into exactly the window that contract guards. Honouring the token is a deliberate behaviour change that belongs in its own story with its own analysis of that window; this one only makes the endpoint proxy-reachable. Passing System.Threading.CancellationToken.None explicitly keeps the pre-change behaviour byte for byte.

get.summary: Lists the operating user's favorites.
get.description:
Bucketed by whether they match the current operating context.
Results are split into two buckets: `inContext` (favorites whose stored scope matches the request's
operating context) is always populated; `outOfContext` is populated only when
WinkPG.Favorites.GetUserFavoritesInput.IncludeAllContexts is `true`, otherwise it is empty.


This read also performs lazy upkeep: each favorite is re-validated against the owning entity's current
authorization and visibility, and any pin the user can no longer see (entity deleted, access revoked) is
quietly removed from their own list. Out-of-context favorites are not treated as orphans.


---
**Required permissions**: `Favorites.Manage`  
**Scope**: merchant

with favorites stored under a different operating context.

post.description:
Idempotent for a given `(operating user, entityType, entityId)`: pinning something already pinned, or
re-pinning an entity the user previously removed, returns the existing (or restored and refreshed) favorite
instead of creating a duplicate. `entityType` must be a lowercase slug and `route` must be a local
app-relative path (absolute URLs and path traversal are rejected). Each user has a maximum number of favorites;
exceeding the cap is rejected rather than silently evicting the oldest.

paymentMethodType.description:
Gets or sets the type of payment method (Card or Check).
Conditional: When IsReaderTokenBacked is true. Must equal Card.

cardData.description:
Gets or sets the card data when  is Card.
Required: When PaymentMethodType == Card.

checkData.description:
Gets or sets the check data when  is Check.
Required: When PaymentMethodType == Check.

isDefault.description: Gets or sets whether this should be the customer's default payment method.

customName.description: Gets or sets an optional user-defined display name (e.g., "Marriott Chase").

initialSchemeTransactionId.description:
Optional initial (first-in-series) network / scheme transaction id captured from the
authorization response of the cardholder-initiated transaction that stored this credential.
Populated only on the transaction-driven save-card path (the manual Customer admin add has no
authorization response); persisted onto the stored payment method so later charges can echo
it without a consent lookup. Non-sensitive card-network protocol metadata.

schemeTransactionIdBrand.description:
Optional card brand at capture time (e.g. "Visa") tagged alongside
PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.InitialSchemeTransactionId. Ignored when the initial id is absent.

schemeTransactionIdProcessor.description:
Optional originating processor ("tsys" / "fiserv") tagged alongside
PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.InitialSchemeTransactionId. Ignored when the initial id is absent.

readerToken.description:
The processor reader token to store for a PAN-less card (a decrypt-and-forward processor such
as MagTek DAF, where the gateway never sees the PAN). When set, this input mints a reader-token
stored method: the token is written encrypted onto the backing vault token's
`ProcessorTokens` and there is no card data to vault. Server-trusted only — carried on the
non-HTTP PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.IInternalCustomerStoredPaymentMethodService seam and never over the HTTP
wire (a client-supplied processor token would be a spoofing vector). Never logged.

readerTokenProcessorName.description:
The processor key ("magtekdaf") the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken belongs to, used as the
`ProcessorTokens` selection key. Required when PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken is set.
Required: When IsReaderTokenBacked is true.

readerTokenProcessorProfileId.description:
The processor profile the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken was captured under, used as the second part
of the `ProcessorTokens` selection key. Optional.

readerTokenRequestorId.description:
Optional token-requestor id captured alongside the PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.ReaderToken. Stored on the
backing token's `ProcessorTokens` entry for lineage. Non-sensitive.

isReaderTokenBacked.description:
True when this input describes a reader-token (PAN-less) stored method rather than a
PAN- or account-backed one. In that case PhoeniXGate.Customers.Customers.AddStoredPaymentMethodInput.CardData is absent by design.

AdjustmentTypes.description:
Per-processor advertised support for the two adjustment-shaped follow-up operations
against an authorized transaction. A processor may legitimately support either, both,
or neither — modeled as a [Flags] enum so capability contributors compose cleanly and
callers can ask "does this processor support `X`" with a single `HasFlag`.
x-enumDescriptions: Processor advertises no adjustment support. Both OfflineAdjustment and IncrementalAuthorization requests are rejected at the AppService boundary.

Processor accepts TransactionOperationType.OfflineAdjustment: pre-settlement edits to the stored settlement record (tip, tax, level-3, AVS) with no network call. Modeled by OfflineAdjustmentFlowRunner.

Processor accepts TransactionOperationType.IncrementalAuthorization: an online amount-bumping auth on top of the existing approved hold (Visa Estimated/Incremental, MasterCard PreAuth+Final, Discover Incremental). Modeled by IncrementalAuthorizationFlowRunner.

ApplePayCheckoutTokenInput.description:
Request body for the Apple Pay "process payment" endpoint — the storefront
posts this after the shopper authorises the payment in the Apple Pay sheet.
Shape mirrors the `ApplePayPayment.token` object the JS client delivers
to `onpaymentauthorized`: only the `token` envelope is carried at
the top level because the rest of the JS event (billing/shipping contacts)
isn't part of this stub flow.
            


This endpoint is the production analog of the POC `ApplePayTestController.ProcessPayment`.
It accepts the encrypted Apple Pay token, logs sanitized metadata (network /
type / transaction identifier), and returns success. It does NOT decrypt the
token here — encrypted-token decryption is performed inside the regular HPP /
transaction-submit pipeline.

ApplePayPaymentDataDto.description:
The encrypted payment payload. WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentDataDto.Data is the base64-encoded
AES-GCM ciphertext that decrypts to the card credentials; WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentDataDto.Signature
is the CMS signature that proves the payload came from Apple. Both are sensitive
and MUST NOT be logged.

ApplePayPaymentHeaderDto.description:
Header carried alongside the encrypted payload. WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.ApplePayPaymentHeaderDto.EphemeralPublicKey
is the ECDH ephemeral key used during decryption and must not be logged.

ApplePayPaymentMethodDto.description:
Wallet-side display metadata for the chosen card on the Apple Pay sheet. None
of these fields carry PAN/CVV — they are safe-to-log presentation values.

ApplePayProcessPaymentOutput.description:
Response shape for the stub process-payment endpoint. Mirrors the POC return
value (`{ success: true }`). Carries no decrypted card data.

successful rotation under the new code populates Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.Autosettle.AutosettlementSettings.CurrentBatchIds for that
processor and clears this scalar. New writes never set this field.

The merchant's billing assignment has no price plan (PricePlanId is null/empty), so there is nothing to rate against.

The billing assignment's effective window (EffectiveFrom/EffectiveTo) does not overlap the billed period — e.g. a plan whose effective date is after the billed month. This is the exact confusion behind the effective-date billing investigation: a merchant is assigned to a plan but skipped because the assignment is not effective for the period.

the interactive single-reseller run inserted its Running lock row and enqueued BillingRunWorkflow on the background-job framework. Per-merchant execution proceeds asynchronously in the Functions host; the terminal status (Completed / PartiallyCompleted / Failed) is written by the workflow and surfaces in the grid + run-detail page over time. ClientIpGeoSnapshot.description: Point-in-time snapshot of geolocation and ISP/ASN data resolved from the transaction's Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.ClientIpAddress at the enrichment stage of the orchestration pipeline. This snapshot is immutable after creation. Subsequent updates to the transaction (capture, refund, reversal, repeat, recurring-billing materializations) MUST NOT overwrite it — the snapshot captures the geo intelligence as it was at the moment the original transaction ran. If the underlying IP intelligence database changes (DB-IP MMDB upgrade, ASN reassignment, ISP rebrand, etc.) the persisted snapshot is preserved so historical transactions remain auditable against the data the system saw at runtime. All fields are nullable because not every IP record carries every column — fine-grained fields like Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.ClientIpGeoSnapshot.City are sparse for IP ranges that DB-IP can only localize to a country or region.

legacyNumber.description:
The contract's legacy numeric key, as used by the v1 API where contracts are identified by an
integer rather than a Guid. Server-owned: stamped once at create from a tenant-scoped counter
and never settable from an inbound payload.

planId.description:
The reusable plan this contract subscribes to for its price, or null when
the contract carries its own inline amount.

deactivationReason.description:
Describes why this contract was deactivated. Null when the contract is active
            or was never deactivated by the billing engine. Set automatically by the
            recurring billing manager and cleared when the contract is reactivated.

creationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was created.

creatorId.description: The ID of the user who created this entity.

lastModificationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was last modified.

lastModifierId.description: The ID of the user who last modified this entity.

isDeleted.description: Indicates whether this entity has been deleted.

deleterId.description: The ID of the user who deleted this entity, if it is deleted.

deletionTime.description: The date and time when this entity was deleted, if it is deleted.

concurrencyStamp.description:
Optimistic-concurrency stamp for the embedded contract. Contracts live inside
the Customer aggregate document, so they carry no per-contract Cosmos ETag; this stamp lets
the Contract API enforce per-contract optimistic concurrency independently of the parent
document. Nullable because documents created before this field carry no stamp: a null stamp
means "no concurrency check" until the contract is next updated, which stamps it going forward.

consecutiveFailures.description:
Consecutive failed billing attempts without an intervening success. Reset to 0 on success.
Used with Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount to determine suspension.

lastSuccessfulExecution.description: Timestamp of the last successful billing execution.

lastExecution.description: Timestamp of the last billing execution (success or failure).

executionHistory.description:
The most recent execution records for this contract (capped at 10, newest first).
Default-initialized to an empty list so new contract documents persist an empty
`"ExecutionHistory": []` in Cosmos — EF Core Cosmos cannot reliably add
detached owned-collection items to a property whose loaded JObject path does
not contain the key (throws System.NullReferenceException in
`DocumentSource.GetCurrentDocument` during `SaveChangesAsync`).


Remains nullable because Newtonsoft deserialization overrides the C# initializer
when the persisted document has an explicit `"ExecutionHistory": null`
(legacy contracts predating this default-initialization fix). Callers must
normalize to an empty list before mutating (`ExecutionHistory ??= []`)
until those docs are backfilled.

ContractAggregates.description: Cumulative execution statistics and recent history for a recurring billing contract.

customerId.description: Gets or sets the identifier of the customer associated with this contract.

perBillInvoice.description: Gets or sets the per-bill invoice configuration, controlling how individual invoices are generated.

thresholds.description: Gets or sets the threshold rules that govern contract execution limits (e.g., maximum amount, retry caps).

aggregates.description: Gets or sets aggregate billing totals and counters tracked across contract executions.

schedule.description: Gets or sets the recurrence schedule that determines when the contract is executed.

payMethod.description: Gets or sets the payment method configuration used when the contract is billed.

emailNotifications.description: Gets or sets the email notification settings for contract billing events.

isActive.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this contract is active and eligible for execution.

planId.description:
Gets or sets the reusable plan this contract subscribes to for its price. Leave it empty to
price the contract inline through PhoeniXGate.Customers.Contracts.ContractCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.PerBillInvoice. When a plan is supplied, the
per-bill amounts on this payload are ignored and replaced with the plan's current price.

description.description: Gets or sets an optional description providing additional context for the contract.

name.description: Gets or sets the display name of the contract.

notes.description: Gets or sets the collection of notes attached to this contract.

tags.description: Gets or sets the collection of tags used to categorize or label this contract.

ContractCreateDto.description: Data transfer object for creating a new recurring billing contract.

ContractDeactivationReason.description:
Describes why a recurring billing contract was deactivated.
Persisted on the contract document for diagnostics and reporting.
x-enumDescriptions: Suspended by the billing engine after consecutive failures exceeded the MaxFailCount threshold.
Total execution count (successful + failed) reached MaxNumPayments.
Successful execution count reached MaxSuccessfulBills.
Cumulative amount billed reached MaxAmount.
The recurrence schedule produced no further occurrences — either the Until end date was reached or the recurrence count was exhausted.
Manually deactivated by an operator via the UI or API.
Cancelled by the cardholder themselves, from the link in an upcoming-charge reminder, with no operator involved.

customerId.description: Gets or sets the identifier of the customer who owns this contract.

customerName.description: Gets or sets the display name of the associated customer, used for grid rendering.

legacyNumber.description:
Gets or sets the contract's legacy numeric key, the integer identifier the v1 API resolves
contracts by. Server-owned: stamped at create and ignored on every inbound payload. Null on
contracts created before the field existed and not yet back-filled by the v1 data migration.

totalExecutions.description: Gets or sets the total number of billing executions performed for this contract.

successfulExecutions.description: Gets or sets the number of successful billing executions.

failedExecutions.description: Gets or sets the number of failed billing executions.

totalAmountBilled.description: Gets or sets the cumulative amount billed across all executions.

amountPerAttempt.description: Gets or sets the amount charged per billing attempt.

paymentMethodType.description: Gets or sets the type of payment method used by this contract.

perBillInvoice.description: Gets or sets the per-bill invoice configuration for this contract.

thresholds.description: Gets or sets the threshold rules governing contract execution limits.

aggregates.description: Gets or sets aggregate billing totals tracked across contract executions.

schedule.description: Gets or sets the recurrence schedule for contract execution.

payMethod.description: Gets or sets the payment method configuration used when the contract is billed.

emailNotifications.description: Gets or sets the email notification settings for contract billing events.

isActive.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this contract is active and eligible for execution.

planId.description:
Gets or sets the reusable plan this contract subscribes to for its price, or null when the
contract carries its own inline amount. When set, the recurring billing engine resolves the
amount from the plan at charge time and the per-bill amounts on this contract are a snapshot
of it.

description.description: Gets or sets an optional description providing additional context for the contract.

deactivationReason.description:
Gets or sets the reason this contract was deactivated, or null when the contract is active
            or was never deactivated. Server-owned: set by the recurring billing engine when a threshold
            or schedule ends the contract, by the self-service cancellation flow when the payer cancels,
            and cleared back to null when the contract is reactivated. Read-only over the API; an
            inbound payload can never set it.

name.description: Gets or sets the display name of the contract.

notes.description: Gets or sets the collection of notes attached to this contract.

tags.description: Gets or sets the collection of tags used to categorize this contract.

concurrencyStamp.description: Gets or sets the concurrency stamp used for optimistic concurrency control.

entityVersion.description: Gets the entity version, incremented on each modification for optimistic concurrency.

ContractDto.description:
Data transfer object representing a recurring billing contract, including execution statistics,
schedule configuration, and payment method details.

executedAt.description: The date and time the billing execution was performed.

success.description: Whether the billing attempt was approved by the payment processor.

amountBilled.description: The amount charged in this billing execution.

transactionId.description: The transaction ID created in the payment engine, if one was created.

failureReason.description: An explanation of why the billing execution failed. Null for successful attempts.

responseCode.description:
The processor response code for this execution. Used for failure classification
against Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailureRetryResultCodes.

scheduledRunTime.description:
The scheduled occurrence time this execution was triggered for.
Used by the Layer 2 idempotency guard to detect duplicate billing for the same
scheduled occurrence. Null for execution records created before this field was added.

ContractExecutionRecord.description:
A single execution record for a recurring billing contract, capturing the outcome
of one billing attempt. Stored as part of Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractAggregates.ExecutionHistory
(capped at the most recent 10 entries).

type.description: Gets or sets the funding instrument family. Determines which raw-data field ( or ) is consulted when the payment method carries no token binding (neither  nor ).

paymentTokenId.description: Internal vault identifier of a previously stored payment method, valid for both Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check contracts. This value correlates directly to stored cardholder data and is an internal binding: prefer Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.PaymentTokenReference on every external integration. It remains accepted inbound for callers that have not yet migrated, and is resolved and re-stamped server-side on every contract write.

card.description: Raw card account data. Populate only when no token is supplied and  is . Prefer  for new integrations.

check.description: Raw check / ACH account data. Populate only when no token is supplied and  is . Prefer  (a stored check/ACH token) for new integrations.

paymentTokenReference.description: The externally-emitted, chargeable public reference of the stored payment method this contract bills: the opaque `pt_`-prefixed handle returned when the payment method was stored. This is the identifier external integrations should use, and it is valid for both Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check contracts.

ContractPayMethod.description: Represents a payment method attached to a recurring billing contract. Exactly one of two shapes is expected on a Create request: Tokenised: set Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.PaymentTokenReference (the opaque `pt_` handle) to reference a previously stored payment method, for either Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type = Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card or Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type = Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check. Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card and Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check must be left null; the recurring billing engine resolves the underlying card or bank-account data from the token store at execution time. This is the recommended shape because it keeps PCI scope at the token layer.Raw: populate Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card (when Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type is Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Card) or Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check (when Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Type is Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethodType.Check) with the account data. Both token fields must be null. The Create validator rejects payloads that mix both shapes (a token alongside raw Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Card/Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractPayMethod.Check data) or that omit both.

ContractPayMethodType.description: Specifies the available payment method types that can be associated with a contract.

merchantId.description: The merchant that owns the plan.

name.description: The plan's operator-facing name. Must be unique within the owning merchant.

ContractPlanPriceChangePolicy.description: When a price change on a plan starts applying to the contracts that subscribe to it.
x-enumDescriptions: The new price applies to every charge executed from the moment the change was saved, including a charge that was already due and has not run yet.

The new price applies only to charges that fall due after the change was saved. A charge that was already due when the price changed still bills at the old price, so a subscriber is never re-priced part-way through a cycle they have already entered.
The new price applies to charges executed on or after an operator-chosen effective moment. Until then every subscriber keeps billing at the previous price.

re-expanding the full recurrence series every cycle. Enables efficient Cosmos queries
(filter at DB level: `contract.Schedule.NextScheduledRun <= now`).

startDate.description:
The earliest date on which this contract is eligible to bill. Set by the user
when creating the contract (defaults to the creation date) and may be set to a
future date to delay first billing. The recurrence engine anchors expansion to
this date and the daily billing job will not fire a contract whose
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.Recurrence.ContractSchedule.StartDate is in the future.
            
Null on legacy documents that predate this field. The canonical fallback chain
callers MUST use is `StartDate ?? Contract.CreationTime ?? DateTime.UtcNow`,
applied server-side by `ContractCrudAppService.ResolveScheduleAnchor`.
The UI does not expand the recurrence for a saved contract at all: it reads
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.Recurrence.ContractSchedule.NextScheduledRun through `ContractNextRunCalculator`, and only
previews an unsaved schedule (anchored on this date, or now when it has none).

Leave it empty for no limit. The contract create and update endpoints require a value

maxNumPayments.description:
Total number of billing attempts, successful or not, the contract may make before it

require at least 1 when a value is supplied; a non-positive value stored by an older save
is read as no limit.

maxSuccessfulBills.description:
Number of successful bills the contract may take before it deactivates itself. Leave it
empty for no limit. The contract create and update endpoints require at least 1 when a
value is supplied; a non-positive value stored by an older save is read as no limit.

maxFailCount.description:
Consecutive failed billing attempts that suspend the contract. Empty or `0` means the
contract is never suspended for failures and retries indefinitely. Unlike the three
capacity caps above, `0` is a valid, accepted value here.

failureInterval.description:
How many Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailurePeriod units to wait before retrying after a failed billing
attempt. Applied together with Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.FailurePeriod.

failurePeriod.description: The unit the  retry delay is measured in.

failureRetryResultCodes.description:
Processor response codes that count toward the Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount suspension threshold.
If a failure's response code is NOT in this list, the failure retries indefinitely
until the contract ends. If the code IS in this list and consecutive failures reach
Phoenix.SharedModels.Contract.ContractThresholds.MaxFailCount, the contract is suspended.
Null or empty means all failure codes count toward suspension.

x-enumDescriptions: A single fixed amount. The only shape permitted under the card brands' general convenience-fee program.

A percentage of the transaction base amount. Permitted only under the card-brand Government / Higher-Education service-fee program, and therefore gated behind the merchant Government/Education attestation. The per-network applicability guard (block on Visa, allow where the network permits) is enforced separately at transaction time.

ConvenienceFeePaymentChannel.description: A payment channel a merchant operates, used to justify a general-program convenience fee (epic #3157, channel-model story #3207). The card brands permit a convenience fee only when it is charged on a genuine alternative channel and a distinct standard channel also exists for the cardholder — the fee is for the channel, not for the card type.
x-enumDescriptions: Face-to-face, cardholder physically present. A standard channel; never an alternative.
Mail order (the cardholder mails payment). A standard channel; never an alternative.
Payment by check. A standard channel; never an alternative.
Online / e-commerce. A qualifying alternative channel; never a standard channel.
Telephone order. Valid as either a standard channel or a qualifying alternative channel.

Self-service kiosk / unattended terminal. A Card-Present Environment per Visa's glossary, so it is not a qualifying alternative channel and cannot bear a convenience fee. Retained only for persisted-document / OpenAPI-schema compatibility; never a standard channel.

customerId.description:
Optional trusted customer id the merchant binds to this session. When supplied, the
session relates to exactly this one customer: customer resolution at consent-capture
time uses this id exclusively and never falls back to the ambiguous cardholder-email
find-or-create, and the resulting transaction's `InvoiceData.CustomerId` is stamped
from it server-side. The id is validated at session-create time to exist, be active, and
belong to the session's merchant; a missing, inactive/soft-deleted, or cross-merchant id
is rejected. `null` (the default) preserves the historical anonymous behavior where
the customer is found-or-created from the cardholder email collected on the form.

prefilledFields.description:
Pre-populated field key/value pairs used to pre-fill the payment form. Use one of the well-known
field keys listed below, or an enabled merchant custom field name. Keys reserved for sensitive card
data or internal identifiers are always rejected.


Handling of an unrecognized custom-field key depends on whether the target page scopes its custom
fields (see the hosted page's custom-field allow-list). When the page does NOT scope its custom
fields, an unrecognized key is accepted but ignored when the form is rendered (unchanged behavior).
When the page DOES scope its custom fields, a key that is not a well-known field and not one of the
page's allowed custom fields is rejected at session create with an error naming the offending key.


A custom field the merchant has configured to accept a value from this API without showing it to
the payer is also accepted here. Its value is applied to the resulting transaction server-side,
exactly as supplied, and the field is not rendered on the payment form. Because the payer never
sees it and nobody can correct it later, the value is validated against the field's own rules
(maximum length, regular expression, numeric range) at session create: a value that breaks one of
them is rejected here rather than being carried and dropped at payment time.
Conditional: When SaveCardOnly is true.
Conditional: When AmountMode == Suggested.
Conditional: When PrefilledFields > 0.

Valid keys (in addition to enabled merchant custom field names):

- `allowed_payment_methods`: Comma-separated list of payment-method keys the session permits (e.g. card,ach).
            A directive, not a form field: it narrows the page's rendered payment methods for this
            session (intersection with the page's configured + capability-filtered methods). Empty
            or absent means no session-level restriction. Values must be recognized
            payment-method keys; session creation rejects unrecognized entries
- `base_amount`: Base transaction amount
- `billing_address1`: Billing address line 1
- `billing_address2`: Billing address line 2
- `billing_city`: Billing city
- `billing_country`: Billing country
- `billing_first_name`: Billing first name
- `billing_last_name`: Billing last name
- `billing_phone`: Billing phone number
- `billing_state`: Billing state or province
- `billing_zip`: Billing ZIP or postal code
- `convenience_fee`: Convenience fee amount
- `customer_email`: Customer email address
- `invoice_number`: Invoice number
- `order_summary`: JSON-serialized order summary containing line items and totals.
            Used to render a detailed summary panel on the payment page.
            Value must be a valid  JSON string
- `shipping`: Shipping amount
- `shipping_address1`: Shipping address line 1
- `shipping_address2`: Shipping address line 2
- `shipping_city`: Shipping city
- `shipping_country`: Shipping country
- `shipping_first_name`: Shipping first name
- `shipping_last_name`: Shipping last name
- `shipping_phone`: Shipping phone number
- `shipping_state`: Shipping state or province
- `shipping_zip`: Shipping ZIP or postal code
- `suppress_convenience_fee`: Declares that this session authoritatively carries no convenience fee, so the public
            surfaces must neither seed one from the merchant's convenience-fee configuration nor recompute
            a percentage one, and must render no fee line and no disclosure block. A directive, not a form
            field: it states a producer's decision rather than a value the payer sees. Must be one of the
             values (true, false); session
            creation rejects anything else. Absent means no declaration, which is the pre-directive
            behaviour: the surfaces resolve the fee themselves
- `surcharge`: Surcharge amount
- `tax`: Tax amount
- `tip`: Tip amount
- `vault_restriction`: Vault-restriction directive controlling how the payment instrument may be stored for
            this session. Must be one of the  constants
            (any, allow_new_and_saved, saved_only). A directive, not a form
            field. Absent means no restriction (any)

Optional — declares whether the cardholder's card should be vaulted as a reusable

`true` forces tokenization on for this session; `false` forces it off regardless

saveCardOnly.description: Optional — when `true`, this session saves the cardholder's card without charging it: the gateway runs a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 + AVS/CVV, immediate void) instead of a payment, then vaults the card and captures consent. Used for "save card now, charge later" onboarding / add-card-to-wallet. Default `false` (a normal chargeable session).

parentOrigin.description:
Optional HTTPS origin (scheme + host, e.g. `https://shop.example.com`) of the parent
page that will embed this HPP session in an iframe. When set, the HPP page emits
`postMessage` lifecycle events (`ready`, `session_loaded`,
`payment_succeeded`, etc.) using this value as the `targetOrigin`; never `'*'`.
The host portion must match an entry in the resolved page's `AllowedEmbeddingDomains`
(wildcard subdomains supported). When `null`, postMessage emission is disabled
(fail-closed) and the iframe still works for non-embedded use.
Conditional: When ParentOrigin is not empty. Max length: 2048.

enableFieldEvents.description: Optional opt-in to per-field `field_focused` / `field_blurred` postMessage events. When `true`, the iframe attaches a single delegated focus/blur listener on the form root and emits one envelope per focus boundary with the element's `data-hpp-field` identifier. Field values are NEVER included. When `false` (the default) no listener is registered, so there is no JS boundary at which a value could leak. Requires PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.CreateHppSessionInput.ParentOrigin to be set — otherwise the emitter is fail-closed and emits nothing regardless of this flag.

page's own campaign, so a merchant can attach a page to a campaign once instead of naming the
campaign on every link it issues. Supply a value and it wins over the page's.

currency.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code this link is denominated in, for example `USD`. Omit it
and the session takes the merchant's own configured currency, which is what every link got
before this field existed. Either way the created session reports the currency it settled on,
so an integrator can read it back rather than infer it.
Conditional: When Currency > 0.

campaignSource.description:
Optional per-channel source tag for this link: `email`, `sms`, `qr`,
`social`, or whatever short label names the channel you are issuing it through. Mint one
link per channel with a different tag and the campaign report compares them side by side.
Conditional: When CampaignSource > 0.

CreateIdempotencyStatus.description:
What create idempotency actually did to a transaction create request, reported on the create
response so a caller can tell from the response alone whether the key it sent protects the
charge.
x-enumDescriptions: The request carried no idempotencyKey, so there was nothing to deduplicate. A repeat send will charge again.

The request carried an idempotencyKey, but deduplication is not enabled for this merchant, so the key had no deduplication effect. It is stored with the transaction and remains available through the lookup-by-idempotency-key operation, but a repeat send with the same key will charge again. Ask your provider to enable deduplication for the merchant.

The request carried an idempotencyKey, deduplication is enabled, and this request claimed the key. This is the original create; a repeat send with the same key inside the deduplication window replays this transaction instead of charging again.

The idempotencyKey matched a create that had already completed for this merchant, so nothing was charged. The response body is that original transaction exactly as it stands, original identifiers and timestamps included.

CreateWalletPaymentSessionInput.description:
Provider-agnostic input for "create a wallet payment session". Apple Pay needs
this (the JS client calls `onvalidatemerchant` → our backend POSTs to
Apple's `startSession`). Wallets that don't issue server-side sessions
(Google Pay) won't implement
!:WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.Providers.IWalletPaymentSessionProvider
and the orchestrator returns "operation not supported by this provider".
            


The caller (HPP browser) supplies only the merchant being checked out on plus
the chosen provider type. Server-side resolution determines which persisted
`WalletProviderRegistration` row applies, using the merchant's own
`DigitalWallets[]` bindings — the Level / Platform-vs-Merchant
distinction is an internal data-modeling concept and never crosses the wire.
