customName.description:
Optional user-defined name for this stored payment method (e.g., "Marriott Chase",
"Bank of America Checkcard"). When set, takes priority over the computed display name.
Nullable for Cosmos backward compatibility — existing documents won't have this field.

initialSchemeTransactionId.description:
The initial (first-in-series) network / scheme transaction id captured from the processor's
authorization response on the cardholder-initiated credential-on-file transaction that stored
this credential. Lets any later transaction (CIT-COF or MIT, any card brand) resolve and echo
the original network transaction id from just the stored token / payment method, without
depending on a StoredCredentialConsent lookup.

lastSchemeTransactionId.description:
The most-recent-in-series network / scheme transaction id. At tokenization this equals
Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.InitialSchemeTransactionId. Card-network rules (Visa 11.1.5, Mastercard 13.1.1)
allow the most recent value in a series to be sent when the original is unavailable, so a later
story can advance this on each subsequent authorization response without losing the first-in-
series anchor. Nullable / non-sensitive as for Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.InitialSchemeTransactionId.

schemeTransactionIdBrand.description:
The card brand at the moment the network transaction id was captured (e.g. "Visa",
"Mastercard", "Discover", "Amex"). Retained because a co-branded card can switch networks
after storage; Mastercard's AltNetTranID handling requires the brand-at-capture to detect the
case where a stored Visa id must be sent in a Mastercard field. Emitting AltNetTranID is out of
scope here — this only preserves the data so the downstream echo work is not precluded.
Nullable / non-sensitive.

schemeTransactionIdProcessor.description:
The processor the network transaction id originated from ("tsys" / "fiserv"). The two
processors' response formats differ (TSYS a single 15-char Transaction Identifier; Fiserv
per-brand, whose Visa value can exceed 15 chars including the trailing Validation Code), so the
id is stored opaquely and tagged with its originating processor. Nullable / non-sensitive.

publicReference.description:
The externally-emitted, chargeable `PublicReference` of the backing `PaymentToken`
(the opaque `pt_`-prefixed handle) captured when this stored method was minted. Persisted
here so the tokenize-on-payment path can surface it on the transaction response / webhook
without re-reading the token, and so a later charge can round-trip the merchant-facing handle.
Distinct from Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.PaymentTokenId, which is the internal vault Guid (PAN-correlated,
never emitted). Nullable for Cosmos backward compatibility: stored methods minted before this
field predate it and carry `null` until the one-time DbMigrator backfill
(`CustomerStoredPaymentMethodPublicReferenceBackfillSeedContributor`) copies the backing
token's handle onto them. The backfill only ever fills a null and never rewrites an assigned
handle. Non-sensitive (an opaque random handle, not a PAN).

origin.description:
The surface / add-channel this stored payment method was captured through (manual admin,
            hosted payment page, virtual terminal, or API). Stamped once at creation and not changed
            afterward.

readerTokenFingerprint.description:
Dedupe fingerprint for a reader-token-backed (PAN-less) stored method: a one-way SHA-256
digest of the processor reader token that this method's backing vault token carries. Set
only for the reader-token shape (decrypt-and-forward processors such as MagTek DAF, where
the gateway never sees the PAN); `null` for every PAN- or account-backed method.

checkFingerprint.description:
Dedupe fingerprint for a check / ACH stored method: a keyed, non-reversible HMAC-SHA-256
digest of the routing number combined with the account number's last four digits. Set only
for the Check shape; `null` for card and reader-token methods.

detail surface, and lets an integrator list exactly what one key has transacted.
Narrowing only: the caller still sees nothing outside its own tenant / merchant scope.

reviewDisposition.description:
When set, restricts results to transactions whose manual fraud-review hold currently sits
                at the given disposition. Matches FraudReviewData.Disposition. Backs the review
                queue () and the dispositioned-history views.
                
                Equality-positive: a transaction that was never held has no FraudReviewData at all,
                so it is absent from the index and correctly drops out of every value of this filter.
                Supply MerchantId alongside it to keep the query single-partition and index-served.
                
                Matched by strict equality, which relies on every held transaction carrying an explicit
                disposition (see the invariant on ).

maxCreationTime.description:
Exclusive upper bound on the transaction's creation time: only transactions created
strictly before this instant are returned. Send an ISO-8601 timestamp in UTC. When
this is earlier than PhoeniXGate.Transactions.GetTransactionContinuationInput.MinCreationTime the range is unsatisfiable and an
empty page is returned rather than an error. Like every other filter on this request,
it must be held constant for the whole continuation sequence: a continuation token is
bound to the query that minted it, so changing a bound mid-sequence pages a different
query.

minCreationTime.description:
Inclusive lower bound on the transaction's creation time: only transactions created
at or after this instant are returned. Send an ISO-8601 timestamp in UTC. Must be held
constant for the whole continuation sequence (see PhoeniXGate.Transactions.GetTransactionContinuationInput.MaxCreationTime).

achWebAuthorizationText.description:
Optional per-page override for the NACHA WEB single-debit ACH authorization wording shown on
the ACH consent checkbox. Blank/unset renders the platform default. Supports the
`{MerchantName}` placeholder, substituted with the merchant's display name at render.
When set it is captured verbatim (with a content version hash) on each resulting ACH WEB
debit, so custom language a merchant's bank/ODFI approved becomes the recorded authorization.
The save-time validator guarantees a configured override never renders blank, so the
submit-time fail-closed gate is never reached with a blank override. Nullable (outside the
Cosmos CDB001 baseline) so existing documents deserialize unchanged.
Conditional: When AchWebAuthorizationText is not empty. Max length: 2000.

achRecurringWebAuthorizationText.description: Optional per-page override for the NACHA WEB recurring ACH authorization wording shown on the ACH consent checkbox of a Save-Card-with-Initial-Charge page. Blank/unset renders the platform default recurring language. Supports the `{MerchantName}` placeholder and the `{RecurringSchedule}` placeholder (substituted with the plan's schedule summary at render). Used only when the ACH debit establishes a recurring arrangement; a one-off ACH debit uses Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPageDisclosures.AchWebAuthorizationText. Captured verbatim (with a content version hash) on the resulting initial ACH WEB debit. Nullable (outside the Cosmos CDB001 baseline) so existing documents deserialize unchanged. Conditional: When AchRecurringWebAuthorizationText is not empty. Max length: 2000.

achSaveOnlyWebAuthorizationText.description: Optional per-page override for the NACHA save-only (storage) ACH authorization wording shown on the ACH consent checkbox of a store-bank-account-no-charge page. Blank/unset renders the platform default save-only language. Supports the `{MerchantName}` placeholder, substituted with the merchant's display name at render. Used only when the account is stored without any debit being taken now; a one-off debit uses Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPageDisclosures.AchWebAuthorizationText and an initial-charge recurring arrangement uses Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPageDisclosures.AchRecurringWebAuthorizationText. Captured verbatim (with a content version hash) on the resulting save. Nullable (outside the Cosmos CDB001 baseline) so existing documents deserialize unchanged. Conditional: When AchSaveOnlyWebAuthorizationText is not empty. Max length: 2000.

allowTransparentEmbedding.description:
Opt-in to a see-through backdrop when this page is rendered inside a merchant iframe, so the
merchant's own page shows through behind the payment form. `null`/`false` is the
default and keeps the page fully opaque.


The transparent render additionally requires that the request is genuinely framed (resolved
server-side from the browser-set `Sec-Fetch-Dest` header) and that
PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPaymentPageCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.AllowedEmbeddingDomains is configured, so it applies only inside the parents
the merchant allowlisted. A page opened directly as a standalone payment link always paints
its own background. Only the backdrop clears: the payment form keeps its own paint.

hideTitle.description:
Suppress the page PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPaymentPageCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.Title on the payer-facing page (both the Classic and the
Streamlined renderer). `null`/`false` is the default and renders the title exactly as
before. Display-only: the title is still stored, still returned, and still shown on the
administrative surfaces (grid, quick view, favorites subtitle).

hideMerchantName.description:
Suppress the merchant business-name line in the Streamlined identity header on the payer-facing
page. `null`/`false` is the default. The banner image in that same header stays
governed by PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HostedPaymentPageCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.HideBanner.


Display-only, and deliberately narrow: the merchant name still reaches the Apple Pay / Paze sheet
total label and the NACHA ACH consent copy (and the consent evidence captured with an ACH
authorization), which must name the real merchant regardless of this flag.

campaignId.description:
Optional campaign this page belongs to. Sessions created from this page inherit it when the

HppCaptureMode.description:
Capture timing for a chargeable Hosted Payment Page (the "Payment" flow). This is an axis
orthogonal to card storage: a page composes a capture mode with the existing save-card option
(tokenization / `SavePaymentDetails`) rather than encoding the combination as a dedicated
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose value. "Save card + delayed capture" is therefore simply
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.Payment + Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppCaptureMode.Authorize + save-card enabled.
x-enumDescriptions: Authorize and capture funds in a single step (the historical, default behavior). null resolves here, so every pre-existing chargeable page keeps doing an implicit Sale.

Authorize now, capture later (delayed capture). The resulting transaction is an Authorization in an Authorized state, eligible for capture and void per the action matrix; the capture is completed later against the resulting transaction id via the existing capture action path (including the Apple Pay single-use token case).

HppDeclineRetryMode.description:
Decides what a hosted payment page session does with its single-use payment link when the
processor answers a submission with a decline.
x-enumDescriptions: The historical behavior, and the default at every level of the resolution chain. Any processor answer spends the link permanently: the session stays Consumed and a payer who reloads it is told the link has already been used.
A definite issuer decline hands the link back to Pending so the payer can correct their card and resubmit on the same URL, instead of having to ask the merchant for a new link.

HppLinkLifetime.description:
How long a merchant-created payment link stays payable. Selected per session at create time and
frozen onto the session, alongside (not instead of) the requested expiry in seconds: the lifetime
picks the bounds the requested expiry must fall within.
x-enumDescriptions: The historical short single-use checkout session: 60 to 900 seconds, defaulting to 600, and still subject to the tenant's own min/max/default TTL settings. What every caller that does not name a lifetime gets.

A long-lived link, bounded by ExtendedMinTtlSeconds and ExtendedMaxTtlSeconds (1 hour to 90 days), for a link that is emailed or texted and paid later. The upper bound is capped by the tenant's HostedPaymentPageSettings.SessionMaxExtendedTtlSeconds setting.

A link that never expires on its own. The session carries no expiry instant and no document time-to-live; it stops being payable only when it is paid, cancelled, or revoked. Requesting an expiry in seconds alongside this is rejected rather than ignored.

HppPagePurpose.description:
First-class, instance-level classification of what a hosted payment page is for. Lets a
merchant dedicate a specific HPP instance to a non-payment task (collecting and storing card
details) instead of flipping a per-session flag on every link.
x-enumDescriptions: The default, historical behavior: a chargeable payment page. null resolves here, so every pre-existing HPP instance keeps behaving exactly as before.

A card-capture page: the cardholder's card is validated via a zero-dollar account verification (authorize $0 + AVS/CVV, immediate void), then vaulted with stored-credential consent. No charge is taken. Amount-bearing configuration (tax, shipping, convenience fee, invoice amounts, donations, tip) is irrelevant and is hidden in the builder / rejected by the validator. Requires the merchant's processor to advertise SupportsZeroDollarVerification.

A card-capture page that also charges the first of a recurring schedule. The cardholder's card is charged a real initial sale (the first payment of a referenced reusable recurring plan, framed as the customer-initiated transaction that establishes the credential-on-file agreement), vaulted with Recurring stored-credential consent, and a customer Contract is created for the remaining payments. Like SaveCard, the amount-bearing builder configuration (tax, shipping, convenience, invoice, donations, tip, customer-set amount) is hidden: the charged amount is driven entirely by the inlined recurring definition, not by per-page amount fields. Requires a complete inlined recurring definition (RecurringPlan).

HppPresentationMode.description:

cardholder navigates to, or as a chrome-less surface mounted inside a merchant-site iframe.
This governs page chrome only (outer surface background, full-viewport height, page padding).
It never changes the session flow, the fields collected, or any compliance content: consent
capture, the NACHA WEB authorization, the convenience-fee disclosure, and the confirmation
panel render identically in both modes.

A chrome-less compact presentation for mounting inside a merchant-site iframe: no standalone page surface or full-viewport height, tight paddings, and narrow-width behavior that stays readable down to a 320 px viewport without horizontal scrolling.

saveCardOnly.description: `true` when the session saves the card via a zero-dollar verification instead of charging it ("save card now, charge later"). Currently always `false` in practice: save-card-only is fail-closed at session creation until the no-charge verification routing is wired end to end, so no persisted session carries it set. Once the path lands it will always also tokenize and capture consent. Shown on admin screens.

Output DTO representing an HPP session for management display.
Pre-filled field values are redacted — only the field key names are exposed
to prevent accidental PII/sensitive data leakage via management APIs.

consentRequired.description: Whether the cardholder must tick the stored-credential consent box before the payment can be submitted.

Whether the public page renders the stored-credential consent prompt for this session, i.e.
whether the session declared any credential-storage intent. When `false`, consent plays
no part in the flow and PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionEffectiveShapeDto.ConsentRequired is `false`.

requestedCredentialStorage.description:
The stored-credential usage scopes the cardholder is being asked to consent to, after
            server-side defaulting and purpose forcing: a tokenizing session that declared no scope
            resolves to , and a Save Card with Initial
            Charge session always has  unioned in on top of
            whatever the request asked for. null means no credential storage was requested.

pagePurpose.description:
The page purpose this session actually runs, after applying the request's optional
            pagePurpose override over the targeted page's own configured purpose. A page with no
            configured purpose resolves to .

tokenizeOnPayment.description:
Whether the cardholder's payment method will be vaulted as a reusable token. This is the
effective decision after the merchant's tokenize-by-default setting is applied and after the
targeted page's tokenization toggle (`SupportTokenization` / `SavePaymentDetails`)
has had its say. A request that asked for `tokenizeOnPayment: true` against a page whose
merchant disabled tokenization reports `false` here: that is the veto, which previously
only appeared in a server-side log line. Always `true` for a card-capture purpose, which
exists to store the credential.

saveCardOnly.description:
Whether this session stores the payment method with no charge at all. `true` for a
resolved Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.SaveCard purpose or an explicit `saveCardOnly`
request on a Payment page. Deliberately `false` for
Phoenix.SharedModels.HostedPaymentPage.HppPagePurpose.SaveCardWithInitialCharge, which takes a real initial charge, so
a request that sent `saveCardOnly: true` against that purpose reports `false` here.

captureMode.description:
Capture timing for the chargeable Payment flow:  authorizes
            and captures in one step,  authorizes now for a later
            capture. Resolved from the request's optional override over the page's configured value.
            Reported as  for a card-capture purpose, where capture
            timing is not an axis: those purposes set their own transaction shape.

amountMode.description:
How the cardholder may set the amount. 
            leaves the page's own amount behaviour in charge; 
            pre-fills an editable amount;  pre-fills a read-only
            amount that the server verifies on submit.

customerEmailVisibility.description:
The per-session visibility of the payer-facing customer-email field, as it was accepted and
            stored. null means the session did not override it and the page's own
            FieldCustomerEmail applies.

declineRetryMode.description:
What this session does with its payment link when a payment is declined, as resolved from
            the per-session override, the hosted page and the tenant default when the session was
            created.

linkLifetime.description:
The link lifetime the session was actually minted with, read off the created session rather
            than off the request.  is what a request that named no
            lifetime resolves to.

remainingDeclineReleases.description:
How many further times this link may be reopened after a declined payment. Always zero when
PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionEffectiveShapeDto.DeclineRetryMode is PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppDeclineRetryMode.ConsumeOnDecline, and it
counts down as a payer spends attempts.

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 currency this session is denominated in, upper-cased. A request that named one
gets it back verbatim, having been checked against the merchant's configured currency; a
request that named none gets the merchant's currency, which is the defaulting this block
exists to report. `null` only when the merchant has no currency configured at all, which
is the state every session predating this field is in.

customerId.description:
The customer this session is bound to, echoed from the request's `customerId` after it
was validated to exist, be active, and belong to the page's merchant. `null` for an
unbound session, where the cardholder's email is the only customer-resolution anchor.

prefilledFieldKeys.description:
The prefilled field keys stored on the session, in no particular order. Values are never
echoed. Compare against what was sent to confirm every key was accepted, and note that the
server may add one: deriving a locked amount from a fixed-amount page stamps
`base_amount` even when the request supplied none.

ignoredPrefillKeys.description:
The subset of PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionEffectiveShapeDto.PrefilledFieldKeys that the hosted page will silently ignore
when it renders: keys that are neither a well-known field nor an enabled, page-visible
merchant custom field. They are accepted and persisted rather than rejected, for backward
compatibility, so this list is the only signal that a key will have no effect (usually a
typo, or a custom field that is disabled or hidden for hosted pages).

HppSessionEffectiveShapeDto.description:

session-create response so an integrator can confirm what was persisted without loading the

HppSessionPurpose.description:
Classifies the calling context that produced an HPP session, which in turn drives the
allowed TTL bounds and any other purpose-specific policy. The default is
PhoeniXGate.HostedPaymentPage.HppSessionPurpose.CheckoutLink, which is the historical merchant-facing pay-link behavior
with a 1-minute–15-minute TTL ceiling appropriate for hot checkout flows.
x-enumDescriptions: Standard merchant-facing pay-link session. Short TTL (60s–900s).
Session created by the invoicing module's send flow to back an invoice's pay-link. Long TTL (1h–90d) so the link survives net-30 invoice terms with margin for late payment.

Session created by the Merchant Billing module to back a stored-payment-method capture link emailed to a merchant. Long TTL (1h–90d) so a link sent now can be completed days later, on the merchant's own time, rather than synchronously by an operator.

HppSessionStatus.description: Represents the lifecycle status of an HPP session.
x-enumDescriptions: The session has been created and is awaiting use by a customer. Also the status a session returns to when a premature consume is released: a submission that was rejected by pure request-shape validation before the orchestrator was invoked leaves the link usable, so the payer can correct their input and resubmit on the same link (see Consumed).

The session has been consumed by a transaction submission. Terminal in practice: the only exit is the narrow release back to Pending performed by HppSession.ReleaseConsume, which requires that the session carries no OrchestratorDispatchedAt marker, that the consuming transaction id is still the one recorded, and that no vault token was minted. Once a submission reaches the orchestrator the marker is durable and the session stays Consumed regardless of the outcome, including a decline. Submit paths additionally validate the request BEFORE consuming, so a rejected request usually never spends the link in the first place; the release covers the rules that can only run inside the create.
The session has been manually revoked by an administrator.

The session was cancelled by the parent page via the iframe two-way command channel Distinct from Revoked (admin-initiated) for clarity in audit + reporting — same terminal effect (session can no longer be consumed).

HppShippingAmountMode.description: Discriminator for where a hosted payment page's shipping amount comes from.
x-enumDescriptions: The cardholder types the shipping amount into the shipping field (today's behaviour, and what a persisted null mode coalesces to).

The merchant fixed a single shipping amount for this page. The field renders visible, seeded with that amount, and non-editable, and the create path stamps the configured value server-side. An amount of zero is free shipping, which is a configured value like any other.

The shipping amount comes from a carrier rate quote the cardholder selects. Reserved by this enum so the rate-selection story adds a member here rather than a second flag and a rule relating the two. Not implemented, and refused at save until it is. No runtime behaviour reads it: every consumer goes through HppFlatShippingAmountPolicy, which treats a non-Flat mode as "no configured shipping", so a page saved in this mode would behave as CardholderEntered under a name that promises a quoted rate. The page validator therefore rejects it; remove that rule when rate selection ships, not before.

entries.description:
One entry per trigger the simulator honoured, plus one per response value it filled in from a
default. Ordered as the simulator resolved them.

The persisted record of what the loopback sandbox processor simulated on a transaction: which
published triggers the request actually fired, and which response values came from a default
rather than from a trigger.

family.description:
Which part of the simulator produced this entry, as one of the
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Loopback.LoopbackSimulationFamilies names.

catalogId.description:
The published identifier this entry resolves against in the loopback catalog, or
null when the entry records something the catalog does not enumerate.

resolvedCode.description:
The verification response code the simulator returned, on an address-verification or
cardholder-verification entry. null on every other family.

matchedOn.description: What the simulator matched on, in prose: "Amount cents", "Billing ZIP", "Latency profile".

observedValue.description: The value that was matched, when it is safe to carry. null otherwise.

effect.description: What the simulator did as a result, stated as an observed fact rather than as documentation.

isDefault.description:
true when this entry records a response value the simulator filled in from a
            default because nothing matched, rather than a trigger that fired.

LoopbackSimulationEntry.description:
One thing the loopback simulator did: a published trigger that fired, or a response value that
fell through to a default.

MITReasonCode.description:
Reason codes for merchant-initiated transactions. Maps to card network indicators
(e.g. TSYS `POSDataCode` CardInputMode values) that justify an MIT against a stored credential.
Required on any transaction where Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.InitiationType is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.InitiationType.MerchantInitiated.
x-enumDescriptions: Fixed or variable charges on a scheduled basis for a subscription or ongoing service the cardholder has enrolled in.
A series of charges dividing a known total amount over a defined schedule.
Charges triggered by a specific, pre-agreed event (e.g. account balance threshold, usage overage). Not on a schedule.

Recharging after a declined or reversed transaction, in accordance with card network resubmission rules. Must be for the same amount as the original declined attempt and within the network's permitted resubmission window.
Re-authorizing a prior authorization (e.g. when the original authorization has expired but the merchant still intends to capture).
A charge finalized after the cardholder's original authorization (e.g. tip adjustment, additional services added after checkout, or final amounts determined after service completion).
No-show or cancellation fee where the cardholder made a reservation or booking and failed to cancel within the required window.
Additional authorization on top of a prior authorization (e.g. hotel incidentals, car rental overages).

            inherits .
            Only the path itself is overridable — collection plumbing (HPP id, collection

            House Merchant per-assignment friction.

MerchantBillingAssignment.description:
Per-merchant billing assignment embedded on the Merchant aggregate root.
Replaces the standalone MerchantPricePlanAssignment container; a merchant has at most
one active price plan at a time, so the assignment behaves as a single-row property
rather than a separate aggregate. Lookup is a point-read on the merchant; the
platform never needs cross-time assignment history (audit log captures changes).

MerchantBillingCaptureLinkStatus.description:
Operator-visible status of the outstanding send-a-link capture link for a billed merchant's
stored payment method. Derived from the latest link-origin
`MerchantBillingPaymentMethodCaptureIntent` for the (reseller, merchant) pair; the intent is
the source of truth (its consumed / cancelled / expiry markers map one-to-one to these states).
x-enumDescriptions: No capture link has been sent for this merchant (no link-origin intent exists).
A link has been sent and is still usable: issued, not yet consumed, not cancelled, and not past its expiry. The merchant can complete the hosted page; the operator can resend or cancel it.
The merchant completed the hosted page: the bound capture-intent was consumed.
The link passed its expiry without being consumed or cancelled. It can be reissued.
An operator revoked the link before it was used. Its hosted page can no longer be completed; it can be reissued.

status.description: The derived status of the latest link for this merchant (None when no link was ever sent).

kind.description:
Card or ACH — the instrument family the outstanding link captures. Null when no link exists; a
            resend reissue reuses this kind so the operator is never asked to re-pick it.

expiresAt.description: When the link (and its bound session/intent) expires, in UTC. Null when no link exists.

canResend.description:
Whether a resend action is available: true whenever a link exists (a usable link is resent for
its existing session; an expired/cancelled/completed one is reissued fresh).

canCancel.description: Whether a cancel action is available: only a still-usable (pending) link can be revoked.

MerchantBillingCaptureLinkStatusDto.description:
Operator-visible status of the outstanding send-a-link capture link for a merchant's stored
payment method, returned by `IMerchantBillingPaymentMethodAppService.GetCaptureLinkStatusAsync`
(and echoed by the cancel call). Carries only non-sensitive link metadata: never a token, recipient
PII, or any card/account detail.

MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.description:
Status of an admin all-resellers billing fan-out batch. A batch wraps the
per-reseller PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunStatus runs the Durable fan-out workflow
produces; only one non-terminal (PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.Pending/PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunBatchStatus.Running) batch may be
in flight at a time (the batch-level single-in-flight guard).
x-enumDescriptions: Batch created and the workflow has been started but discovery has not run yet.
The fan-out workflow is running per-reseller billing runs.
Every reseller that ran completed without a failed reseller run.
At least one reseller ran successfully and at least one reseller run failed.
No reseller ran successfully and at least one reseller run failed.

An admin force-cleared the batch from the Billing Runs page. A terminal, non-failure state distinct from Failed: it records a deliberate operator action (releasing a stuck or stale batch) rather than a run that errored. Like every other terminal status it is reclaimable by the next fan-out's lock-recovery, and is never treated as in-progress.

MerchantBillingRunResultStatus.description: Outcome status for an individual merchant within a billing run.
x-enumDescriptions: Merchant rated successfully. Terminal for a dry run; on a non-dry run it is a transient pre-dispatch state that the fulfillment dispatcher advances to a path-specific status (Invoiced or ChargePending).
Billing failed for this merchant.
Merchant was skipped (e.g., inactive or excluded).
No active price plan assigned to this merchant.
No usage recorded for this merchant in the billing period.

Neither ResellerBillingPreferences.DefaultFulfillmentPath nor the per-merchant MerchantBillingAssignment.FulfillmentPath override is set, so the resolver cannot decide how to collect payment for this merchant.
The effective fulfillment path is RecurringContract but no active MerchantBillingPaymentMethod row exists for the (ResellerId, MerchantId) pair, so the recurring charge has no token to draft against.
The effective fulfillment path is RecurringContract but the reseller has not configured a CollectionMerchantId, so there is no party to own the recurring contract.
The effective fulfillment path is Invoicing but the reseller has not configured an HppPageId, so the generated invoice has no payment link destination.
The merchant was rated successfully and the Invoicing fulfillment path produced an issued invoice. Terminal for the Invoicing path — see MerchantBillingRunResult.InvoiceId for the artifact.

The RecurringContract path charge completed successfully. Set when the downstream charge reconciliation (tracked separately) confirms an approved transaction; see MerchantBillingRunResult.TransactionId.

The merchant was rated successfully and the RecurringContract path dispatched a charge request into the Transaction Manager. The charge has not yet been reconciled; the run records this as a non-terminal "awaiting result" state. See MerchantBillingRunResult.ContractId.
The RecurringContract path charge was attempted but declined or errored. Set by the downstream charge reconciliation (tracked separately).

Usage was recorded for the merchant in the billing period, but the plan produced no positive-charge line item, so there is nothing to bill. Distinct from NoUsage (which means no usage aggregates existed at all): here the merchant genuinely transacted, the usage simply fell entirely within a rate entry's included/free allowance or matched no billable rate entry. Where a rate entry matched the usage, the rated run keeps the zero-billable line item visible so the operator can see the usage and why it was not charged; usage that matched no rate entry produces no line item.

Billing run is currently processing merchants.
All merchants processed successfully.
Some merchants processed successfully, others failed.
All merchants failed or the run itself failed.
Billing run was manually cancelled.

digitalWallets.description:
Per-merchant digital wallet bindings (Apple Pay, Google Pay, …). At most one
entry per `WalletProviderType`; each row carries the master enable
flag and a pointer to the `WalletProviderRegistration` row this
merchant uses (platform-level or merchant-level).

threeDSBindings.description:
Per-merchant 3-D Secure provider bindings. At most one entry per `ThreeDSProviderType`;
each row carries the master enable flag, the policy mode, and the vendor credentials.
            


The JWT secret is write-only. It is never returned on a read, so a caller round-tripping a
merchant sends null back here; a null or empty secret on a save keeps the one already
stored, and a non-empty one replaces it. There is therefore no payload that clears a secret
without also removing the binding.
Conditional: When ThreeDSBindings is set.

taxBindings.description:
Per-merchant tax provider bindings. At most one entry per provider name; each row carries the master
enable flag, whose provider account the lookups are billed to, and the provider's configuration
values.
            


Secret field values are write-only. They are never returned on a read, so a caller round-tripping a
merchant sends null back here; a null or empty secret on a save keeps the one already stored, and a
non-empty one replaces it. There is therefore no payload that clears a secret without also removing
the binding.


A binding whose credential source is `Gateway` must carry no field values: the gateway holds
those credentials, and a copy of them on a merchant document is exactly what the credential source
exists to avoid. The validator refuses a gateway-sourced binding that supplies any.
Conditional: When TaxBindings is set.

MerchantDigitalWallet.description:
Per-merchant digital wallet record (Apple Pay, Google Pay, …). Persisted as an
element of `Merchant.DigitalWallets`. The aggregate keeps at most one
entry per Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.MerchantDigitalWallet.WalletProviderType; collection membership decides whether
the merchant participates in that wallet at all, and Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.MerchantDigitalWallet.IsEnabled
decides whether the merchant currently has it switched on.
            

Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.MerchantDigitalWallet.PaymentTokenizationRegistrationId points at a row in the
PaymentTokenization module's `WalletProviderRegistration` aggregate. It may
reference either a platform-level row (merchant inherits the platform's Apple
Merchant ID + domain set) or a merchant-level row (this merchant brought its own
Apple Merchant ID).


Adding new fields here: this type is persisted inside Cosmos `Merchant`
documents, so any new field must be nullable (or default to a safe value) so that
existing documents written before the field existed deserialise cleanly.

digitalWallets.description:
Gets or sets the per-merchant digital wallet bindings (Apple Pay, Google Pay, …).
At most one entry per `WalletProviderType`; each carries the master enable
flag and a pointer to the `WalletProviderRegistration` row this merchant uses
(platform-level or merchant-level).

threeDSBindings.description: Gets or sets the per-merchant 3-D Secure provider bindings. At most one entry per `ThreeDSProviderType`; each carries the master enable flag, the policy mode, and the vendor credentials. The JWT secret is never populated on a read. It is stripped server-side before this DTO leaves the application service, so a caller sees null there whether or not one is stored. Sending null or an empty string back on a save keeps the stored secret; sending a value replaces it.

taxBindings.description: Gets or sets the per-merchant tax provider bindings. At most one entry per provider name; each carries the master enable flag, whose provider account the lookups are billed to, and the provider's configuration values. Secret field values are never populated on a read. They are stripped server-side before this DTO leaves the application service, and each field reports `isConfigured` instead so an operator can tell a stored secret from an empty one. Sending null or an empty string back on a save keeps the stored secret; sending a value replaces it. A binding whose credential source is `Gateway` carries no values at all: the gateway's own provider credentials are never copied onto a merchant, and are resolved at lookup time instead.

Identifier of the screening provider, matching a provider returned by the screening provider
discovery endpoint. Required.

providerName.description:
Which tax provider this entry binds the merchant to, matching
WinkPG.TaxCalculation.ITaxProviderContributor.ProviderName. A string rather than an enum so adding a
provider package does not change this assembly, and compared case-insensitively everywhere.
A null or blank provider is treated as no binding at all, so an incompletely boarded row
cannot silently become a live selection.
Required: When IsEnabled is true.

isEnabled.description:
Master enable flag for this provider on this merchant. When `false` or null, the selector
must not return this binding even though the row exists.

credentialSource.description:
Whose provider account the lookups are billed to. Null reads as
            .

fieldValues.description: The provider-declared configuration values for this merchant, keyed by the setting names the provider's contributor declares. Secret values are stored encrypted and are stripped, not decrypted, on every read that leaves the server: the admin UI and the API both see null and re-send a secret only when the operator changes it. The one path that sees plaintext is WinkPG.TaxCalculation.Merchant.IMerchantTaxBindingProvider, which exists to hand credentials to a provider. Empty for a WinkPG.TaxCalculation.Merchant.TaxCredentialSource.Gateway binding, whose values are filled in at read time from the host-scoped provider settings instead. A gateway-sourced row that carried values would be a copy of the gateway's key living on a merchant document. Conditional: When FieldValues is set.

defaultCountryCode.description:
The country code to use for a lookup that does not name one. Null falls back to the
gateway-wide `TaxCalculation.DefaultCountryCode` setting.

MerchantTaxBinding.description: Per-merchant tax provider binding. Persisted as an element of `Merchant.TaxBindings`, and the successor to the `TaxCalculation.ProviderName` setting the service first shipped with. The setting shape it replaces resolved a merchant through the ambient operating context, which is null on an Azure Functions host and on any path with no signed-in operator, so a merchant's selection silently fell through to the gateway-wide value. Tax liability is a property of the selling merchant, and a payment that computes tax on a background path has to reach the same answer as one computed while an operator watches, so the merchant has to be named explicitly. Collection membership decides whether the merchant is boarded with that provider at all, and WinkPG.TaxCalculation.Merchant.MerchantTaxBinding.IsEnabled decides whether it is currently switched on: the same two-level shape the 3-D Secure and wallet bindings use, so a merchant can be un-switched without losing credentials. Adding fields here: this type is persisted inside Cosmos `Merchant` documents, so every value-type member is nullable. A non-nullable value type added later reads back as its CLR default on every document written before it existed, which is indistinguishable from a merchant that chose that value.

providerType.description:
Which 3-D Secure provider this entry binds the merchant to. Nullable per the Cosmos-baseline
            convention; a null provider type is treated as no binding at all rather than as
            , so an incompletely boarded row cannot silently
            become a live selection.

isEnabled.description:
Master enable flag for this provider on this merchant. When `false` or null, the
selector must not return this binding even though the row exists.

policyMode.description:
How hard the merchant wants authentication applied. Null means the platform default, which
            callers read as .

apiKey.description:
The vendor API key. Successor to `3DSPaayApiKey`. Not a secret in the sense the JWT
secret is (it is sent as a request header and appears as a JWT audience), so it round-trips
on reads; it is still never logged.
Required: When IsEnabled is true.

jwtSecret.description: The shared secret the request JWT is signed with. Successor to `3DSPaaySecret`, which the TSYS profile stores and renders in cleartext. Stored encrypted. The value persisted in the Cosmos document is ciphertext produced by the merchants module's binding cipher. It is stripped, not decrypted, on every read that leaves the server: the admin UI and the API both see null here and re-send the secret only when the operator changes it. The one path that sees plaintext is WinkPG.ThreeDSecure.Merchant.IMerchantThreeDSBindingProvider, which exists to hand it to the provider. Never log this, never put it on a WinkPG.ThreeDSecure.Messages.ThreeDSProviderError, never attach it to an exception, and never emit it in an event or a webhook payload.

providerRegistrationId.description:
Optional pointer at a vendor-side registration record for this merchant, for vendors that
board a merchant out of band and hand back an identifier. Nullable because most bindings

MerchantThreeDSBinding.description: Per-merchant 3-D Secure provider binding. Persisted as an element of `Merchant.ThreeDSBindings`, and the successor to the seven `3DSPaay*` fields the TSYS processor profile carries today. The binding is deliberately independent of the acquiring processor. The directory server and access control server a card authenticates against belong to the card network, not the acquirer, so a merchant can change processor without changing 3-D Secure vendor and vice versa. Folding these fields into `ProcessorProfile` (where the legacy ones live) makes the two impossible to move apart. Collection membership decides whether the merchant is boarded with that provider at all, and WinkPG.ThreeDSecure.Merchant.MerchantThreeDSBinding.IsEnabled decides whether it is currently switched on: the same two-level shape `MerchantDigitalWallet` uses, so a merchant can be un-switched without losing credentials. Adding fields here: this type is persisted inside Cosmos `Merchant` documents, so every value-type member is nullable. A non-nullable value type added later reads back as its CLR default on every document written before it existed, which is indistinguishable from a merchant that chose that value.

digitalWallets.description:
Per-merchant digital wallet bindings (Apple Pay, Google Pay, …). At most one
entry per `WalletProviderType`; each row carries the master enable
flag and a pointer to the `WalletProviderRegistration` row this
merchant uses (platform-level or merchant-level).

threeDSBindings.description:
Per-merchant 3-D Secure provider bindings. At most one entry per `ThreeDSProviderType`;
each row carries the master enable flag, the policy mode, and the vendor credentials.
            


The JWT secret is write-only. It is never returned on a read, so a caller round-tripping a
merchant sends null back here; a null or empty secret on a save keeps the one already
stored, and a non-empty one replaces it. There is therefore no payload that clears a secret
without also removing the binding.
Conditional: When ThreeDSBindings is set.

taxBindings.description:
Per-merchant tax provider bindings. At most one entry per provider name; each row carries the master
enable flag, whose provider account the lookups are billed to, and the provider's configuration
values.
            


Secret field values are write-only. They are never returned on a read, so a caller round-tripping a
merchant sends null back here; a null or empty secret on a save keeps the one already stored, and a
non-empty one replaces it. There is therefore no payload that clears a secret without also removing
the binding.


A binding whose credential source is `Gateway` must carry no field values: the gateway holds
those credentials, and a copy of them on a merchant document is exactly what the credential source
exists to avoid. The validator refuses a gateway-sourced binding that supplies any.
Conditional: When TaxBindings is set.

tipAmount.description: Replacement gratuity in major currency units (e.g. `5.00` = $5.00). Mutates the settlement `` and `` elements and patches the transaction document's `/InvoiceData/Amounts/Tip` field when populated. `0` is interpreted as "clear the existing tip". The transaction's `Total` is intentionally not patched — `TrxAmounts.Total` is a computed property (`Base + Tip + Tax + Shipping + Convenience`) re-derived on every hydration, so the new tip flows through to the displayed Total automatically without a stored mutation. Wired today. Conditional: When TipAmount and HasValue meet conditions. Must be >= 0.

OfflineAdjustmentFields.description:
Structured field bundle for the OfflineAdjustment operation. Each property is optional;
only the populated fields are emitted into the adjustment-request XML and propagated
onto the corresponding transaction-document patches.
            
"Offline" denotes that the adjustment is applied to the transaction's settlement record
without contacting the processor network. Eligible fields are limited to those the
legacy `TipAdjustment.vb` path collected from `htData` (TIPAMT / TAXAMT /
LEVEL3AMT / PONUM / STREET / ZIP) — adjusting any other field requires re-authorization
at the rails (incremental authorization stage, separate ticket).
            
Industry eligibility for the tip-bearing path (TIPAMT) is enforced inside
`WinkPG.TransactionManager.ProcessorCommon.TipAdjustmentProcessor` today; lifting
the rule to a stage-level precondition is a deferred follow-up and is not duplicated
on this DTO.

UTC timestamp of the moment Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalData.Disposition last moved. Set alongside every

UTC instant by which a Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalDisposition.Pending disposition must be

requestedAmount.description:
The amount the gateway asked the issuer to authorize, in major currency units, snapshotted

approvedAmount.description:
The lesser amount the issuer actually authorized, in major currency units, snapshotted at
detection time. The shortfall a split tender needs to collect is
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PartialApprovalData.RequestedAmount minus this value.

PartialApprovalData.description:
Durable record of a partial approval: the issuer authorized less than the requested amount,
and the gateway captured the evidence plus the lifecycle of the decision that followed.

PartialApprovalDisposition.description:
Tracks what happened to a partially approved authorization: the issuer approved less than
the requested amount, and someone (the operator, the cardholder, or a gateway timeout) has
to decide whether to keep the reduced authorization, void it, or collect the shortfall on a
second tender.
x-enumDescriptions: The partial approval has been detected and recorded, but nobody has decided its fate yet. The transaction is holding a reduced authorization at the issuer and is waiting on an operator/cardholder acknowledgment until DispositionDeadlineUtc elapses.
The reduced authorization was accepted as-is. No reversal is issued and the transaction proceeds through the normal capture/settlement path for the approved (lesser) amount.

The reduced authorization was rejected and reversed, so the issuer hold is released. The reason is recorded on VoidReason (operator choice, acknowledgment timeout, or an automatic gateway policy void).
The reduced authorization was kept and a follow-up tender was started to collect the shortfall. The continuation transaction carries the same SplitTenderGroupId with the next SplitTenderSequence.

PartialApprovalStrategy.description:
How the platform disposes of a partial approval: an authorization the issuer approved for less
than the requested amount, typically because the cardholder's available balance (or, for a
benefit card, the eligible balance) is lower than the sale.
x-enumDescriptions: Hold the partial authorization and wait for an operator to accept the approved amount or void it. The platform takes no action of its own until the operator answers, or until PartialApprovalAckTimeoutMinutes elapses.
Keep the approved amount without asking. The remainder is collected as a second tender when split tender is permitted, or left uncollected when it is not.
Void the partial authorization immediately and treat the sale as not completed. Use where a short payment is never acceptable and the cardholder should be asked for another card.

voidReason.description:
Optional short note recording why the reduced authorization was rejected, kept for the merchant
audit trail. A gateway-authored code or a brief operator note only: never processor response
text, and never anything card-derived.

PartialApprovalVoidInput.description: The body of a request to void a partial approval.
