paymentDetails.description: The payment details snapshot associated with this token.

type.description: The underlying payment type of the token.

category.description: The category of the token (e.g., internal, network).

merchantId.description: Id of the related Merchant.

tokenSharing.description: The sharing status of the token.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the token.

status.description: The status of the token (Active, Inactive, Invalidated).

invalidatedByTokenId.description: The ID of the token that replaced this one (if invalidated and regenerated).

replacesTokenId.description: The ID of the token that this token replaced (if this is a regenerated token).

regenerationReason.description: The reason for token regeneration (if applicable).

lastRegeneratedAt.description: The timestamp when this token was last regenerated.

publicReference.description:
The stable, opaque `pt_`-prefixed handle for this token: the only token identifier
permitted to leave the gateway, and the value to charge against on a merchant-initiated
transaction. Distinct from the internal id, which correlates to a card number and is never
treated as a merchant-facing handle.

numericToken.description: The numeric representation of the token.

cardFormatToken.description: The card format representation of the token.

transactionId.description: The unique identifier of the associated transaction when the token was created.

paymentDetails.description: The payment details snapshot associated with this token.

type.description: The underlying payment type of the token.

category.description: The category of the token (e.g., internal, network).

merchantId.description: Id of the related Merchant.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the token (e.g. "John's Visa").

isActive.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this entity is active.

status.description: The status of the token (Active, Inactive, Invalidated).

invalidatedByTokenId.description: The ID of the token that replaced this one (if invalidated and regenerated).

replacesTokenId.description: The ID of the token that this token replaced (if this is a regenerated token).

regenerationReason.description: The reason for token regeneration (if applicable).

lastRegeneratedAt.description: The timestamp when this token was last regenerated.

concurrencyStamp.description:
The concurrency stamp read from the token being updated. When supplied, the update is
rejected with a conflict if the stored token has since changed. Omit it to accept
last-write-wins.

PaymentType.description: Specifies the supported payment types used by the transactions processor.

paymentType.description:
The payment-type bucket, drawn from the same granular vocabulary the transaction dashboard
reports (for example `Visa`, `MasterCard`, `Amex`, `Debit`, `Ebt`,
`Check`, `Ach`, `ApplePay`, `Generic`). Buckets with no activity in the
window are omitted.

transactionCount.description:
Number of approved transactions contributing to this rollup, counting both the sale side and
the credit side. Declined and in-flight transactions are excluded.

grossAmount.description:
Sum of the approved sale-side amounts (authorization, sale, force, capture, capture-all and
repeat sale) for this payment type.

netAmount.description:
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Reports.PaymentTypeTransactionSummaryDto.GrossAmount less the approved credit-side amounts (returns and voids) for this
            payment type.

PaymentTypeTransactionSummaryDto.description: Per-payment-type rollup of the transactions in the requested window.

ecommerceIndicatorOverride.description:
Force the e-commerce indicator the charge message declares, replacing the value the handler
derives from the stored-credential classification. Drives `PTechCharge.ECI`.

forcePartialAuthorization.description:
Force `AllowPartialAuths=True` on an authorizing message regardless of the merchant's
profile toggle, so the cert script's partial-approval scenario can run against a profile that
has partial authorization switched off.

forceStoredCredential.description:
Treat the transaction as a credential-on-file leg even when the platform's classifier did not,
which emits `ECI=2` and the matching recurring submission marker.

forceCommercialCard.description:
Treat the card as commercial / purchasing even when the platform's BIN classification did not,
so the Level 2 addendum the cert script asks for can be produced. Drives
`PTechCharge.Level2Data` by way of `PaymentechLevel2Builder`.

sequenceNumberOverride.description:
Force the per-message sequence number instead of deriving it from the transaction key. Drives
`PTechCharge.SequenceNumber`.

settlementBatchNumberOverride.description:
Force the number the terminal-capture settlement batch is submitted under, instead of the one
the platform's atomic per-merchant sequence provider drew. Drives
`PTechManualSettle.BatchNumber`.

$processor.description: Type discriminator identifying these overrides as the paymentech shape. Must be sent as "paymentech".

PaymentechCertificationOverrides.description:
Chase Paymentech certification override knobs. Steer the NetConnect (Tampa) charge message at
auth time, and the terminal-capture batch at settle time, when the cert script needs a path the
production-shape request fields cannot otherwise reach.

PazeCertificateEnvironment.description: Paze environment a certificate belongs to. Sandbox self-signs; Production is CA-issued (CSR + merge).

PazeCertificateGenerateOutput.description: Result of a Paze "generate" call. WinkPG.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.PazeCertificateGenerateOutput.CsrPem is set only for the Production CSR flow.

PazeCertificateStatusOutput.description: Snapshot of a Paze certificate's lifecycle state, read live from Key Vault.

alg.description: Algorithm: `RS256` for the sig entry, `RSA-OAEP-256` for the enc entry.

kid.description: Key id Paze looks the entry up by.

x5c.description: Public certificate chain (base64 DER). Emitted only when a certificate is available.

PazeJwkDto.description: A single RSA public key as a JWK. `n`/`e` are base64url of the modulus/exponent.

keys.description: The key entries. One `sig` and one `enc`, both from the environment's single certificate.

PazeJwksDto.description: A JWK Set — the public keys Paze fetches to verify our OAuth assertion and encrypt payloads.

id.description: The announcement ID.

creationTime.description: When the announcement was created.

PendingPopupAnnouncementDto.description: Represents an announcement that requires a popup to be shown.

Period.description: Represents a period of time associated with a customer.

isDisposablePhone.description: A value indicating whether the phone number is associated with a disposable or temporary phone service.

isInBlacklist.description: A value indicating whether the phone number is in the blacklist database of the fraud screening service.

PhoneNumberEvaluation.description: Represents the evaluation results for a phone number in a fraud screening process.

deniedCode.description:
The AVS or CVV response code that matched the denylist (e.g. "N", "P", "S").
This is a processor result code, not the cardholder's CVV input value.

deniedCodeType.description:
Whether the triggering code was an AVS or CVV result.
Expected values: `"Avs"` or `"Cvv"`.

deniedCodeDescription.description:
The logical key emitted by `CardVerificationFilter` identifying which
rule fired (e.g. `"AVNoMatch"`, `"CVNoMatch"`, `"AVZipOnly"`).
This is a stable, grep-friendly machine identifier — NOT a user-facing
sentence. The merchant detail page renders this value verbatim alongside
the human-readable rule label. If a future iteration wants prose
description text, add a separate property rather than overloading this
field. Safe to display to merchants — does not reveal the cardholder's
actual input.

ruleSource.description:
Identifies which denylist configuration rule triggered the rejection
(e.g., "AvsDeclineCodes", "CvvDeclineCodes", or a merchant-specific rule name).

rejectedAt.description: UTC timestamp of the denylist evaluation that triggered this rejection.

reversalResultCode.description:
The result code from the reversal or void issued after the denylist match.
             if no reversal/void was attempted.

reversalResultMessage.description:
The result message from the reversal or void.
null if no reversal/void was attempted.

reversalAttemptedAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the reversal or void attempt.
null if no reversal/void was attempted.

requiresReversal.description:
Whether the orchestrator should schedule an auto-reversal for this policy
rejection. null (the default for historical gateway-side
rejections written before the field existed) is treated as "yes, reverse" —
the original behaviour. The native AVS/CVV decline path sets
false because the processor declined at auth time and never
placed a hold, so there is nothing to reverse and the
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PolicyRejectionData.ReversalResultCode / Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.PolicyRejectionData.ReversalAttemptedAt fields
stay null.

PolicyRejectionData.description:
Records the post-authorization denylist match that caused a transaction to be policy-rejected.
Stored on the transaction so the merchant audit trail shows the full sequence:
auth approved → denylist matched → reversal/void issued → PolicyRejected.

pricePlanId.description: The price plan the report is scoped to.

currentPlanName.description: The plan's current name (row-level names are run-time snapshots).

fromPeriodKey.description: Inclusive start of the effective period range (yyyyMM).

toPeriodKey.description: Inclusive end of the effective period range (yyyyMM).

rows.description: Report rows, sorted by merchant name then period.

PricePlanHistoryDto.description:
Plan-scoped historic billing report: every billing-run outcome where a merchant was
billed against the requested price plan, ordered by merchant then period.

PricePlanHistoryPaymentStatus.description:
Coarse paid/unpaid classification for the plan-scoped historic report, derived from
PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.MerchantBillingRunResultStatus. An invoice settled after the run keeps
showing PhoeniXGate.MerchantBilling.BillingRuns.PricePlanHistoryPaymentStatus.Pending until charge reconciliation updates the run result.
x-enumDescriptions: Not applicable — the merchant was not billed (skipped/unresolved).
Charge confirmed (recurring path reconciled).
Awaiting payment — invoice issued or charge dispatched but not reconciled.
Billing or charge failed for this merchant.

merchantId.description: The billed merchant.

merchantName.description: Merchant name snapshot at billing time.

planNameSnapshot.description: Price plan name snapshot at billing time.

totalFees.description: Total sell-side fees charged to the merchant for the period.

paymentStatus.description: Coarse payment status derived from the run-result status.

fulfillmentPath.description: How the charge was (or would be) collected.

billingRunId.description: The billing run this row came from (links to the run detail page).

invoiceId.description: Generated invoice, when the Invoicing path produced one.

PricePlanHistoryRowDto.description:
One merchant × billing-run outcome for the plan-scoped historic report. All display
fields are snapshots captured at run time (merchant name, plan name) so the report
reflects the plan as it existed when the run executed, not the current plan.

PricingModel.description: Defines how the unit price for a product is determined.
x-enumDescriptions: A single fixed price per unit.
Price varies by quantity tier (e.g., 1-10 = $5, 11-50 = $4).
Price determined by metered usage (e.g., per GB, per API call).
Custom pricing negotiated per deal or contract.

PricingSource.description: Indicates how the unit price on a line item was determined.
x-enumDescriptions: Price taken from the product catalog at time of invoicing.
Price manually overridden by the user.
Price determined by a promotion or coupon.
Price from a negotiated contract or quote.

duplicateCheck.description: Gets or sets the duplicate transaction detection settings.

orderDataDefaults.description: Gets or sets the default order data values applied to transactions when not explicitly provided.

cardVerification.description: Gets or sets the AVS and CVV card verification settings that control transaction approval behavior.

requireLevel2Data.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether card bins qualifying for level 2 processing are required
to supply level 2 data (manually or via order data defaults).

requireNameOnCard.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the cardholder name must be provided
with the transaction regardless of entry mode.

requireZipCode.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the billing zip code must be provided
with the transaction regardless of entry mode or AVS settings.

requireShipping.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the shipping amount must be provided with the transaction.

enableForceCapture.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether force capture transactions are allowed for this merchant.

requestProcessorToken.description:
Merchant preference for requesting a processor-issued reusable token at authorization
time, referenced elsewhere as `Processing.RequestProcessorToken`. Tri-state:
null (the default) means "auto", resolved ON wherever the routed
processor advertises processor tokenization; true / false
force the preference on or off. Surfaced on the merchant Processing tab as a tri-state
selector (Auto / Always request / Never request); carried on the DTO so the value
round-trips through the merchant create/update flow.

enableCreateIdempotency.description:
Opt-in for caller-facing create idempotency on the transaction-create surface, referenced
elsewhere as `Processing.EnableCreateIdempotency`. When true, a
caller-supplied `idempotencyKey` on a create is validated and claimed, so a retried
create returns the original transaction instead of charging again. false
means off. null means the merchant sets no value and inherits its reseller's
create-idempotency default; with no reseller default set, that resolves to off, as it always
has.

processorProfiles.description:
Gets or sets the collection of processor profiles configured for this merchant.
Each profile maps a payment processor and its supported payment types.

screeningProviderProfiles.description:
Gets or sets the external screening providers configured for this merchant. Each profile points
at a registered screening provider and carries that provider's per-merchant field values.
Conditional: When ScreeningProviderProfiles is set.

processorRoutingRuleSet.description:
Gets or sets this merchant's conditional processor routing rule set: an ordered, first-match
            list of rules that send a transaction to one of the merchant's own processor accounts based on
            deterministic attributes of that transaction.

autoSettlement.description: Gets or sets the auto-settlement configuration that controls automatic batch settlement behavior.

registers.description: Gets or sets the collection of registers (point-of-sale terminals) assigned to this merchant.

ProcessingSettingsDto.description:
Data transfer object containing all processing-related settings for a merchant,
including duplicate checks, card verification, level 2/3 data requirements, processor profiles,
auto-settlement configuration, and register assignments.

$processor.description: Type discriminator naming the processor these certification overrides target. Required whenever processorCertificationOverrides is supplied. Accepted values: "fiserv", "paymentech", "tsys". Values are lower-case and case-sensitive.

ProcessorCertificationOverrides.description: Per-processor certification override knobs. These are cert-only escape hatches for forcing network-request indicators that production traffic never needs. Examples include flipping a card-present transaction to card-not-present routing for a specific cert scenario, or supplying a hard-coded scheme transaction id for a Visa MIT cert flow.

processorId.description:
Identifier of the processor this schema describes. Submit this as the processor configuration's
`ProcessorId` in a merchant create/update request.

fields.description:
The fields applicable to the requested payment types, ordered by
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.Position.

schemaVersion.description: Opaque, deterministic content hash of this processor's full projected field schema. It is derived from the field definitions (not hand-maintained), so it changes whenever a field is added, removed, or edited, and is stable otherwise. It is per-processor (covers the whole field catalog), so it does not vary with the `paymentTypes` filter. Cache the schema keyed by this value to detect drift; it is also returned as the response `ETag`, and a request with a matching `If-None-Match` receives `304 Not Modified`.

ProcessorConfigSchemaDto.description:
The configuration schema for a single processor: the set of fields a client must populate to
build a valid processor profile for that processor. Returned by the config-schema discovery
endpoint and intended to be paired with a merchant create/update request.

isValid.description:
True when every applicable field passed validation (no PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorConfigValidationResultDto.Results entry has
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.Ok == false).

results.description:
One entry per field that was evaluated for the requested payment-type selection. Fields outside
the selection are not evaluated and are omitted.

ProcessorConfigValidationResultDto.description:
Result of a stateless dry-run validation of a processor configuration payload. Returned by the
validate-config endpoint with HTTP 200 whether or not the payload is valid — it is a per-field
report, not an error response. No merchant document is written.

key.description:
Stable identifier used to store and retrieve the field value. Submit this verbatim as the
`Key` of the processor field value in a merchant create/update request.

name.description:
Human-friendly label for the field. Supplying it on the corresponding field value is optional;
when omitted, the server fills it from this definition.

description.description: Longer description or help text for the field.

displayType.description: Hint for how a UI should render the field (text box, toggle, or dropdown).

fieldType.description: Underlying value type of the field (string, bool, int, datetime).

options.description:
For dropdown fields, the selectable options as explicit `{value, label}` pairs. Submit
the option's `Value` verbatim as the field value. When a field has no distinct backing
wire code, `Value` equals `Label`. Null for non-dropdown fields. This is the
preferred shape for closed-set fields.

dropdownList.description:
For dropdown fields, the labels presented to the operator. Aligned by index with
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.DropdownValues when backing values differ from the labels.

dropdownValues.description:
For dropdown fields, the backing values stored for each option. When null, the label from
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.DropdownList is also the stored value.

isRequired.description: Whether a value must be supplied for this field, effective for the requested payment-type selection. When the config-schema request is scoped to a set of payment types, the response contains exactly the fields applicable to that selection and PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.IsRequired reflects it — so the returned set with `IsRequired == true` is the required-field minimum for that selection. Fields outside the selection are omitted entirely (see PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.ApplicablePaymentTypes).

position.description: Relative ordering among fields. Fields are returned ordered by this value.

isSecret.description:
Whether the field holds a secret (credential) value. Secret values are encrypted at rest and
are never returned in plaintext; clients should treat secret fields as write-only.

validationRegex.description: Optional regular expression the submitted string value must match.

maxLength.description: Maximum character length for string values. Null means no limit.

validationMessage.description: Human-readable message shown when validation fails. When null, a generic message is generated.

applicablePaymentTypes.description: Payment type names this field applies to — the same tokens as PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorSummaryDto.SupportedPaymentTypes and PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.Name, so a client can correlate a field to a payment type with one consistent token (no side lookup). Null or empty means the field applies to every payment type. When a request scopes the schema to a subset of payment types, fields outside that subset are omitted from the response.

defaultValue.description: Optional default value pre-populated when creating a new processor profile.

ProcessorFieldDefinitionDto.description:
Describes a single configuration field that a processor requires when building a
merchant processor profile. Returned by the processor config-schema discovery endpoint
so API clients know which keys to populate, their types, and their validation rules.

value.description: The value to submit for the field when this option is selected. Submit this verbatim.

label.description: The human-friendly label to present for this option.

ProcessorFieldOptionDto.description:
A single selectable option for a closed-set (dropdown) field, as an explicit
`{value, label}` pair. This removes the ambiguity of the legacy parallel
`DropdownList` / `DropdownValues` arrays: a client submits PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto.Value
verbatim as the field value and shows PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto.Label to an operator.

key.description: The field definition key this result is for.

ok.description: True when the submitted value passed every constraint for this field.

message.description: Human-readable failure detail when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.Ok is false; null when the field passed.

ProcessorFieldValidationResultDto.description: The validation outcome for a single processor configuration field.

key.description: Unique field key used to match with the corresponding processor field definition. Required on input.

name.description:
Human-friendly label for UI display. Optional on input; when omitted, the server fills it from
the matching processor field definition.

rawJson.description:
Raw JSON value stored for the field (the JSON token serialized as a string). Optional on input
when PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorFieldValueDto.Value is supplied instead; the two are kept in sync.

value.description:
The field value as a JSON token. Preferred input form: send the value directly (string, number,
boolean, etc.) and it is round-tripped through PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorFieldValueDto.RawJson. A field with no value
reads as an empty object, and both that and an explicit null clear PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorFieldValueDto.RawJson on the
way back in, so a value read from the API can be written back unchanged.

ProcessorFieldValueDto.description:
A single processor-specific field value within a merchant's processor profile, both on input
(merchant create/update) and output (merchant read).

id.description: Global, environment-independent identifier of the payment type.

name.description:
Name of the payment type (e.g. "Visa", "Debit", "EbtSnap"). This is the value a client submits
when populating a profile's payment types; the server resolves PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.Id from it.

ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.description:
A reference to a payment type as an explicit `{id, name}` pair. This is the platform's
standard representation convention for entity references on the processor discovery surface
(closed-set dropdown options use the parallel PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorFieldOptionDto`{value, label}` shape).

processorProfileId.description:
The processor profile these capabilities describe. Correlates with
`processorProfileId` on the processor-profiles API.

processorId.description:
The stable processor key the profile is boarded on (for example `tsys` or
`fiserv`). Echoed exactly as stored on the profile, so it matches the value on the
processor-profiles API. Compare it case-insensitively: the platform resolves the key that way
and the stored casing is not normalized.

processorName.description:
The processor's display name as stored on the profile. Presentation only: never match on
this, always match on PhoeniXGate.Merchants.Processing.ProcessorProfileCapabilitiesDto.ProcessorId.

supportsZeroDollarVerification.description:
Whether this processor supports a zero-dollar account-verification authorization (authorize
$0 with an AVS/CVV check, then void immediately). This is what gates the hosted payment page's
"save my card, do not charge me" flow: when false, a save-card-only session
on this processor cannot complete without an amount.

supportsReversal.description: Whether the processor accepts a reversal of an authorization that has not settled.

reversalWindowSeconds.description:
The maximum age, in seconds, an authorization may have and still be reversible, or
null when the processor publishes no window.

supportsVoid.description: Whether the processor accepts a void of a transaction in the open batch.

supportsPartialRefund.description: Whether the processor accepts a refund for less than the original settled amount.

supportsPartialReversal.description:
Whether the processor accepts a reversal that releases only part of the authorization hold.
When false, only full-amount reversals are accepted.

supportedAdjustmentTypes.description:
The adjustment-shaped follow-up operations the processor advertises (offline adjustment,
            incremental authorization, both, or none).

ProcessorProfileCapabilitiesDto.description: The capabilities one of a merchant's boarded processor profiles can actually deliver.

outcome.description:
The outcome name: one of the `DatawireRegistrationOutcome` values
(`Registered`, `AlreadyProvisioned`, `Failed`, `ConfigurationError`,
`RegisteredNotPersisted`), or PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorProfileDatawireRegistrationDto.FaultedOutcome.

message.description:
A message written for the operator reading it, never a raw processor payload. Says what to do
next where there is something to do.

datawireId.description: The Datawire ID that was issued but could not be written onto the profile, and only that.

ProcessorProfileDatawireRegistrationDto.description:
What automatic Datawire registration did during the processor-profile write that returned the
profile carrying it. Present only on the sub-resource write responses, and only when registration
actually ran for that profile (a Fiserv profile saved with a blank Datawire ID).

openBatchIds.description:
Always empty under the open-batch-eligibility predicate (eligible transactions have
no `ProcessorBatchId` stamped). Retained for HTTP-client / generated-SDK
backward compatibility; will be removed in a future major.

ProcessorProfileDeactivationValidationDt.description: Result of processor profile deactivation validation.

merchantConcurrencyStamp.description: The merchant's concurrency stamp after the removal. Echo it back on the next write.

ProcessorProfileDeletionResultDto.description: The result of removing a single processor profile from a merchant.

processorProfileId.description: Gets or sets the unique identifier of this processor profile.

merchantId.description: Corresponding merchant id

paymentTypes.description: Payment types turned on for this profile.

isActive.description: Shows if the current profile is active or not.

enabledTenders.description:
Per-tender enable flags applied by the capability cascade at the
            processor-account layer. null indicates "all disabled" for legacy
            profiles that have never opted in to a non-credit tender.

merchantProcessorConfiguration.description: Corresponding configuration holding the details of the processor.

merchantConcurrencyStamp.description:
The merchant's concurrency stamp after the write that returned this profile, or
null on a read.

datawireRegistration.description:
What automatic Datawire registration did during the write that returned this profile, or
             when it did not run (any non-Fiserv profile, a Fiserv profile that
            already carries a Datawire ID, and every read).

ProcessorProfileDto.description:
Represents a payment processor profile assigned to a merchant, defining which processor
handles transactions and which payment types are supported.

processorKey.description:
The processor key (processor configuration id, e.g. "tsys", "cash"). Empty when the profile has
no configuration.

processorName.description:
Human-friendly processor name for display. Falls back to PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorProfileSummaryDto.ProcessorKey when the
profile carries no explicit name.

isActive.description: Whether the profile is active.

paymentTypes.description: Payment-type names enabled on the profile (e.g. "Credit", "Debit", "ACH").

displayFields.description:
Non-secret configuration fields safe to display, as label/value pairs. Only field definitions
whose `IsSecret` flag is false are included; secret fields are excluded server-side before
this DTO is built, so no secret value ever reaches the shape.

ProcessorProfileSummaryDto.description:
Read-only, non-secret summary of a merchant processor profile for display in a viewer (e.g. the
transaction-detail routing-decision panel's profile modal). Deliberately distinct from
PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorProfileDto: it is produced by a non-decrypting read
(M:PhoeniXGate.Merchants.IMerchantProcessorProfileAppService.GetProcessorProfileSummaryAsync(System.Guid,System.Guid)) and never
carries secret processor field values. Only field definitions marked non-secret are projected
into PhoeniXGate.Merchants.ProcessorProfileSummaryDto.DisplayFields; secret values are not read, not decrypted, and not present in
this shape at all.

name.description: Human-friendly field label.

category.description:
The field definition's UI grouping category (for example "Credit", "Debit", "EBT"). Projected
verbatim from the processor's field definition so a viewer can group fields whose labels are
only unique within a category. Null, blank, or the processor-default category all mean the
field belongs to the catch-all group.

position.description:
The field definition's relative position, used to order fields within their category. Lower
sorts first; ties keep the order the values were projected in.

ProcessorProfileSummaryFieldDto.description: A single non-secret label/value pair displayed in the processor profile summary.

result.description: Gets or sets the result code for the processing operation.

resultText.description: Gets or sets the textual result associated with this response detail.

approvalCode.description: Gets or sets the approval code associated with the processor response.

hostReferenceNum.description: Gets or sets the host reference number associated with the processor response detail.

hostDate.description: Gets or sets the host date associated with the processor response detail.

hostTime.description: Gets or sets the host time associated with the processor response detail.

avsResponse.description: Gets or sets the Address Verification Service (AVS) response code returned by the payment processor.

avsResponseText.description: Gets or sets the Address Verification Service (AVS) response text returned by the payment processor.

cvResponse.description: Gets or sets the CV response associated with this processor response detail.

cvResponseText.description: Gets or sets the response text associated with the processor response detail.

isCommercialCard.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the payment card is identified as a commercial card.

extendedErrorData.description: Gets or sets additional error data provided by the processor.

ProcessorResponseDetail.description: Represents detailed information about a processor's response, typically used for error reporting.

attestedBy.description: The id of the user who attested. Server-populated; any value supplied on input is ignored.

attestedAtUtc.description:
When the attestation was recorded, in UTC. Server-populated; any value supplied on input is
ignored.

note.description:
Optional free-text note, for example the entity or ownership evidence the attesting user
relied on.

ProcessorRoutingAttestationDto.description:
Records who confirmed that the processor profiles the rules target all belong to the same legal
entity as the merchant, and when.

name.description: Operator-facing label for this rule. Carries no matching semantics.

isActive.description: Whether this rule participates in evaluation. An inactive rule is skipped entirely.

cardBrands.description:
Card brands this rule matches, as canonical lowercase tokens ("visa", "mastercard", "amex",
"discover", "jcb", "diners", "unionpay", "interac"). Omit or send an empty list to match every
brand. Recognized spellings are normalized on save, so "Visa" is stored as "visa"; an
unrecognized brand is rejected.
Conditional: When CardBrands is set.

tenderTypes.description:
Card-rail tenders this rule matches. Omit or send an empty list to match every tender.

also submit a payment type by PhoeniXGate.Transactions.ProcessorProfile.ProcessorPaymentTypeRefDto.Name alone and let the

a processor's schema changed from a single listing call, without re-fetching every schema.

RateLimitAccumulationType.description: Determines what a rate limiter accumulates per window.
x-enumDescriptions: Counts discrete requests, checked against PermitLimit.
Accumulates a decimal amount (for example a transaction value), checked against MaxAmount. Only FixedWindow supports amount accumulation.

RateLimitAlgorithm.description: The algorithm used to enforce a rate limit.
x-enumDescriptions: Fixed (tumbling) window: the counter resets when the window rolls over. The window identifier is derived from the current UTC instant, so every process agrees on the boundary without coordination.
Sliding window: tracks individual request timestamps over a rolling span using a sorted set. More precise than a fixed window at the cost of more Redis memory.
Token bucket: permits replenish at a steady rate and short bursts are allowed up to the bucket capacity.
Concurrency limiter: bounds the number of concurrent in-flight requests. The slot is held for the duration of the downstream request and released afterwards.

RateLimitScope.description:
The scope at which a rate limiter operates. Determines the Redis key partitioning
and which identifier is extracted from the request context.
x-enumDescriptions: Platform-wide limit shared across all tenants and merchants.
Per-tenant limit. Keyed by the tenant identifier.
Per-merchant limit. Keyed by the merchant identifier.
Per-entity limit (for example a specific hosted payment page instance). Keyed by the entity identifier supplied by an IRateLimitEntityConfigProvider.
Per-endpoint limit. Keyed by the matched EndpointPattern rather than the raw request path, so a pattern containing a wildcard produces one bounded counter key instead of one key per distinct URL.
Per-API-key limit. Keyed by the API key identifier (never the key secret).
Per-IP-address limit. Keyed by the resolved client IP address.

x-enumDescriptions: Receipt generated after a successful authorization.
Receipt generated after a capture/settlement.
Receipt generated after a full refund.
Receipt generated after a partial refund. Multiple partial refund receipts may exist on a single transaction, each with a distinct sequence number.
Receipt generated after a void.

Receipt generated after a full reversal — the entire approved amount has been released back to the issuer. Distinguished from PartialReversal so the transaction-detail / explorer pages can show the lifecycle event clearly.
Receipt generated on-demand from the UI (legacy/fallback for pre-module transactions).
Receipt generated after a partial reversal. Multiple partial reversal receipts may exist on a single transaction (one per reversal operation), each with a distinct sequence number.

x-enumDescriptions: Not a refund, or kind has not been classified. Default for all non-refund transactions.

A refund run as a follow-up action against a previously approved and settled original transaction. The refund is a new transaction in its own right and flows through the normal auth + settlement pipeline, but carries a reference to its parent via OriginalTransaction and debits the parent's refund capacity.

SettlementBatchStatus.description: Status of a settlement batch through its lifecycle.
x-enumDescriptions: Batch created, awaiting processor submission.
Batch successfully settled with the processor.
Batch settlement failed.
Some transactions settled, others rejected by the processor.

No transactions were eligible to settle for this (merchant, processor) group. A successful no-op outcome, distinct from Failed (a genuine fault) and from Completed (a real settle). Recorded so a settlement run leaves a history row for every targeted (merchant, processor) even when zero transactions are loaded. The short explanation is carried in SettlementBatch.ErrorMessage as the per-batch outcome detail.

The batch could not be settled automatically and is parked for operator action . Distinct from Failed: a Failed closed batch is re-attempted on the next run (transient fault), whereas an OperatorActionRequired batch is deliberately excluded from automatic retry because blindly re-submitting it would just re-fail. Two causes park a batch here: a non-transient duplicate-batch-number processor rejection (the same processor BatchNumber will keep colliding until an operator bumps it), and exhaustion of SettlementConsts.MaxSettlementRetries transient retries. The batch's transactions are moved to SettlementStatus.SettlementOnHold so they stop auto-retrying; the reason is carried in SettlementBatch.ErrorMessage. The operator UI (follow-up story) lists these and can retry with a bumped processor BatchNumber.

The batch was not submitted because a concurrent settlement run already held the terminal lock for the same (Fiserv MerchID, TermID) pair (UMF Appendix M 42.1: only one batch at a time per terminal). Distinct from Failed: nothing went wrong, this run simply deferred to the run that already owned the terminal. The next scheduled run retries normally.

runDateUtc.description:
When the settlement run that produced this batch was kicked off (`SettlementBatch.RunDate`).
This is the batch's "Run Date" display value, not its completion time.

completedAtUtc.description:
When the batch first reached a terminal outcome (`SettlementBatch.CompletedAtUtc`).
Null for legacy batches created before the field existed, or a batch still in flight.

duration.description:
The settlement-attempt duration: PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.CompletedAtUtc minus the batch's audit
creation time, computed server-side via `SettlementDurationCalculator` (clamped at zero).
Null when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.CompletedAtUtc is null. Derived from per-batch set-once timestamps so
it is immune to later batch mutations (re-settle, park, backfill, override).

settledCount.description:
Number of items that successfully settled. Equals PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchSummaryDto.TotalTransactionCount
for fully successful batches; less for PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchStatus.PartiallyCompleted.
Null for legacy batches and batches still PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementBatchStatus.Pending.

processorKey.description:
The lower-cased processor key the batch was produced for (the same key the settlement
close fans out on). Needed by the operator retry action to target the re-settle engine
entrypoint at the correct (merchant, processor) counter. Null for legacy batches created
before the key was persisted. Non-sensitive: a short identifier such as `tsys`.

gatewayBatchId.description:
The gateway batch id this run settled (`SettlementBatch.OpenBatchId`). Identifies the
single batch the operator retry resubmits. Null for legacy batches created before the id
was persisted. Non-sensitive: an internal batch identifier, never PAN/card data.

succeeded.description: True when the override was applied and persisted.

previousStatus.description: The status the transaction held immediately before the override (or null when it could not be loaded).

newStatus.description: The status the transaction holds after the override (null when the override did not apply).

skipReason.description:
Stable diagnostic code populated when PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementOverrideAttemptResult.Succeeded is false. Values are
drawn from PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementOverrideSkipReasons.

SettlementOverrideAttemptResult.description:
Per-transaction outcome of a M:PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.ITransactionSettlementOverrideAppService.OverrideAsync(PhoeniXGate.Transactions.Settlement.SettlementOverrideRequestDto)
call. The service returns one entry per requested transaction id so a (single or bulk)
caller can render success / partial-success / failure states deterministically.

transactionIds.description: The transactions to apply the override to. 1–200 ids per request.

newStatus.description: The settlement status to switch to. Must be admin-targetable.

SettlementOverrideRequestDto.description:
Request payload for an admin-driven manual settlement-status override. Designed
from day one to carry one or many transaction ids so the same service can serve
the single-transaction detail-page modal and a future grid bulk-action.

SettlementStatus.description: Settlement status for transactions requiring processor settlement
x-enumDescriptions: Transaction is waiting to be settled with the processor
Settlement completed successfully with the processor
Settlement failed - requires review and retry (rollback)
Transaction is not eligible for settlement (voided, reversed, or not yet captured)
Settlement is currently in progress with the processor.
Settlement is on hold and cannot proceed at the moment.
Settlement was rolled back or reversed after a completed attempt. Distinct from SettlementFailed which indicates a transient failure needing retry.

A reversal was attempted but the processor did not confirm that the authorization hold was voided — the contributor saw a non-Ok result code (transport failure, timeout, swallowed exception, malformed response, etc.). Distinct from NotEligible (a confirmed reversal/void) and SettlementFailed (a settlement-time failure). Operations need to confirm the hold state with the processor and reverse manually if required. The transaction's Stage is left at the pre-reversal value; the close-stage history entry is NOT written.

previousStatus.description: The settlement status the transaction held before this override was applied.

newStatus.description: The settlement status the operator selected.

reason.description: Free-text justification supplied by the operator. Required, trimmed, 5-500 chars.

operatorUserId.description: The user id of the operator who applied the override.

operatorUserName.description:
The display name of the operator at the time of the override (snapshot — does not
follow rename of the underlying user account).

overriddenAt.description: UTC timestamp the override was applied.

SettlementStatusOverrideRecord.description:
A single audit record for an admin-driven manual override of a transaction's
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.SettlementStatus. Records are appended to
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.OverrideHistory by the
`Transaction.OverrideSettlementStatus` domain method and rendered on the
transaction detail page so subsequent admins can see who changed the settlement
state, when, why, and from what value.


All value-type properties are nullable so existing Cosmos documents that gain
an Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.OverrideHistory entry from an older code
path (or are deserialised by a future shape-mismatched build) do not fail
deserialisation. New records are always written with all fields populated; UI
and audit code should treat null fields on a persisted record as a corrupt
document and surface accordingly rather than papering over it.

SetupFieldDisplayType.description: Specifies the display type used to render a setup field in a user interface.

SetupFieldType.description: Represents the supported field types used in setup and configuration models.

isAddressShipForward.description: A value indicating whether the shipping address is identified as a known ship-forward address.

isBillingCountryMatch.description: A value indicating whether the country of the shipping address matches the country of the billing address.

isBillingStateMatch.description: A value indicating whether the state/region of the shipping address matches the state/region of the billing address.

isBillingCityMatch.description: A value indicating whether the city of the shipping address matches the city of the billing address.

isBillingPostcodeMatch.description: A value indicating whether the postcode/ZIP code of the shipping address matches the postcode/ZIP code of the billing address.

isExportControlledCountry.description: A value indicating whether the shipping address is in a country subject to export controls.

isInBlacklist.description: A value indicating whether the shipping address is in the blacklist database of the fraud screening service.

ShippingAddressEvaluation.description: Represents the evaluation results for a shipping address in a fraud screening process.

SignatureData.description: Represents signature data for a transaction.

SignatureTypes.description: Represents the various types of signatures used in transactions.
x-enumDescriptions: Represents the first signature type.
Represents the second signature type.
Represents the third signature type.
Represents the fourth signature type.
Represents the legacy Hypercom signature type.
Represents the enhanced Hypercom signature type.
Represents the first receipt signature type.

SkuAggregationType.description: Defines how usage quantities are aggregated for a SKU.
x-enumDescriptions: Counts discrete events (transactions, API calls).
Sums monetary amounts (dollar values).
Sums time durations (seconds, milliseconds).
Sums data volumes (bytes transferred/stored).

description.description: Description of what this SKU measures.

defaultIncludedQuantity.description: Default included quantity when no explicit entitlement exists.

supportsHardLimit.description: Whether this SKU supports hard-limit enforcement.

requiresInlineAggregation.description: Whether aggregates are updated inline during consumption.

parentSkuCode.description: Optional parent SKU code for composite/rollup metering.

supportedDimensions.description: Dimension keys supported by this SKU.

SkuDefinitionDto.description: DTO for a SKU definition from the in-memory registry.

id.description: Unique identifier of the entitlement.

skuCode.description: The SKU code this entitlement applies to.

scope.description: The scope level of this entitlement.

resellerId.description: Reseller ID. Set for Reseller and Merchant scope.

merchantId.description: Merchant ID. Set for Merchant scope only.

hardLimitEnabled.description: Whether this SKU enforces a hard limit.

overageAllowed.description: Whether overage beyond the included quantity is allowed.

overageLimitQuantity.description: Cap on overage quantity. Null means unlimited overage.

enabled.description: Kill switch — when false, all consumption of this SKU is blocked.

resetPeriod.description: How often the usage counter resets.

concurrencyStamp.description: Optimistic concurrency stamp.

SkuEntitlementDto.description: Read DTO for a SKU entitlement.

displayName.description: Display name from the SKU definition.

totalQuantity.description: Total quantity consumed in this period.

totalAmount.description: Sum of dollar values in this period (for percentage billing).

amountCurrency.description: ISO currency code for the amount.

entryCount.description: Number of ledger entries in this period.

includedQuantity.description: Included quantity from the effective entitlement.

isUnlimited.description:
True when the effective entitlement has no enforceable upper bound. The UI
should render "Unlimited" instead of WinkPG.Usage.Dtos.Reporting.SkuUsageSummaryDto.IncludedQuantity and hide
progress meters. Set by the server when `HardLimitEnabled == false` or
when `IncludedQuantity == long.MaxValue` (the platform-default sentinel
from `PlatformDefaultEntitlementsSeedContributor`).

hardLimitEnabled.description: Whether a hard limit is enforced.

remaining.description: Remaining quantity, or null if unlimited.

inOverage.description: Whether the current usage exceeds the included quantity.

percentageUsed.description:
Percentage of included quantity consumed (0.0 to 1.0+).
Greater than 1.0 indicates overage.

SkuUsageSummaryDto.description: Per-SKU usage summary enriched with entitlement data for reporting.

SmsConsentCaptureMethod.description:
How a consent or opt-out record came to be. Part of the proof-of-consent evidence retained per the
Twilio Messaging Policy record-keeping requirement, and useful for triage when a recipient disputes
having opted in or out.
x-enumDescriptions: Capture method was not supplied. Treated as the least-authoritative evidence.
Recipient opted in through a public web form (e.g. a hosted checkout consent checkbox).
An operator captured consent while taking the payment in the Virtual Terminal.
Consent was captured on a Hosted Payment Page flow.
The record was created from a bulk import of prior consent evidence.
Consent or opt-out was recorded through the API by an integrating system.
An administrator recorded the consent or opt-out manually.

Opt-out was back-filled from a carrier send-time signal (Twilio error 21610 on send). The platform learned of the revocation from the carrier rather than capturing it directly. Inbound STOP / START replies use InboundKeyword instead, which keeps a more precise evidence trail.

Consent transition was captured from an inbound SMS keyword the recipient texted to the platform number (STOP / UNSUBSCRIBE / START / etc.), received on the Twilio inbound webhook. The inbound message SID is retained as the evidence reference.

phoneNumber.description: The E.164-normalized number the check was resolved against. Empty when the input could not be normalized.

merchantId.description: Merchant scope the check was evaluated in.

hasRecord.description: `true` when a consent record exists for this number in scope.

status.description: The record's current status, or null when no record exists.

isOptedOut.description: `true` when the recipient has opted out — the SMS channel should be disabled.

canSendSms.description: `true` when a send is currently allowed by the consent store. This is the inverse of PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsConsentCheckResultDto.IsOptedOut: no record and opted-in both allow. (Whether express consent is required before the first send is a caller policy decision, not enforced here.)

SmsConsentCheckResultDto.description:
Result of a send-time pre-check: whether SMS may be sent to a phone number for a merchant scope.
A send UI uses this to disable the SMS channel for an opted-out recipient before the operator sends
(e.g. the invoice pay-link send dialog).

phoneNumber.description: Canonical E.164 phone number this record governs.

merchantId.description: Merchant the record is scoped to.

status.description: Current consent state.

captureMethod.description: How the most recent transition's evidence was captured.

statusChangedAt.description: When the current status was last set (UTC).

evidenceText.description: Proof-of-consent evidence for the current status.

evidenceReference.description: Stable reference for the current status's source.

history.description: Append-only audit trail of every status transition, oldest first.

SmsConsentDto.description: Read-only DTO for a merchant-scoped SMS consent / opt-out record, including its audit history.

status.description: The status this transition moved the record to.

captureMethod.description: How this transition's evidence was captured.

evidenceReference.description: Stable reference tying this transition to its source.

SmsConsentHistoryEntryDto.description: Read-only DTO for one entry in a PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsConsentDto's audit trail.

SmsConsentStatus.description: Consent / opt-out state of a phone number for a single (tenant, merchant) scope.
x-enumDescriptions: The recipient has expressly consented to receive SMS from this merchant. Sends are allowed.
The recipient has revoked consent (STOP keyword, carrier unsubscribe, or an operator action). The send-time gate blocks every SMS to this number for this merchant until a re-opt-in is recorded.

SmsDeliveryStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a single outbound SMS, as recorded on its `SmsEvents` row. The first three
values are gateway-side outcomes stamped by the platform at send time; the rest arrive later on
Twilio status callbacks.
x-enumDescriptions: No state recorded. Only ever seen on a malformed document.

The send-time compliance gate refused the message (for example the recipient has opted out). No Twilio API call was made, so no carrier callback will ever follow. Distinct from GatewaySendFailed so a compliance block is auditable separately from a carrier fault.
The Twilio API rejected the create-message call. The message never entered the carrier network.
Twilio accepted the message. Carrier callbacks (if a status callback URL was set) follow.
Carrier callback: the message is queued, accepted, scheduled, or sending.
Carrier callback: the message has been handed to the carrier.
Carrier callback: the carrier confirmed delivery to the handset.
Carrier callback: the carrier could not deliver the message. Usually carries a Twilio error code.
Carrier callback: the message failed outright or was cancelled. Usually carries a Twilio error code.

SmsInboundKeyword.description:
Classification of an inbound SMS the platform received on its Twilio number. Drives whether an
inbound message records a consent transition (opt-out / opt-in), returns a branded informational
reply (help), or is simply persisted for operator review (none).
x-enumDescriptions: Not a recognized keyword. The message is persisted for operator review; no consent change.
An opt-out keyword (STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, OPTOUT, CANCEL, END, REVOKE, QUIT).
An opt-in / re-subscribe keyword (START, UNSTOP, YES).
The HELP keyword: the recipient asked for program identification and a support contact.

correlationId.description:
The platform correlation id for this message. Equal to Volo.Abp.Application.Dtos.EntityDto`1.Id: there is
exactly one row per outbound message, so the correlation id is the document key. Surfaced under
its own name because that is what callers of the send API hold.

toPhoneNumberMasked.description: Recipient reduced to its last four digits (for example `•••••••4567`).

fromPhoneNumberMasked.description: Sending number reduced to its last four digits, when the send used a from-number.

messagingServiceSid.description: The Messaging Service SID the send routed through, when one was configured.

messageSid.description: Twilio's message SID, once the API accepted the message. Null for blocked / failed sends.

status.description: Where the message currently sits in its lifecycle.

isFailure.description: Whether PhoeniXGate.Twilio.SmsLog.SmsLogDto.Status means the message did not reach the handset.

twilioErrorCode.description: Twilio numeric error code from the failing send or callback, when one was reported.

failureCode.description: Platform error code explaining a gateway-side refusal (for example a compliance block).

bodyLength.description: Message length in characters. The body itself is never stored or returned.

lastStatusAt.description: When the most recent carrier callback was applied (UTC). Null until the first one lands.

tenantId.description: Tenant the message was sent under.

merchantId.description: Merchant the message belongs to.

SmsLogDto.description: Read-only projection of one outbound SMS delivery-log row.

SmsMessageCategory.description:
Compliance category of an outbound SMS. Carried on `SmsMessage.Properties` (see
PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsMessageProperties) so the send-time gate and the content / quiet-hours policy
(PhoeniXGate.Twilio.Sms.SmsContentPolicy) can distinguish message classes.
x-enumDescriptions: Transactional message tied to a specific interaction the recipient initiated or expects (payment link, receipt, invoice, one-time passcode). This is the platform's default when a caller sets no category: every SMS sender wired today is transactional.

Promotional / marketing message. Requires express marketing consent and is subject to the stricter content and timing policy. Callers sending marketing SMS must set this explicitly; it is never inferred.

Recurring reminder in an ongoing program the recipient enrolled in (an overdue-invoice reminder series, a scheduled payment nudge). Not marketing, but recurring, so CTIA requires the opt-out instruction to ride on the message itself and TCPA timing applies.

SoftDescriptor.description: Represents a soft descriptor for a transaction, containing alternative merchant information.

SpecialCondition.description:
Visa/Mastercard "special condition" tag for transactions that need network-specific
handling beyond standard purchase semantics. Maps to TSYS `SpecialConditionIndicator`
(and the equivalent indicators on other processor networks).
x-enumDescriptions: No special condition applies — standard purchase semantics.

Quasi-cash purchase: a transaction that resembles cash equivalent (money orders, foreign currency, traveler's cheques, gaming chips, casino vouchers, etc.). Triggers TSYS SpecialConditionIndicator=8 and requires a populated CardholderId on the network request.

Quasi-MOTO: a card-present capture that the merchant is required to process under MOTO routing rules (e.g. cert scenarios, specific Visa product types). Distinct from QuasiCash — the merchant remains in retail context but presence flags flip to MOTO for network routing.

splitTenderGroupId.description: Identifier shared by every tender in the group.

sequence.description: 1-based position of the transaction this context was assembled for.

role.description:
Whether the transaction this context was assembled for is the group's primary tender or a
            continuation.

totalRequestedAmount.description:
The order total the group is collecting toward, in major currency units: the amount
originally requested on the primary tender.

totalApprovedAmount.description:
Sum of the approved amounts across every non-voided tender in the group, in major currency
units.

remainingAmount.description:
What is still owed, in major currency units: PhoeniXGate.Transactions.SplitTenderContextDto.TotalRequestedAmount minus
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.SplitTenderContextDto.TotalApprovedAmount. Zero once the group has collected the full order total.

tenderCount.description:
Number of tenders currently in the group, including voided ones (they remain part of the
audit trail).

SplitTenderContextDto.description:
The split-tender membership of a single transaction, plus the running balance the group has
collected so far. Lets a caller render "tender 2 of 3, $40.00 still owed" without fetching and
summing every member of the group itself.

SplitTenderRole.description:
Identifies a transaction's position within a split-tender group: the set of transactions that
together collect one order total after a partial approval left a shortfall.
x-enumDescriptions: The first tender in the group: the transaction whose partial approval created the shortfall. Exactly one member of a group holds this role, and it always carries SplitTenderSequence = 1.

A follow-up tender collecting part of the remaining balance. A group may hold several, ordered by SplitTenderSequence (2, 3, ...). A continuation can itself be partially approved, which starts the disposition cycle again.

eventType.description: Canonical event type to build the sample for.

StageSampleEventInput.description: Request to stage the catalog's sample for one event type into a live session.

StoredCredentialUsage.description:
Flags describing the permitted uses of a stored payment credential. Captured at consent time
and checked when a subsequent merchant-initiated transaction is submitted against the credential.
A consent's `AllowedUsages` must include the MIT reason's corresponding usage before the
MIT can proceed.
x-enumDescriptions: No permitted uses. Consent record is effectively inactive.
Scheduled recurring charges (subscriptions, membership dues). Maps to Recurring.
Fixed-schedule installment plans dividing a known total. Maps to Installment.

Merchant-triggered charges for pre-agreed events (balance top-ups, usage overages, no-show fees, delayed charges). Maps to several MIT reason codes including UnscheduledCOF, NoShow, DelayedCharge, and IncrementalAuth.
A single known future cardholder-initiated purchase the credential was saved for (e.g. "save card for my next order"). Not used for MITs.

tokenReference.description: The network token (DPAN) reference value. Encrypted at rest; never logged.

tokenRequestorId.description: The token-requestor identifier the network token was provisioned under.

tokenStatus.description: The token's lifecycle status as last known to the gateway.

expiryMonth.description: The network token's expiry month (1–12), when provided by the token service.

expiryYear.description: The network token's expiry year, when provided by the token service.

createdAt.description: When the network token was provisioned and stored.

StoredNetworkToken.description: A network-issued token (DPAN) stored on a payment method.

StoredPaymentMethodOrigin.description:
The surface / add-channel a Phoenix.SharedModels.Customer.CustomerStoredPaymentMethod was captured through.
Stamped once when the method is first stored and not changed afterward.
x-enumDescriptions: The add-channel was not recorded. Assigned to methods that predate this field (materialized from a null value) and to any path that did not classify its origin.

Added by an operator through a Customer admin surface that mints the stored method on the customer document directly (the customer edit form's payment-methods dialog, and the create-customer / create-contract-from-transaction dialogs). Note: the contract add-payment dialog submits through the HTTP add endpoint and is therefore recorded as Api, since origin on that boundary is server-authoritative and cannot be caller-supplied.
Vaulted from a hosted payment page — either tokenize-on-payment or the direct ACH vault flow.
Vaulted from a Virtual Terminal save-on-payment.

Added through the HTTP add-stored-payment-method endpoint. Covers external API token registration and any in-process operator surface that submits through that same gated endpoint (e.g. the contract add-payment dialog): origin on this boundary is stamped server-side and is never caller-supplied.

processorName.description:
The processor type key the token was minted under (for example `"tsys"`).
Part of the token's selection key.

processorProfileId.description:
The processor profile (acquirer credential set) the token was minted under. Part of
the token's selection key; a token is only replayed against the same profile.

token.description: The processor-issued token value. Encrypted at rest; never logged.

tokenStatus.description: The token's lifecycle status as last known to the gateway.

tokenRequestorId.description: The token-requestor identifier associated with the token, when the processor supplies one.

createdAt.description: When the token was first captured and stored.

lastUsedAt.description: When the token was last replayed at the rail. null until first reuse.

StoredProcessorToken.description:
A processor-issued reusable token (e.g. a TSYS `RequestToken`) captured at
authorization time and stored on a payment method alongside the encrypted PAN.
Repeat / merchant-initiated sales prefer a matching stored token at the rail and fall
back to the PAN when none exists.

StoredTokenStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a token (processor token or network token) stored on a payment
method. Shared by Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.Token.StoredProcessorToken and Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.Token.StoredNetworkToken.
x-enumDescriptions: The token is active and may be replayed at the rail.
The token is present but should not currently be used (for example the processor reported it inactive). Retained so it can be reactivated rather than re-minted.
The token has been invalidated or replaced and cannot be used.

SubscriptionScope.description:
Defines the organizational scope at which a notification subscription operates.
Determines which events the subscription can match against based on the
reseller/merchant hierarchy.
x-enumDescriptions: Subscription scoped to a specific merchant. Only matches events originating from that merchant.
Subscription scoped to a reseller and all its descendants (sub-resellers and merchants). Uses ResellerPathPrefix for efficient hierarchy matching.
Subscription with tenant-wide scope. Matches events across all resellers and merchants within the tenant. Requires admin-level permissions.

summaryFilters.description:
Dictionary mapping summary keys (e.g., "succeeded", "failed") to their filter definitions.
Null values mean "no additional filter" (count all matching the base filter).

baseFilter.description: Optional filter from other active layers (tabs, chips) that is AND-merged with each summary filter before counting.

SummaryCountsRequest.description:
HTTP request body for the summary counts endpoint.
Wraps the two parameters of `GetSummaryCountsAsync` into a single [FromBody] model.

SurchargeChannelFlags.description:
The payment channels a merchant's surcharge configuration applies to. A bit flag so a merchant can
enable surcharging on any combination of channels. Stored on the configuration as
`ChannelRestrictions`; a channel is surchargeable only when its bit is set.
x-enumDescriptions: No channels enabled.
Merchant-operated virtual terminal.
Direct API integrations.
Hosted payment pages.
Recurring / scheduled billing.

creationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was created.

creatorId.description: The ID of the user who created this entity.

lastModificationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was last modified.

lastModifierId.description: The ID of the user who last modified this entity.

isDeleted.description: Indicates whether this entity has been deleted.

deleterId.description: The ID of the user who deleted this entity, if it is deleted.

deletionTime.description: The date and time when this entity was deleted, if it is deleted.

merchantId.description: The merchant this configuration belongs to (partition key).

tenantId.description: Owning tenant (null in the host tenant).

isEnabled.description: Whether surcharging is currently enabled for the merchant.

status.description: Persisted lifecycle status of the configuration.

waitingPeriodExpiresAt.description:
The instant surcharging becomes permitted, i.e. when the mandatory notice waiting period
elapses. Surcharging is blocked until this is in the past.

noticeFiledAt.description: When the most recent notice was recorded in WinkPG.

noticeFiledBy.description: The user who filed the most recent notice.

noticeAttestedDate.description:
The calendar date the merchant attested they filed the most recent notice with the card
networks, when that predates WinkPG.Surcharging.SurchargeConfigurationDto.NoticeFiledAt. Null when the notice was filed as of
the record date, and on every notice recorded before this fact existed.

defaultRate.description: Default surcharge rate (decimal fraction) when no network override applies.

processorAccountId.description: The processor account under which the current notice / waiting period was established.

disclosureCopyTemplate.description:
The merchant's own surcharge disclosure copy in the WinkPG.Surcharging.SurchargeDisclosureCopy token
grammar, or null when the platform default copy applies.

attestedCostOfAcceptanceRate.description: The merchant's attested effective cost of acceptance (decimal fraction), a hard ceiling.

costOfAcceptanceAttestedAt.description: When the cost-of-acceptance rate was attested.

costOfAcceptanceAttestedBy.description: The user who attested the cost-of-acceptance rate.

differentialNetworkRatesAttested.description:
Whether differing surcharge rates across the allowed card networks have been attested as
carrying documented legal signoff. Required before such a rate set can be saved.

differentialNetworkRatesAttestedAt.description: When the differential-rate signoff was attested.

differentialNetworkRatesAttestedBy.description: The user who attested the differential-rate signoff.

forceEnabledAt.description:
When surcharging was activated through the non-production waiting-period bypass, if it ever
was. Null on every configuration activated the normal way, so a non-null value is the signal
that this merchant's notice waiting period was not actually served.

forceEnabledBy.description: The user who activated surcharging through the non-production bypass.

concurrencyStamp.description: Optimistic-concurrency token; supply the value read here when updating.

SurchargeConfigurationDto.description:
Full read model for a merchant's surcharge configuration: lifecycle status, rate, channel and
network policy, notice / waiting-period state, and the cost-of-acceptance attestation. Rates are
decimal fractions (0.03 = 3%). Carries WinkPG.Surcharging.SurchargeConfigurationDto.ConcurrencyStamp so a client can round-trip
it into WinkPG.Surcharging.UpdateSurchargeConfigurationDto for optimistic concurrency.

SurchargeConfigurationStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a merchant's surcharge configuration. Persisted on the aggregate (not merely
computed) so the waiting-period sweep can query `Status == WaitingPeriod` in Cosmos.
Transitions are owned by `SurchargeConfigurationManager`.
x-enumDescriptions: No surcharging has been set up for the merchant.
Configuration exists but the required card-brand notice has not been filed.
Notice filed; the mandatory waiting period is still running.
Surcharging is live.
Surcharging was turned off after having been configured.

platformRulesEnforced.description:
Whether the platform-seeded ruleset is currently enforced underneath merchant policies. When
`false`, every row's merged outcome comes from the merchant layer alone and the platform
columns are informational.

resolvedAtUtc.description:
The instant the platform rules were resolved against, so a row's effective-dated rule is
reproducible. UTC, as everything the API returns is.

configurationExists.description:
Whether the merchant has a persisted surcharge configuration. When `false` there is nothing
for a state policy to attach to, so the write path would fail; the view still resolves and shows
the platform layer.

policies.description: One row per constrained state, ordered by state code. States neither layer restricts are omitted.

SurchargeEffectiveStatePoliciesDto.description:
The effective state-policy view for one merchant: every state that either layer says something
about, each carrying the platform rule, the merchant override, and the merged outcome. Read-only.

stateCode.description: Two-letter US state or territory code, uppercase.

hasMerchantOverride.description:
Whether the merchant has an entry of their own for this state. Reported separately from
WinkPG.Surcharging.SurchargeEffectiveStatePolicyDto.MerchantRestrictionType because that property is nullable on the persisted policy
too (every value type on a Cosmos document is), so a null restriction cannot distinguish "no
entry" from "an entry that never recorded one".

merchantRestrictionType.description:
The merchant's configured restriction for this state, or null when the merchant has no
            entry for it (in which case the platform layer alone governs). Check
             to tell that apart from an entry with no restriction recorded.

merchantCapRate.description: The merchant's configured cap for this state (decimal fraction), if any.

platformRestrictionType.description:
The platform-seeded restriction governing this state on the evaluation date, or null when
            the platform seeds no rule for it.

The presentment channel the quote is for. Defaults to , the

SurchargeQuoteRequestDto.description:
Request for the authenticated, merchant-scoped surcharge-eligibility quote endpoint
(WinkPG.Surcharging.Eligibility.ISurchargeQuoteAppService). A direct API integrator supplies a BIN prefix (never a
full PAN), the transaction amount, the cardholder state, and the presentment channel; the platform

ineligibilityReason.description:

statement), matching what the Virtual Terminal and Hosted Payment Page show the same cardholder.

SurchargeStateRestrictionType.description:
How a US state restricts credit-card surcharging. Paired with an optional per-state cap
(`CapRate` on `SurchargeStatePolicy`) because the restriction category alone
cannot express a numeric ceiling such as Colorado's 2% cap or the cost-of-acceptance cap states.

The merchant's own SurchargeStatePolicy entry produced the outcome. Merchant policy can only tighten a platform rule, never relax one.

Your own identifier for this create request, used to make a retry safe. Send the same value
again and the gateway returns the transaction the first request produced instead of charging a
second time. This is the recommended pattern for reconciling a create whose response you never
received.

receiptIds.description:
List of receipt IDs generated for this transaction. Used for point-read access to receipts.
Stored as strings: see Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.Transaction.ReceiptIds remarks for rationale.
Read-only: set by the server; ignored on the AutoMapper write maps.

decisionNotes.description:
System-emitted decision explanations recorded against this transaction, surfaced
read-only on the transaction-detail view. Like PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.ReceiptIds, this is server state:
it is populated on load for display but ignored on the create/update write maps, so a client
can never persist decision notes.

initiationType.description: Identifies whether this transaction was initiated by the cardholder (CIT) or the merchant (MIT).

mitReason.description: For merchant-initiated transactions, the reason code justifying the MIT. Null for CITs.

storedCredentialConsentId.description:
Reference to the `StoredCredentialConsent` that authorizes this MIT. Null for CITs.
Optional, and best omitted: when it is absent the server resolves the consent from the stored
credential itself (resolved from the token plus `InvoiceData.CustomerId`) and selects the
most recently captured one that permits the declared MIT reason. Send a value only to pin a
specific consent when the credential carries several, for example after a re-enrollment, and
only when the value is a consent identifier this platform issued for that same credential
(from a capture response, a consent lookup, or a webhook). A supplied value is validated
strictly and is rejected if it belongs to a different credential, has been revoked, or does
not permit the declared reason. Note that a credential whose consent lineage predates this
platform's consent tracking has no consent record at all: an identifier minted by a prior
system is never valid here, so such a charge is rejected with
`stored_credential_consent_required` whether or not this field is sent. Remediate by
having the merchant attest the credential, which mints a new platform consent; the charge then
succeeds with the field omitted, and the newly issued identifier is accepted when sent.

The card network's trace ID for this transaction chain. Captured from the processor response

Running total of refund amounts applied to this transaction.
Read-only: computed from refund operations.

Running total of reversal amounts applied to this transaction.

The immutable amount the issuer authorised at the close of the Authorization stage.
