saveCardRequested.description:
Operator (VT) or cardholder (HPP) opt-in to save the card for future merchant-initiated
use. Flows from the UI into the create request; the server-side
`CardTokenizationFinalizeContributor` reads this flag at the Finalize stage to
decide whether to mint a stored payment method against the customer document.
Auth-time-only — the AutoMapper Update map and the recurring-billing map both ignore
it so it cannot be set on subsequent operations.

isAccountVerification.description:
When true, this transaction is a zero-dollar account verification
rather than a charge: the gateway authorizes for $0 to confirm card validity (with
AVS/CVV) and immediately voids the authorization. Used by the Hosted Payment Page
"save card only — don't charge me" flow to vault a card without charging it. Mutually
exclusive with a non-zero amount. Auth-time-only — the AutoMapper Update and
recurring-billing maps both ignore it so it cannot be set on subsequent operations.
null (the default) is an ordinary chargeable transaction.

convenienceFeeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt.description: UTC timestamp of the moment the payer accepted the disclosed convenience fee (the confirm-click, NOT the submit). This is the caller's attestation that the fee was disclosed and agreed to, and it is required on any request charging a non-zero `invoiceData.amounts.convenience` on a card tender, alongside PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.ConvenienceFeeDisclosureChannel. The Virtual Terminal stamps it from its confirm modal (the CSR attesting as the cardholder's proxy) and the Hosted Payment Page from the cardholder's own acceptance; a direct API integration owns its own disclosure UX and supplies the same attestation. It may not sit more than a few minutes ahead of the gateway's clock: a disclosure cannot have been accepted after the request that reports it. Auth-time-only: the AutoMapper Update and recurring-billing maps both ignore it, so it cannot be set on subsequent operations. null when no fee was charged. An ACH / e-check debit is out of scope; a convenience fee on an EBT / eWIC tender is prohibited outright and rejected before this field is examined.

convenienceFeeDisclosureChannel.description:
The surface on which the convenience-fee disclosure was shown and accepted. One of
`"VirtualTerminal"`, `"HostedPaymentPage"`, or `"Api"` (a direct integration's
own checkout); matched case-insensitively, and any other value is rejected. Paired with
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.ConvenienceFeeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt and required on the same requests.
Auth-time-only.

convenienceFeeEligibilitySnapshot.description:
Serialized convenience-fee eligibility decision (reason code + assessed amount) captured
at disclosure-acknowledgment time. Codes / amounts only: no request- or response-derived
free text (PCI). Gateway-produced and optional: the Virtual Terminal and Hosted Payment Page
serialize their own fee decision into it, and a direct API integration has no equivalent
internal decision to record, so it is never required. Auth-time-only.

convenienceFeeCancelledAmount.description:
The convenience-fee amount the Virtual Terminal operator declined on the disclosure-confirm
modal, removing it from this submission. Set by the VT cancel path (button, X, or Esc) so the
authorization pipeline can record a `CsrCancelledVtModal` convenience-fee decision note
carrying the amount that was waived: the fee is gone from the amounts by submit time, so the
evaluator has nothing left to explain without this marker.


Audit-only. It never adds to any total, never reaches the processor, and is honoured only when
the submitted transaction carries no convenience fee, originates from the Virtual Terminal, and
belongs to a merchant with an active convenience-fee configuration. Auth-time-only: the
AutoMapper Update and recurring-billing maps both ignore it. null (the
default) on every submission where no disclosed fee was cancelled.

surchargeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt.description:
UTC timestamp captured at the surcharge disclosure confirm-click moment (NOT at submit). Set
by the Virtual Terminal confirm modal / HPP acceptance when a surcharge is disclosed and
agreed. Auth-time-only — the AutoMapper Update and recurring-billing maps both ignore it so
it cannot be set on subsequent operations. null when no surcharge
disclosure was acknowledged.

surchargeDisclosureChannel.description:
Channel on which the surcharge disclosure was acknowledged (`"VirtualTerminal"`,
`"HostedPaymentPage"`, or `"Api"`). Paired with
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.SurchargeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt. Auth-time-only.

achWebAuthorizationText.description:
The NACHA WEB single-debit authorization language shown to the payer, captured verbatim at
ACH submit on the Hosted Payment Page. The consent evidence NACHA requires to substantiate an
internet-initiated (WEB) ACH debit. Auth-time-only — the AutoMapper Update and
recurring-billing maps both ignore it so it cannot be set on subsequent operations.
null for non-ACH tenders. PCI-safe: authorization language only.

achWebAuthorizationConsumerIp.description:
Consumer IP recorded at ACH WEB authorization time (required NACHA evidence). On the anonymous
HPP create path the server derives this from the request context for direct API callers and
does not trust a client-supplied value except the coordinator-captured IP the Blazor surfaces
pass server-side. Auth-time-only. null for non-ACH tenders.

achWebAuthorizationAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the ACH WEB authorization. Server-stamped on create; a client-supplied value
is never trusted. Auth-time-only. null for non-ACH tenders.

achWebAuthorizationSecCode.description:
SEC code the ACH WEB authorization was captured under (always `"WEB"` for HPP ACH).
Auth-time-only. null for non-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationAttested.description: Operator attestation signal for a Virtual Terminal CSR-keyed ACH debit: `true` when the operator confirmed they obtained the account holder's authorization (TEL or PPD) for the debit. This is a transient input only — the server consumes it to gate the submit (fail-closed when a VT ACH debit is not attested) and to stamp the persisted `AchAuthorization*` evidence fields; it is never persisted on its own. null / `false` for non-VT-ACH tenders and for callers that do not attest.

achAuthorizationStatementText.description:
The CSR attestation statement captured for a Virtual Terminal CSR-keyed ACH debit (NACHA TEL /
PPD). Server-owned: rendered from the selected SEC code and stamped at create time, never
trusted from the client. Auth-time-only — the AutoMapper Update and recurring-billing maps both
ignore it so it cannot be set on subsequent operations. null for non-VT-ACH
tenders. PCI-safe: authorization language only.

achAuthorizationStatementVersion.description:
Stable version hash (`sha256:{hex}`) of PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.AchAuthorizationStatementText.
Server-recomputed from the statement text; a client-supplied value is never trusted.
Auth-time-only.

achAuthorizationSecCode.description:
SEC code the VT ACH authorization was captured under (`"TEL"` or `"PPD"`).
Server-owned from the operator's selection on `CheckData.SecCode`. Auth-time-only.
null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationChannel.description:
Channel on which the VT ACH authorization was attested (`"VirtualTerminal"`). Server-owned.
Auth-time-only. null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the VT ACH authorization. Server-stamped on create; a client-supplied value is
never trusted. Auth-time-only. null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

TransactionCreateDto.description: Represents the data required to create a new transaction.

category.description: The subsystem that made the decision.

outcome.description: The decision's effect on the transaction.

createdAt.description: UTC timestamp the note was recorded.

code.description:
The discriminated reason within the Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNote.Category (e.g. `"SuppressedChannel"`).
Owned by the consuming subsystem; resolved to copy with Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNote.Category at render time.

amountDelta.description:
Signed amount impact where meaningful (e.g. the waived/assessed fee). Currency is implied by
the transaction. Null when not applicable.

occurredOnStage.description: Optional pipeline stage the decision occurred on, for ordering/diagnostics.

TransactionDecisionNote.description:
A single, system-emitted explanation of a decision made about a transaction.
Stored append-only in the top-level `Transaction.DecisionNotes` collection.

TransactionDecisionNoteCategory.description:
The subsystem that produced a Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNote. Seeded with
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNoteCategory.ConvenienceFee; designed to grow (Surcharge, Tax, Avs, Cvv, Fraud, Tip, …) as
other subsystems start recording decision explanations, with no new transaction fields.
x-enumDescriptions: The convenience-fee evaluator (first consumer).

The surcharge eligibility pipeline. Records why a surcharge was not applied to a transaction on an enabled merchant (e.g. debit/prepaid card, restricted state, unsupported network), so the veto reason is queryable/displayable rather than buried in the /SurchargeResult snapshot (single-fee / debit-rejection story #3212). The Code is a SurchargeIneligibilityReason value name.

The manual fraud-review hold. Records that a transaction was parked for human disposition and how that hold ended, so the timeline explains a gap between screening and authorization rather than leaving an operator to infer it from /FraudReviewData. The Code is one of ReviewHeld, ReviewApproved, ReviewDeclined, or ReviewExpired.

TransactionDecisionNoteOutcome.description:
The effect a decision had on the transaction. Drives the verb shown to the operator and lets
the display group/filter without parsing the per-category Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNote.Code.
x-enumDescriptions: The thing was applied (e.g. a fee was assessed).
The thing was deliberately not applied (e.g. a fee was waived/suppressed).
The thing was applied at a modified value (e.g. a capped/percentage amount).
The transaction was blocked by the decision.
Purely informational; no effect on amounts or flow.

TransactionDecisionNoteSeverity.description:
Display severity for a Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionDecisionNote. Drives styling on the
transaction-detail view; carries no business meaning.
x-enumDescriptions: Neutral/informational styling.
Attention styling (e.g. an expected fee that did not apply).

creationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was created.

creatorId.description: The ID of the user who created this entity.

lastModificationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was last modified.

lastModifierId.description: The ID of the user who last modified this entity.

isDeleted.description: Indicates whether this entity has been deleted.

deleterId.description: The ID of the user who deleted this entity, if it is deleted.

deletionTime.description: The date and time when this entity was deleted, if it is deleted.

cardBrand.description: The card brand (e.g., "VISA", "MASTERCARD") resolved from BIN data.

lodging.description:
Lodging detail for a stay-related transaction, echoed back as it was submitted. Null on every
            transaction outside a lodging industry.

duplicateCheck.description:
The duplicate-check intent the submitting request carried, echoed back as it was
submitted. Null means the request expressed no opinion and the merchant's screening
configuration decided, which is the value a request that omitted the field carries.
False means the request asked to waive the check, and it was waived only if the merchant
permits per-transaction overrides. Transactions written before this field became nullable
read as false regardless of what the caller intended.

receiptIds.description:
List of receipt IDs generated for this transaction. Used for point-read access to receipts.
Stored as strings for Cosmos DB compatibility.

refundTransactionIds.description:
IDs of the linked-refund child transactions issued against this transaction (as the parent
sale). Drives the detail-page reverse relationship ("Refunded by <guid>" and the
Related Transactions grid). Empty/null when this transaction has no linked refunds. Stored
as strings for Cosmos DB compatibility (see `Transaction.RefundTransactionIds`).

decisionNotes.description:
System-emitted decision explanations recorded against this transaction,
e.g. why the convenience-fee evaluator applied or suppressed a fee. Read-only on the wire:
written only by server-side contributors, never by an update. Rendered on the transaction
detail view via the decision-note copy resolver.

linkedFeeChargeTransactionId.description:
On a primary charge: the id of the separate convenience-fee charge linked to it (the
reverse link, primary → fee), when a card-brand program required the fee to settle as its own
authorization. Null when there is no linked fee charge. Server-state; read-only on the wire.
See `Transaction.LinkedFeeChargeTransactionId`.

primaryChargeTransactionId.description:
On a convenience-fee charge: the id of the primary charge this fee is linked to (the forward
link, fee → primary). Null for an ordinary transaction. Server-state; read-only on the wire.
See `Transaction.PrimaryChargeTransactionId`.

processorProfileId.description: The unique identifier of the merchant processor profile that processed this transaction.

processorKey.description: The processor type key (e.g., "tsys", "fiserv") used for this transaction.

routingResult.description:
The persisted routing decision produced by the processor-routing pipeline: the selected
            processor + profile, the ordered contributor audit trail, and every evaluated candidate with
            its score and eliminated flag. Server-owned (mapped entity -> DTO by convention; never accepted
            on a create/update). Back-office only: it is stripped for public API-key callers (see
            TransactionCrudAppService) and denylisted from outbound webhook payloads, since contributor
            names and scoring internals are operational detail.  for legacy rows and
            flows that never route.

loopbackSimulation.description:
What the sandbox simulator did on this transaction: the published triggers your request fired,
            and the response values it filled in from a default because nothing matched. Read it when a
            sandbox answer is not the one you expected and you want to know which trigger the sandbox saw.
            Each entry carries isDefault, which separates a trigger you sent from a value the
            sandbox supplied. A card-verification entry reports the response code the sandbox returned and
            never the security code you submitted.
            
            Server-owned: it is never accepted on a create or update, and nothing in it changes what the
            transaction did.  on every transaction the sandbox simulator did not
            answer, which includes every transaction a live processor handled, and on every row written
            before the trace existed.

surchargeResult.description:
The surcharge evaluation decision produced by the surcharge eligibility pipeline: the verdict,
            applied rate, cap provenance, and the per-stage audit trail. Server-owned (mapped entity -> DTO
            by convention; never accepted on a create/update). Back-office only: stripped for public
            API-key callers and anonymous callers, mirroring .
             when the surcharge decision was never evaluated (no active surcharge
            configuration, non-card tender, or a legacy row).

correlationId.description: The correlation ID linking this transaction to its orchestration audit trail.

cumulativeRefundedAmount.description: Running total of refund amounts applied to this transaction.

cumulativeReversedAmount.description: Running total of reversal amounts applied to this transaction.

authorizedAmount.description:
The immutable amount the issuer authorised at the close of the Authorization stage.
UI should read this — not PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionDto.ResponseData.`Amounts.Approved` — when
computing remaining-reversible / remaining-refundable balances, because the
processor's reversal-response payload overwrites `/ResponseData` in place.
Null on legacy rows that pre-date.

policyRejection.description:
Audit record of the post-authorization denylist match that policy-rejected this
            transaction. Top-level — not nested under  — because the
            auto-reversal flow Sets /ResponseData wholesale, so anything stored there
            is clobbered. Null for any transaction that was not policy-rejected.

partialApprovalData.description:
Durable record of a partial approval (the issuer authorized less than was requested) and
            the disposition decided for it. Read this — not
            .IsPartialApproval — anywhere outside the synchronous
            create response: the response flag is erased by the reversal that every non-accepted
            disposition issues, whereas this object is top-level and survives. Its mere presence means
            "this transaction was partially approved". Null when the issuer approved in full.

fraudReviewData.description:
Durable hold state when this transaction was parked for manual fraud review: when the hold
            started, when it expires, what triggered it, and the disposition that was reached. Top-level
            rather than nested under the screening results, which are rewritten wholesale on every
            screening retry. Server-owned and read-only on the API surface. Null when the transaction was
            never held for review.

splitTenderGroupId.description:
Groups this transaction with the other tenders that together collect one order total after
a partial approval left a shortfall. Server-owned; read-only on the API surface. Null when
the transaction is not part of a split tender.

splitTenderSequence.description:
1-based position within the PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionDto.SplitTenderGroupId group, so the tenders can be
presented in the order they were taken. Null when the transaction is not part of a split
tender.

splitTenderRole.description:
Whether this transaction is the primary tender of its split-tender group or a continuation
            collecting part of the remaining balance. Null when the transaction is not part of a split
            tender.

initiationType.description:
Identifies whether this transaction was initiated by the cardholder (CIT) or the merchant (MIT).
            Null on legacy transactions.

mitReason.description: For MIT transactions, the reason code justifying the merchant-initiated charge.

storedCredentialConsentId.description: Reference to the stored credential consent authorizing this MIT.

schemeTransactionId.description: The card network's trace ID linking this transaction to its original CIT.

description.description:
The merchant-supplied free-text payment description recorded on this transaction, echoed
back exactly as it was submitted. null when the create request carried
none, in which case the processor received the gateway's own reference instead.

tender.description:
The tender the create request explicitly declared, echoed back as it was submitted.
             when the request declared nothing, which includes every card, check,
            and token transaction and any cash transaction submitted without the declaration.

cardholderPresence.description:
How present the cardholder is at the point of sale, separate from the physical entry mode.
            Drives network-level presence indicators at auth time.

processorCertificationOverrides.description:
Per-processor certification override knobs. Non-null only for cert-tooling traffic.
            Production traffic always sees this as .

refundKind.description:
Classifies a refund transaction as linked (follow-up against a previously approved
            original transaction) or unlinked (standalone).  for
            non-refund transactions.

pendingRefundAmount.description:
Reserved-but-not-yet-completed refund amount for this transaction (as a parent),
tracked separately from PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionDto.CumulativeRefundedAmount so UI can show
"refund pending settlement" vs "refund completed". null means zero.

saveCardRequested.description:
Operator (VT) or cardholder (HPP) opt-in to save the card for future merchant-initiated
use, captured at create time. Read-only on the API surface — the consumer cannot mutate
it through Update calls (server-side AutoMapper ignores the field on the Update map).

tokenizedPaymentMethodId.description:
The `CustomerStoredPaymentMethod.Id` minted by the TM Functions
`CardTokenizationFinalizeContributor` at Finalize stage when a CIT was approved
with PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionDto.SaveCardRequested = true. VT and HPP post-CIT
consent-capture flows read this to land a `StoredCredentialConsent` against the
real payment-method id. null on transactions that did not request
save-card, were declined, or where tokenization failed.

isAccountVerification.description:
When true, this transaction is a zero-dollar account verification (the HPP
"save card only" flow) rather than a charge — the card was authorized for $0 to confirm it,
vaulted with consent, and not charged. Read-only on the API surface; create-time-only (the
Update map ignores it). null on ordinary chargeable transactions.

convenienceFeeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt.description:
UTC timestamp when the convenience-fee disclosure was accepted (CSR-as-proxy in the Virtual
Terminal, cardholder on the Hosted Payment Page, or the integrator's own checkout on a direct
API create), captured at confirm-click time. Echoed back as submitted: this is the caller's
attestation, set on create and never editable afterwards (the Update map ignores it).
null when no non-zero convenience fee was charged. See
`TransactionCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.ConvenienceFeeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt` for when it is
required.

convenienceFeeDisclosureChannel.description:
The surface on which the convenience-fee disclosure was shown and accepted:
`"VirtualTerminal"`, `"HostedPaymentPage"`, or `"Api"`. Set on create and never
editable afterwards.

convenienceFeeEligibilitySnapshot.description:
Serialized convenience-fee eligibility decision (reason code + assessed amount) captured
at disclosure-acknowledgment time. Codes / amounts only. Produced by the Virtual Terminal and
Hosted Payment Page; optional on a direct API create. Set on create and never editable
afterwards.

convenienceFeeCancelledAmount.description:
The convenience-fee amount the Virtual Terminal operator declined on the disclosure-confirm
modal, removing it from the submission. Audit-only: it was never charged, and the matching
`CsrCancelledVtModal` convenience-fee decision note carries the same amount. Read-only on
the API surface. null when no disclosed fee was cancelled.

surchargeRate.description:
The surcharge rate actually applied to this transaction. Indexed top-level mirror of
PhoeniXGate.Transactions.TransactionDto.SurchargeResult.AppliedRate (which is on the Cosmos indexing exclusion list).
null when no surcharge was assessed.

surchargeDisclosureAcknowledgedAt.description:
UTC timestamp when the surcharge disclosure was acknowledged, captured at confirm-click time.
Read-only on the API surface. null when no surcharge was disclosed.

surchargeDisclosureChannel.description:
Channel on which the surcharge disclosure was acknowledged
(`"VirtualTerminal"` / `"HostedPaymentPage"` / `"Api"`). Read-only on the API surface.

surchargeReversedAmount.description:
The portion of the assessed surcharge amount reversed by a subsequent void or refund.
Read-only on the API surface. null when nothing has been reversed.

achWebAuthorizationText.description:
NACHA WEB single-debit authorization language shown to the payer, captured verbatim at ACH
submit. Read-only on the API surface; delivered on the ACH completion webhook. PCI-safe.
null for non-ACH tenders.

achWebAuthorizationConsumerIp.description:
Consumer IP recorded at ACH WEB authorization time (required NACHA evidence). Read-only.
null for non-ACH tenders.

achWebAuthorizationAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the ACH WEB authorization (server-stamped). Read-only.
null for non-ACH tenders.

achWebAuthorizationSecCode.description:
SEC code the ACH WEB authorization was captured under (always `"WEB"`). Read-only.
null for non-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationStatementText.description:
CSR attestation statement captured for a Virtual Terminal CSR-keyed ACH debit (NACHA TEL / PPD).
Read-only on the API surface; delivered on the ACH completion webhook. PCI-safe.
null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationSecCode.description:
SEC code the VT ACH authorization was captured under (`"TEL"` or `"PPD"`). Read-only.
null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationChannel.description:
Channel on which the VT ACH authorization was attested (`"VirtualTerminal"`). Read-only.
null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

achAuthorizationAt.description:
UTC timestamp of the VT ACH authorization (server-stamped). Read-only.
null for non-VT-ACH tenders.

idempotencyStatus.description:
What create idempotency did to the request that produced this response: whether a
            idempotencyKey was sent, whether deduplication was in effect for the merchant, and
            whether this response replays an earlier create.

creatorId.description: The ID of the user who created this entity.

creationTime.description: The date and time when this entity was created.

lifecycleStatus.description:
The merchant-facing lifecycle status this entry was published under, or
null when the entry carries none.

linkedReceiptId.description: The ID of the receipt generated for this timeline entry, if any.

linkedReceiptType.description: The type of the linked receipt.

linkedReceiptSequenceNumber.description: The sequence number of the linked receipt within the transaction.

success.description: Whether the operation was successfully submitted to the orchestrator.

transactionId.description: The original transaction ID the operation was performed on.

operationType.description: The operation type that was executed.

errorCode.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling.

timedOut.description:
True when the operation was submitted to the orchestrator but completion
timed out. The operation may still be processing — the user should check the transaction status.

newTransactionId.description:
The ID of a newly created transaction, set when the operation creates a new transaction
(e.g., Repeat). Null for operations that modify the existing transaction in-place.

TransactionOperationResultDto.description: Result of a transaction operation execution.

TransactionOperationType.description: Specifies the type of operation performed on a transaction.
x-enumDescriptions: Finalizes a previously-approved authorization by sending an online capture / clearing message to the processor. Moves the transaction from "funds held" to "marked for the next batch close" — settlement still happens later when the merchant's batch cuts. Valid only against approved, uncaptured TransactionType.Authorization transactions; the action matrix removes Capture once the transaction is settled (Refund is the post-settlement undo). Partial captures (less than the authorized amount) are supported and release the unused portion of the issuer hold per network rules.

Returns funds to the cardholder by spawning a new standalone TransactionType.Return transaction linked back to the parent via OriginalTransaction.TransactionId. The new transaction flows through the normal auth + settlement pipeline rather than mutating the parent in place. Used once the parent has settled (post-batch-close), at which point Reversal and Void are no longer applicable. Refund capacity is reserved against the parent's PendingRefundAmount with optimistic concurrency so concurrent partial refunds from different callers cannot collectively exceed the parent's available balance.

Offline ledger-only cancel: marks the transaction for exclusion from the next batch close without sending any processor message. Used pre-settlement. Acts as the fallback when the configured processor does not support online Reversal (or the reversal window has expired). The action evaluator's mutual-exclusion step drops Void from the candidate set when Reversal is also eligible — Reversal is a strict superset of Void on the same stage. Terminal once approved.

Online undo: sends a processor message (0420-equivalent on card networks) that releases the issuer hold on a captured-but-not-cleared transaction and pulls the transaction from the next clearing. Distinct from Void in that an actual rails-level message is exchanged with the processor; the processor can decline. Eligible post-auth and pre-settlement against Authorization, Sale, RepeatSale, and captured Authorization stages. Per-processor support is advertised via ProcessorCapabilities.SupportsReversal and gated by ReversalWindowSeconds; the gateway falls back to Void when the processor opts out. Partial reversals (strictly less than the remaining authorized balance) are supported when the processor also advertises SupportsPartialReversal; a partial reversal leaves the transaction non-terminal until cumulative reversed equals the authorized ceiling. Once settlement has cleared, Reversal is no longer valid and Refund is the only available undo.

Re-runs a previously-approved transaction with the same payment data by spawning a new transaction linked back to the parent via OriginalTransaction.TransactionId. Authorizations repeat as Authorization (re-hold funds); Sale and RepeatSale both repeat as RepeatSale. Used for recurring billing, card-on-file scenarios, and operator-initiated re-charges. The caller may supply a different amount than the original; the new transaction flows through the normal auth + settlement pipeline. Available against approved transactions in any settlement state — once an authorization has settled, Repeat is the only re-charge path (Capture is no longer eligible).

Re-attempts a previously declined or failed transaction with the same TransactionType and the same amount as the original — changing either would violate retry semantics. Spawns a new transaction linked back to the parent via OriginalTransaction.TransactionId. Available only when the parent ended in a non-approved result code (decline, processing error, gateway failure). Distinct from Repeat, which preserves type-mapping rules (Sale → RepeatSale) and allows a caller-specified amount; Retry is intended to recover from a transient failure on the original attempt without altering its commercial intent.

An offline adjustment to a previously-authorized transaction's settlement record: tip (gratuity), tax, level-3 data, PO number, or AVS fields. Modifies the settlement amount/data before batch close without contacting the processor network. Tip and other amount-bearing fields are constrained to industry types that allow post-auth adjustments (restaurant, retail, e-commerce). Online amount changes (incremental authorization) belong to IncrementalAuthorization.

An online incremental (or "estimated → final") authorization on top of a previously authorized — but uncaptured — transaction. The processor sends a fresh auth message to the brand network; on approve, the transaction's Total_Auth_Amt is bumped and a new auth response (with its own customer-facing receipt) replaces the prior one. Distinct from OfflineAdjustment in that an actual rails round-trip is performed and the issuer can decline. Valid only against TransactionType.Authorization transactions that have not yet been captured. Per-processor support is advertised via ProcessorCapabilities.SupportedAdjustmentTypes; the gateway rejects the operation up front when the configured processor lacks the capability.

Acknowledges a partial approval by keeping the reduced authorization as-is. The issuer approved less than the gateway asked for, and the operator (or the cardholder) has decided the lesser amount is acceptable, so no reversal is issued and the transaction proceeds through the normal capture / settlement path for the approved amount. Valid only while the transaction is parked at TransactionStage.SplitTenderPending with PartialApprovalData.Disposition still Pending; a late acknowledgment against a disposition the deadline sweep has already resolved is expected traffic and is rejected. Its counterpart is Void, which rejects the reduced amount instead.

Acknowledges a partial approval by keeping the reduced authorization and collecting the shortfall on a second tender. The continuation transaction carries the same SplitTenderGroupId with the next SplitTenderSequence. Valid only while the transaction is parked at TransactionStage.SplitTenderPending, and only when the merchant permits split tender and the group has not reached VirtualTerminalSettings.SplitTenderMaxTenders.

id.description: The unique identifier for the transaction register.

name.description: The name of the transaction register.

TransactionRegister.description: Represents a transaction register in the system.

cardValidationData.description: The card validation data associated with the transaction.

resultCode.description: The result code of the transaction. Defaults to ResultCode.Undefined.

resultMessage.description:
The result message of the transaction. For successful (Ok) transactions this is normalized
against a case-insensitive allow-list of canonical approved messages ("Approved", "Card OK",
"Partial Approval"); when the trimmed processor text matches the allow-list its original
casing is preserved, otherwise the message is rewritten to "Approved" so the UI/transaction
explorer does not surface processor-specific AVS/CVV chatter (e.g. TSYS host text like
"NO MATCH") as if it were a transaction-level outcome. For non-Ok results the trimmed
processor text passes through verbatim so decline/error reasons remain actionable.
The processor's original message — leading/trailing whitespace trimmed but otherwise
untouched — is preserved on Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.OriginalProcessorMessage for audit/diagnostics.

originalProcessorMessage.description:
The processor's result text as returned by the processor handler, prior to approved-message
normalization. Trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace but otherwise unmodified — preserves
processor context (e.g. "APPROVED - {host text}", "NO MATCH") that Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.ResultMessage
may have collapsed to a generic "Approved" for UI consumption. Null when the processor
supplied no text or only whitespace.

debitTraceNumber.description: The debit trace number for the transaction.

resultDetail.description: Gets or sets additional details about the transaction result.

authorizationCode.description: The authorization code for the transaction.

responseDate.description: The date and time when the response was received.

authorizingNetworkId.description: The ID of the authorizing network.

authorizingNetworkName.description: The name of the authorizing network.

routingIndicator.description: The routing indicator for the transaction.

customerSignatureRecommended.description: Value indicating whether a customer signature is recommended.

processorResponseDetail.description: Gets or sets detailed response information from the processor.

associationResponseCode.description: The association response code for the transaction.

responseCategoryCode.description: The response category code for the transaction.

cardIndicator.description: The card indicator for the transaction.

detailedProductId.description: The detailed product ID associated with the transaction.

clientIpAddress.description: The client's IP address for the transaction.

amounts.description: The response amounts for the transaction.

settlementXmlData.description:
Carrier for settlement XML from processor responses.
Populated by `EPSProcess.ProcessData`, then converted to JSON, encrypted,
and written to Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.SettlementDataJson by the
authorization contributor. The contributor replaces the raw XML with a masked
sentinel (`"****"`) before the `/ResponseData` patch reaches Cosmos,
so the stored value indicates that settlement data was received and processed
without exposing the original content.

processorTraceNumber.description: Retrieval reference number / trace number from processor.

cardLevelResults.description: Card level results (A/B/C for Visa/MC card levels).

returnedAci.description:
The Returned ACI (Authorization Characteristics Indicator) the network echoed back on the
authorization response, stored as the raw single-character code. It reports how the
transaction actually qualified (for CPS and related programs), which can differ from the ACI
the gateway requested. Meanings are processor-specific, so the friendly description is
resolved at display time from the transaction's processor key via
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.ReturnedAciCatalog rather than persisted here. Null when the processor returned
no ACI (blank / space-filled) and on every non-card flow. Non-sensitive protocol metadata.

additionalProcessorData.description:
Additional processor-specific response data, keyed by merchant-facing display label.
Populated by the per-processor detail-extraction registry
(`ProcessorDetailExtractionExecutor`) from the processor's settlement/detail
aggregate at authorization time.


Every key is governed by the registry's PCI allowlist (`ProcessorDetailPciPolicy`),
which is what makes this dictionary safe on all three surfaces it reaches: the
merchant-facing transaction DTO, outbound webhook projection, and the transaction
history `DetailsJson` copy of the `/ResponseData` patch. Card number, track,
EMV, CVV, and expiration can never land here. Size is capped by
`ProcessorDetailBudget` because the history copy duplicates this value per entry.


Not queryable: `/ResponseData/AdditionalProcessorData/*` is index-excluded. A
field that needs server-side filtering or reporting must be promoted to a typed
property instead.

eci.description:
Electronic Commerce Indicator returned by the network, canonicalized by the
processor's detail adapter (upper-cased, whitespace-trimmed, leading zeros
preserved: `05` and `5` are distinct ECI values). Promoted to a typed
property because it is network-defined, normalizable across processors, and used for
interchange-qualification reporting. null when the processor
returned none.

entryDataSource.description:
Entry data source indicator describing how the card data reached the terminal
(keyed, swiped, contactless, stored credential), canonicalized by the processor's
detail adapter. Promoted because entry mode is semantically common across processors
and drives downgrade/qualification analysis. null when the
processor returned none.

requestedAci.description: Authorization Characteristics Indicator the gateway requested: the interchange qualification level sought for this authorization. A value differing from Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.ReturnedAci means the transaction downgraded to a costlier interchange tier, which is why the requested side is promoted to a typed, queryable property rather than left in Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.AdditionalProcessorData (dictionary values can never be queried server-side). Extracted from the processor's settlement/detail aggregate. null when the processor returned none.

achTraceNumber.description:
NACHA-format ACH trace number echoed back by the ACH processor (15 characters:
8-digit Originating Depository Financial Institution identifier + 7-digit
sequence). Stable for the logical transaction lifecycle — capture, refund,
reversal, and return responses repeat the trace assigned at authorization
so downstream consumers can correlate the lifecycle to a single ACH entry.
Null on card flows.

nachaReturnCode.description:
NACHA return code (e.g. `R01`, `R02`, `R10`) when the ACH
transaction was returned by the receiving bank. null on
approved/pending entries and on all card flows. The full canonical list is
R01 through R85 per the NACHA Operating Rules.

nachaReturnReason.description:
Human-readable reason text paired with Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.NachaReturnCode (for example
"Insufficient Funds" for R01, "Account Closed" for R02). Surfaced verbatim in
the audit log and transaction explorer to spare consumers from maintaining
their own code-to-reason mapping. Null when Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.NachaReturnCode is null.

effectiveEntryDate.description:
The effective entry date the ACH entry will post to the receiving account, in the
originator's local processing window. After the daily NACHA cutoff this rolls
forward to the next banking day. Null on card flows.

originatingDfi.description:
ABA routing number of the Originating Depository Financial Institution that
transmitted the entry on behalf of the gateway/merchant. Null on card flows.

secCode.description:
Standard Entry Class code echoed from the request — for example
`PPD`, `CCD`, `WEB`, `TEL`, `ARC`. Mirrors
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.CheckData.SecCode as a string so the response shape matches
raw NACHA carrier fields rather than the gateway's enum representation.
Null on card flows.

micrEcho.description:
Verbatim echo of the inbound MICR line when the request carried check-image
data (POP, ARC, BOC). Null for non-image ACH flows (PPD, CCD, WEB, TEL) and
on all card flows.

tokenResult.description:
When the card on this transaction was vaulted (HPP / VT save-card-on-payment), the
             merchant-facing token the gateway generated — so it can be retrieved from the
             transaction response / HPP callback / webhook and charged later. null when the
             card was not tokenized. Server-produced; never accepted on a create request. The
             internal vault id is on Transaction.PaymentTokenId and is not emitted here.
            .

processorTokenId.description:
Reusable processor token captured from the processor at authorization time
(TSYS wire path first). Populated only on a successful tokenizing auth: an auth the
gateway gated on (SaveCardRequested AND the routed processor advertises tokenization AND
the merchant preference), otherwise null.


PCI: this identifier is PAN-correlating. It is encrypted at rest (EF Core
`HasEncrypted` on `ResponseData.ProcessorTokenId`, applied by the authorization
contributor before the raw `/ResponseData` patch reaches Cosmos), is stripped from
the merchant-facing `TransactionDto` mapping, and is denylisted from outbound webhook
projection. Never log its value, and never place it in exceptions, events, or API error
bodies.

processorTokenStatus.description:
The processor's status for the token minted on this auth (e.g. active /
provisioned). Non-sensitive processor metadata; null on non-tokenizing auths.

tokenRequestorId.description:
The network Token Requestor ID the token was minted under, echoed back by the
processor. Non-sensitive scheme/config identifier; null when not applicable.

processorTokenProfileId.description:
The processor profile id the token was minted under, so a later stored-credential
charge can be routed through the same processor profile. null on
non-tokenizing auths.

isPartialApproval.description: Whether the issuer approved less than the amount the gateway requested. Set by the authorization contributor when it observes the approved amount coming back below the requested amount — not by testing Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.ResultCode alone: the TSYS handler maps a host code-10 partial approval to Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.ResultCode.Ok with a reduced approved amount, so a `ResultCode.Partial` check would miss the common case.

TransactionResponseData.description: Represents the response data for a transaction, containing various details about the transaction outcome.

estimatedSettleDate.description: The estimated settlement date for the transaction.

dateSettled.description: The actual date when the transaction was settled.

flag.description:
Legacy settlement flag. Retained for Cosmos backward compatibility only.
            Use  for all new code.

processorBatchId.description: The processor's batch identifier for this transaction.

gatewayBatchId.description: The gateway's batch identifier for this transaction.

settlementDataJson.description:
Settlement aggregate data as JSON string (converted from processor XML).
This contains the data needed to settle the transaction with the processor.
Encrypted at rest via EF Core value converter — the Phoenix.EntityFrameworkCore.Encryption.EncryptedPropertyAttribute
enables the base repository to detect that this entity requires an encryption scope.

settlementStatus.description:
Current settlement status of the transaction for processor settlement tracking.
            Nullable to handle existing Cosmos documents that predate this property.
            Treat null as .

settlementAttemptedAt.description: Timestamp when settlement was last attempted with the processor.

settledAt.description: Timestamp when settlement succeeded with the processor.

settlementRetryCount.description:
Number of settlement retry attempts.
Nullable to handle existing Cosmos documents that predate this property.
Treat null as 0.

batchId.description:
Gateway batch identifier assigned at authorization time for batch boundary management.
Transactions are grouped into settlement batches by this ID, which is stamped from
the merchant's `CurrentBatchId` during the authorization flow.
Nullable because existing documents predate this property.

closedSettlementBatchId.description:
Identifier of the closed `SettlementBatch` (its aggregate-root `Id`) that settled this
transaction, stamped by `SettlementManager.CommitSettlementAsync` at batch close. This is a
scalar, index-friendly link from a transaction to its closed batch: it lets the Transaction Explorer
scope to a batch with a single equality predicate (`SettleData.ClosedSettlementBatchId == batchId`)
instead of expanding the batch's `Items` list into an `Id == a OR Id == b OR …` tree.


Distinct from the other batch identifiers on this type: Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.BatchId / Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.GatewayBatchId
are the open batch at authorization time, and Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.ProcessorBatchId is the processor's batch
reference; none of them equals `SettlementBatch.Id`.

Nullable because existing documents predate this property, and a transaction is only stamped once its
batch closes. Transactions in batches closed before this field existed have no value and are scoped via
the legacy `Items` fallback instead.

overrideHistory.description:
Append-only list of admin-driven manual overrides applied to Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSettleData.SettlementStatus.
Populated by the `Transaction.OverrideSettlementStatus` domain method.
Null on transactions that have never had a manual override (the default for the vast
majority of rows). Omitted from JSON when null so existing Cosmos documents do not
gain an empty array on the next write.

TransactionSource.description: Represents the source of a transaction in the payment processing system.
x-enumDescriptions: The source of the transaction is unknown or not specified.
The transaction originated from a virtual terminal interface.
The transaction was initiated through an API call.
The transaction was processed via a hosted payment page.
The transaction is part of a recurring billing cycle.
The transaction was processed as part of an offline batch.
The transaction is an automatic charge against an invoice (e.g. a recurring-invoice auto-charge or a smart-retry attempt) submitted by the Invoicing module.

source.description: The primary source of the transaction (virtual terminal, API, etc.).

hostedPaymentPageId.description:
When Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.Source is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.HostedPaymentPage,
this is the ID of the hosted payment page where the transaction was run.

contractId.description:
When Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.Source is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.RecurringBilling,
this is the ID of the recurring billing contract.

offlineBatchId.description:
When Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.Source is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.OfflineBatch,
this is the ID of the batch which submitted the transaction.

invoiceId.description:
When Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.Source is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.Invoicing,
this is the ID of the invoice the automatic charge (or smart-retry attempt)
is settling. Stamped server-side by the Invoicing module's auto-charge executor;
the join key used to reconcile the resulting transaction back onto the invoice.

apiKeyId.description:
When Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.Source is Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.Api,
this is the ID of the api key used to submit the transaction.

apiKeyName.description: The name associated with the API key used as the source of the transaction.

usedHppSession.description:
Indicates the transaction was initiated via an HPP pre-filled session.
Set to `true` when a session was resolved and consumed during form submission.

usedManualStoredPaymentMethodAdd.description:
Indicates the transaction is the internal account verification run when a payment method
is manually added as a stored payment method from the Customers back office. Set to
`true` only by the server-trusted manual-add verification seam
(`IInternalTransactionEntryService.CreateManualStoredAchVerificationAsync`), never
from client input.


Load-bearing for the ACH manual-add flow (WPG20-4221): the Transaction Manager routing
strategy diverts an ACH account-verification carrying this marker (with
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSource.VirtualTerminal) to the internal ACH verification
contributor, the same way Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.UsedHppSession gates the HPP save-only ACH flow.
It is the manual-admin analogue of the HPP-session marker: a second origin signal so the
divert is not reachable from a bare `Source == VirtualTerminal` value alone.


Genuinely server-stamped (stronger than Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.UsedHppSession, which stays
defence-in-depth): `TransactionCrudAppService.CreateInternalAsync` scrubs any
client-supplied value to `null` on every create path and re-stamps `true` only
for the trusted manual-add seam, so a forged value on the public create path never reaches
the routing divert. Mirrors the server-only-marker treatment of Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.HppSessionId
and `InvoiceId`.

hppSessionId.description:
The ID of the Hosted Payment Page session that produced this transaction.
Populated only when the transaction was created through the HPP session flow;
`null` for every other source (Virtual Terminal, API, recurring billing,
offline batch, and HPP submits that did not resolve a session).


This is a stable, server-supplied join key: integrators that drive transactions
through the HPP session API can read it back from the transaction to correlate
the originating session without subscribing to completion events. Distinct from
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.HostedPaymentPageId, which identifies the reusable page template
rather than the single-use session.


Read-only from a client's perspective: the value is stamped server-side only on
the verified HPP-session create path. Any value supplied on an inbound create
request is ignored and overwritten with `null`, so it cannot be used to
fabricate a session-to-transaction correlation.

campaignId.description:
The campaign the payment link that produced this transaction belonged to, when it belonged
to one. `null` for every transaction created outside a campaign, which is every
transaction created before campaigns existed and every one whose link named no campaign.


Stamped server-side on the verified HPP-session create path from the session document,
exactly like Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.HppSessionId, and scrubbed to `null` on every other create
entrypoint. A campaign report is a claim about which links earned which money, so a value a
caller could supply would let one merchant's traffic be attributed to a campaign it never
ran.

campaignSource.description:
The per-channel source tag carried by the payment link that produced this transaction
(`email`, `sms`, `qr`, `social`), when the link carried one. Bounded and
normalized by Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.CampaignSourceRules; `null` when the link named no source.


Meaningful only alongside Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.CampaignId: it is the breakdown inside one
campaign, not a standalone classification. Server-stamped and client-scrubbed on the same
terms as Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionSourceData.CampaignId.

clientIpAddress.description:
The IP address of the client that initiated the transaction.
Null for system-initiated transactions (recurring billing, offline batch).

clientIpGeo.description:
Point-in-time geolocation / ISP / ASN snapshot resolved at the
                enrichment stage from .
                
                Snapshot — does NOT update if the underlying IP intelligence
                database changes. Once written by the enrichment pipeline this
                value is immutable; subsequent transaction operations (capture,
                refund, reversal, repeat, recurring-billing materializations) must
                not overwrite it.
                
                Null when no client IP was available (system-initiated
                transactions, or when the IP geo provider could not resolve the
                address — loopback / private / unrouted ranges).

createdByUserId.description:
The ABP user ID of the user who created the transaction.
Null for anonymous or system-initiated transactions.

metadata.description: Optional extra metadata for future sources or provider-specific data.

TransactionSourceData.description: Encapsulates the origin of a transaction and any source-specific identifiers.

TransactionStage.description: Represents the stage of a transaction within the transaction management workflow.
x-enumDescriptions: A partial approval is holding a reduced authorization and the gateway is waiting for the operator or cardholder to decide its fate: accept the lesser amount, void it, or start a continuation tender for the shortfall. Non-terminal — the transaction leaves this stage once Transaction.PartialApprovalData.Disposition moves off PartialApprovalDisposition.Pending, or when the acknowledgment deadline elapses and the gateway voids on the operator's behalf.
Auth succeeded at the processor but a post-authorization denylist rule matched (AVS or CVV response code). A reversal or void was issued and the transaction is permanently rejected by gateway policy.

the order is stable across identical requests. Empty when nothing in the window is visible
to the caller.

publicReference.description:
Stable, URL-safe opaque external reference for the token. This is the identifier
surfaced in the transaction-completed event and the HPP postMessage envelope for
integrators to correlate the saved credential — never the internal vault Guid
(PAN-correlated).

TransactionTokenResult.description:
The merchant-facing token identifiers the gateway generated when the card on a
transaction was vaulted (HPP / Virtual Terminal "save card on payment"). Surfaced on
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TransactionResponseData.TokenResult so ISVs / resellers / merchants can
retrieve the reusable token from the transaction response (and the HPP callback /
webhook) and charge it later.

TransactionType.description: Represents the various types of transactions that can be performed in the system.
x-enumDescriptions: Represents an authorization transaction, typically used to verify funds availability without capturing the amount.
Represents a sale transaction, which authorizes and captures funds in a single step.
Represents a return transaction, used to refund money to the customer.
Represents a void transaction, used to cancel a previously authorized transaction before it is settled.
Represents a force transaction, typically used to manually enter a previously authorized transaction.
Represents a capture transaction, used to capture funds from a previously authorized transaction.
Represents a capture all transaction, used to capture funds from multiple previously authorized transactions.
Represents a repeat sale transaction, used to process a new sale based on a previous transaction's details.
Represents an adjustment transaction, used to modify the amount of a previous transaction.
Represents an activate transaction, typically used to activate a gift card or prepaid card.
Represents a deactivate transaction, typically used to deactivate a gift card or prepaid card.
Represents a redeem transaction, typically used to redeem value from a gift card or loyalty program.
Represents an inquire transaction, used to check the status or balance of an account or card.
Represents a reload transaction, typically used to add value to a gift card or prepaid card.

Represents an offline EBT voucher clear: a terminal was offline, a paper food-stamp (SNAP) or eWIC voucher was written against a voice-obtained approval code, and the voucher is later uploaded so the benefit clears. Permitted on EBT SNAP and eWIC tenders only.

processorKey.description:
Optional processor key scoping the close to a single processor's open batch. When set, the
run fans out only to the matching (merchant, processor) group, leaving every other
processor's batch untouched; when null, the historical all-processor behaviour is preserved.
Matched case-insensitively against the merchant's active processor keys.

base.description: The base amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative and is required.

tip.description: The tip amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

tax.description: The tax amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

shipping.description: The shipping amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

convenience.description: The convenience fee amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

conveniencePercentage.description: The convenience fee percentage of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

surcharge.description:
The surcharge amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative. Applies only when the
surcharging feature is enabled for the merchant: on an initial transaction submit, a non-zero
value is rejected at the create boundary when surcharging is disabled.

surchargeAssessed.description:
Server-owned marker indicating the gateway itself computed Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.Surcharge for this
transaction. Only the trusted surcharge-enrichment path may set this; every other create/update
path must leave it null, including when a caller supplies a raw Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.Surcharge value.

convenienceChargedSeparately.description:
Server-owned marker indicating the convenience fee is billed as a separate, linked charge
transaction rather than folded into this transaction's Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.Total. Only the trusted
transaction pipeline may set this; every create/update path must leave it null, including
when a caller supplies a raw Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.Convenience value.

cashback.description: The cashback amount of the transaction. This value cannot be negative.

total.description:
The total amount of the transaction. This property is calculated based on the sum of Base, Tip, Tax, Shipping, Convenience,
and (when Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.SurchargeAssessed is true) Surcharge amounts. When
Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TrxAmounts.ConvenienceChargedSeparately is true the Convenience amount is excluded, because
the fee bills as its own linked charge transaction.
The value must be positive and is required.

id.description: Identifier of the custom-field entry.

name.description:
Name of the merchant's custom-field definition this value belongs to. Required, at most
50 characters, and free of control characters. On the authenticated API the name must match
an enabled custom-field definition configured for the transaction's merchant.

TrxCustomField.description:
A single merchant-defined custom field carried on a transaction: the name of the merchant's
field definition and the value captured for this transaction.

forceCardNotPresent.description:
Force the network request to card-not-present routing even when the request data
implies a card-present capture. Replaces the legacy `MOTO` sentinel and the
`SETSPECIALFIELDSFORCNP` sentinel applied to a CP-entry-mode card. Drives TSYS
`AccountDataSource=@`.

forceLevel3WithSwipeEntry.description:
Emit Level 3 fields even when the captured entry mode is a magnetic-stripe swipe.
Replaces the legacy `ISLEVEL3TRANSACTIONSWIPE` sentinel; production Level 3
is normally limited to manual / e-commerce / MOTO entry modes.

setSpecialFieldsForCnp.description:
Apply the 2025 cert-suite "special fields for CNP" indicator set on a card-present
transaction. Replaces the legacy `SETSPECIALFIELDSFORCNP` sentinel. Distinct
from Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.TsysCertificationOverrides.ForceCardNotPresent: this only flips the special-fields indicator
without rewriting the entry-mode-derived `AccountDataSource`.

merchantInitiatedReferenceOverride.description:
Hard-coded scheme transaction id supplied to a Visa MIT cert request when the
captured `SchemeTransactionId` is unavailable (e.g. fresh cert merchant with
no prior CIT in the same scheme). Replaces the legacy `VALUE(host)` parenthesis
pattern that used to be smuggled inside `CustomerId`.

forceStoringCardCertFlag.description:
Emit the legacy "this transaction is storing a card" cert flag in the TSYS request,
independent of whether the request actually tokenises a card. Replaces the
`ISSTORINGCARD` sentinel.

forceManualEntryMode.description:
Force `EntryMode` to `Manual` for the request even when the captured
entry mode is something else. Replaces the legacy `MANUAL` sentinel and is
applied by `CardPhDataBuilder` before the handler runs.

TSYS-specific certification override knobs. Drive the TSYS SDK `Config(...)` call
sequence at auth time when the cert harness needs to exercise a path the production-shape
request fields cannot otherwise reach.

from their statement analysis. A surcharge may never exceed this, so a configured rate above it
(or above the 3% network cap) is rejected at save. Supplying a value records the attestation with
the acting user and a timestamp; null leaves it unattested and withdraws any prior attestation.
Conditional: When AttestedCostOfAcceptanceRate and HasValue meet conditions. Range: 0–1.

provisions are what make the signoff necessary.

leaves every surface on its platform default copy.

visaServiceFeeRegistered.description: Merchant self-declared record that its account is registered with the acquirer for the Visa Service Fee program. Distinct from Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.GovEducationAttested: that attestation is the merchant's claim to qualify as a Government or Education entity (and gates percentage mode plus the debit/prepaid exemptions), whereas this records the Visa-specific registration the program requires on top of qualifying. A Gov/Ed-attested merchant without this registration is not blocked; the mismatch surfaces as a non-blocking save warning and an inline warning in the convenience-fee editor, because the registration happens outside the platform and the operator may be recording it after the fact. At transaction time this is what lets a percentage fee apply on Visa: the percentage network guard (Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.ConvenienceFeeNetworkGuard) otherwise applies a brand-uniform flat fallback or suppression whenever the merchant's accepted-brand set includes Visa. That consumption is behind the `ConvenienceFee:HonorVisaServiceFeeRegistration` rollout gate, so setting this alone does not change what a cardholder is charged until the gate is enabled.

visaServiceFeeRegisteredOn.description: The date the acquirer registered this merchant for the Visa Service Fee program, as supplied by the operator. Required once Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.VisaServiceFeeRegistered is set (enforced by Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.ConvenienceFeeSaveGate). This is a calendar date, not an instant: it is the acquirer's registration date, so it must never be timezone-converted for display. The audit timestamp for when the flag itself was recorded is Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.VisaServiceFeeRegistrationRecordedOn, which is a UTC instant.

attestedCostOfAcceptanceRate.description:
Merchant self-declared cost of acceptance, as a decimal fraction of the transaction base
(e.g. `0.025m` = 2.5%). Some jurisdictions (e.g. Georgia, New York) require a convenience
fee to be capped at the merchant's actual cost of acceptance; this rate is the cap basis. At
transaction time the ceiling is `AttestedCostOfAcceptanceRate x base amount`, and the
resolved fee is reduced to it when it exceeds it and the governing state requires the cap
(#3211). Mirrors the surcharge side's
`MerchantSurchargeConfiguration.AttestedCostOfAcceptanceRate` (#1585). Null (or a
non-positive value) means the merchant has not attested a cost of acceptance, so no numeric cap
is applied. Consumed only when the state-override rollout gate
(`ConvenienceFee:EnforceStateOverrides`) is enabled.

on the same terms as Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.GovEducationAttestedBy (`readOnly` on the published
schema).

exemptDebit.description: Stored merchant preference to exempt debit-funded transactions from the convenience fee. Configuration only — not enforced at payment time yet. No per-transaction evaluator consumes this flag today; it is persisted and gated here so the runtime suppression can be wired later (the separate convenience-fee evaluator story) with no schema change. Until that lands, setting this does not change what a cardholder is charged. When the evaluator ships it will suppress the fee on debit-funded transactions per the card-brand rules. Permitted only under the card-brand Government / Higher-Education service-fee program, so it is gated behind Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.GovEducationAttested (enforced by the validator and disabled in the editor until the attestation is set). Independent of Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.ExemptPrepaid so a merchant can exempt debit only, prepaid only, or both. Nullable for Cosmos baseline compatibility: documents written before this field deserialize to `null`, which every consumer treats as "not exempt".

exemptPrepaid.description: Stored merchant preference to exempt prepaid-funded transactions from the convenience fee. Configuration only — not enforced at payment time yet, same status as Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.ExemptDebit: the consuming per-transaction evaluator is not wired yet, so setting this does not currently change what is charged. Gated behind Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.GovEducationAttested exactly like Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.ExemptDebit, and independent of it. Nullable for Cosmos baseline compatibility (legacy documents deserialize to `null`, treated as "not exempt").

The merchant must explicitly choose a fixed amount or attest to gov/education registration.
Surfaced as a review banner in the settings UI; never causes a silent percentage migration.

offlineChannelExceptionGranted.description: Operator-granted exception to the two card-not-present platform proxies, recording that this merchant genuinely operates a standard payment channel WinkPG cannot observe (typically payment by cheque or by post). Read through M:Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.HasOfflineChannelException. This does not replace the channel declaration: the merchant still declares Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.StandardChannel / Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.AlternativeChannel normally (e.g. Check plus Online) and Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.VirtualTerminalConvenienceFeeField.AlternativeChannelAttested still applies. The grant asserts that the declared offline standard channel really exists despite the platform having no evidence of it.

allowPartialApprovals.description:
Merchant-level master switch for partial approvals. When false, no processor profile can
enable partial approvals for this merchant; when true, each profile still decides per card
type through its own partial-auth field. A merchant document written before this setting
existed carries no value, which reads as the default (available).
Conditional: When AllowPartialApprovals is true.

allowSplitTender.description:

Null reads as the default (permitted).

allowTipAdjustmentOnPartialApproval.description:
Whether a tip may be adjusted on a transaction the issuer already reduced. Opt-in; null
reads as the default (not permitted).
Conditional: When AllowPartialApprovals is true.

splitTenderMaxTenders.description:
Maximum number of tenders a single sale may be split across. Null reads as the default
(Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.PartialApprovalConsts.DefaultSplitTenderMaxTenders).
Conditional: When AllowPartialApprovals is true.

partialApprovalAckTimeoutMinutes.description:
How long the platform waits for an operator to accept or void a partial approval before the
acknowledgment window closes. Only meaningful under
Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.PartialApprovalStrategy.RequireOperatorAcknowledgment. Null
reads as the default (Phoenix.SharedModels.Merchant.VirtualTerminal.PartialApprovalConsts.DefaultPartialApprovalAckTimeoutMinutes).
Conditional: When PartialApprovalAckTimeoutMinutes is true.

WalletCheckoutSnapshot.description:
Storefront-safe projection of a Phoenix.SharedModels.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.WalletProviderRegistration row,
keyed by `(providerType, merchantId)`. Returned by the anonymous checkout
snapshot endpoint so the FE can decide whether to render the wallet button and

not leak operational state.

WalletMerchantOnboardingInput.description:
Optional richer onboarding details carried on a create/update DTO for wallet providers
whose registration shape exceeds Apple's (Paze: structured address, merchant category
code, self-assigned profile id).
            


The merchant name is not here: every provider takes it from the shared
`WalletProviderRegistrationCreateOrUpdateDtoBase.MerchantDisplayName`. One name per
registration is deliberate, so Paze has no separate legal/trade name input.


Provider-neutral by name. Null for Apple Pay (which maps only the flat
identifier/displayName/url/domains fields), so it is inert for the existing path. The
CRUD app service maps it onto the Domain-layer `WalletMerchantOnboardingDetails`
threaded to the orchestrator + provider.

`IWalletPaymentSessionProvider` — i.e., requires a server-issued
payment session. Apple Pay: true; Google Pay: false.

supportsDomainAssociation.description:

`IWalletDomainAssociationProvider` — i.e., expects the merchant domain
(or PSP-hosted domain) to serve a provider-issued verification file at a
well-known path. Apple Pay: true; Google Pay / Paze: false.

Capability snapshot for a single wallet provider — what the frontend needs to
know to drive a dynamic wallet selector. The frontend should disable controls
for capabilities the chosen provider doesn't support rather than letting the
user submit a request that will return "not supported".

WalletRegistrationLevel.description:
Scope of a Phoenix.SharedModels.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.WalletProviderRegistration aggregate.
<list type="bullet"><item>Phoenix.SharedModels.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.WalletRegistrationLevel.Platform — the PSP-level (platform integrator's own)
    wallet merchant, stored with `MerchantId = null`. Used by the
    gateway's own hosted checkout pages (e.g. `checkout.winkpg.com`).
    Multiple platform rows per provider type are allowed, distinguished
    by `ProviderMerchantIdentifier`.</item><item>Phoenix.SharedModels.PaymentTokenization.WalletProviderRegistrations.WalletRegistrationLevel.Merchant — a sub-merchant's own wallet binding,
    stored with `MerchantId` set. One row per
    `(MerchantId, ProviderType)`. Used when the merchant wants the
    wallet button on their own domain.</item></list>

The wallet provider's wire API call is identical for both levels — Apple
Pay's `registerMerchant` doesn't know about "platform vs merchant",
it just registers an integrator. The distinction is internal: it picks
which Cosmos row carries the registration state. The provider layer
(`ITokenizationProvider`) never sees this enum.

eventType.description: The canonical event type string this schema describes.

hasRichPayload.description:
True when the event delivers a structured `data` object (an aggregate-backed event such
as a transaction completion). False for events that deliver only the flat `attributes`
map — for those, WinkPG.Notifications.WebhookPayloadSchemaDto.DataFields is empty and the sample shows the flat shape.

dataFields.description:
The schema of the `data` object's fields, generated from the payload CLR type via the
same exclusion logic the runtime projector uses. Empty when WinkPG.Notifications.WebhookPayloadSchemaDto.HasRichPayload is false.

sampleEnvelopeJson.description:
A pretty-printed, illustrative sample of the full webhook envelope (id, type, version,
createdUtc, scope ids, correlationId, data) with placeholder values. For display only —
the values are synthetic, the shape is real.

WebhookPayloadSchemaDto.description:
Self-service description of the webhook payload a subscriber receives for one event type:
the schema of the rich `data` body plus a realistic, illustrative sample of the full
delivered envelope. Returned by `INotificationEventTypeAppService.GetPayloadSchemaAsync`
and rendered in the notification event catalog so customers can see the payload shape without
firing a real event at a test endpoint.

name.description: The JSON field name (the CLR property name, emitted verbatim by the projector).

type.description:
The JSON type the value serializes as. One of the values in
WinkPG.Notifications.WebhookPayloadSchemaTypes: `string`, `integer`, `number`,
`boolean`, `datetime`, `object`, or `array`.

nullable.description:
Whether the field can be `null` / absent. Reference types and System.Nullable`1
value types are nullable; non-nullable value types are not. This is a best-effort hint derived
from the CLR type, not a guarantee that the field is always populated.

fields.description: For WinkPG.Notifications.WebhookPayloadSchemaField.Type == `object`: the nested fields of the object. Null for scalar fields.

items.description:
For  == array: a descriptor for the array's element. The element
            descriptor's  is empty. Null for non-array fields.

truncated.description:
True when the describe walk stopped at this node because the recursion-depth ceiling or a
type cycle was hit. The actual delivered payload carries a `__truncated` marker in the
same place. Defensive guard — not expected on today's tree-shaped aggregates.

WebhookPayloadSchemaField.description: One node in a webhook payload schema tree. Describes a single field that a subscriber will see in the rich `data` body of an outbound webhook for a given event type. The tree is produced by `IWebhookEntityProjector.DescribeAsync(Type)`, which walks the payload CLR type through the same exclusion layers the runtime projector applies when it builds the actual delivered payload. A property that the projector strips (PCI-sensitive, encrypted, or framework/system) is therefore absent from this schema as well — the schema and the delivered payload cannot drift because they share one traversal.

isRotating.description: Whether an overlap is open, so deliveries carry two signature values.

rotationStartedUtc.description: When the overlap began, UTC. Null when no rotation is in progress.

WebhookSecretRotationStateDto.description: Whether a webhook destination is currently signing with two secrets, and since when.

This is the benefit kind, not the precise food taxonomy — the fine-grained USDA coding lives in Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.Level3LineItem.WicFoodCategoryCode and Phoenix.SharedModels.Transaction.Level3LineItem.WicSubcategoryCode.

Standard fixed-quantity food benefit, redeemed by USDA food category/subcategory against the cardholder's remaining prescribed balance for that category.
Cash Value Benefit (CVB) / Cash Value Voucher (CVV) — a dollar-denominated benefit for fruits and vegetables, redeemed against a remaining dollar balance rather than a fixed quantity.

TooManyRequests.description: The request was refused because a rate limit was exceeded. Wait at least the interval `Retry-After` names before retrying, then back off. Limits are tuned per deployment, so read the allowance from the response headers rather than assuming a fixed ceiling.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying, in whole seconds. Always at least one, and always the same figure as `retryAfterSeconds` in the body.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The ceiling the limiter that bound this request measures against. Sent on rate limited responses and on the successful ones the same limiters govern. Absent when no allowance was measured, which a client should read as no reported allowance rather than as zero.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: How much of that ceiling is left, never below zero. Sent and omitted together with `X-RateLimit-Limit`.
